# Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Regulations 1997

Statutory Rules No. 328, 1997

made under the

Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Act 1997

**Compilation No. 274**

**Compilation date:** 26 August 2026

**Includes amendments:** F2026L01097, F2026L01098, F2026L01099, F2026L01100, F2026L01102, F2026L01103 and F2026L01104

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Regulations 1997* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 26 August 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

Contents

### Part 1—Preliminary

###### 1 Name of regulations

These regulations are the *Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Regulations 1997*.

###### 3 Definitions

In these regulations:

***Act*** means the *Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Act 1997*.

### Part 2—Supplementary powers to make commitments to spend money and be involved in companies etc.

###### 16 Arrangements and programs (Act s 32B)

(1) For the purposes of subsection 32B(2) of the Act:

(a) Part 1 of Schedule 1AA specifies:

(i) arrangements under which relevant money or other CRF money is, or may become, payable by the Commonwealth; and

(ii) classes of arrangements; and

(b) Part 2 of Schedule 1AA specifies:

(i) grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; and

(ii) classes of grants; and

(c) Part 3 of Schedule 1AA specifies:

(i) grants of financial assistance to persons other than a State or Territory; and

(ii) classes of grants; and

(d) Part 4 of Schedule 1AA specifies programs.

Note: ***Arrangement*** is defined in subsection 32B(4) of the Act.

(2) The specification of an arrangement, grant or program in Schedule 1AA is not affected by:

(a) a change in the name of the Department or authority specified as administering the arrangement, grant or program; or

(b) the transfer to another Department or authority of responsibility, in whole or in part, for the administration of the arrangement, grant or program.

(3) For the purposes of subsection 32B(2) of the Act:

(a) Part 1 of Schedule 1AB specifies:

(i) arrangements under which relevant money or other CRF money is, or may become, payable by the Commonwealth; and

(ii) classes of arrangements; and

(b) Part 2 of Schedule 1AB specifies:

(i) grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; and

(ii) classes of grants; and

(c) Part 3 of Schedule 1AB specifies:

(i) grants of financial assistance to persons other than a State or Territory; and

(ii) classes of grants; and

(d) Part 4 of Schedule 1AB specifies programs.

Note: ***Arrangement*** is defined in subsection 32B(4) of the Act.

###### 22AB Supplementary powers to form companies etc. (Act s 39B)

(1) For the purposes of paragraphs 39B(1)(a) and (2)(a) of the Act, each item of Schedule 1B specifies a company.

(2) For the purposes of paragraphs 39B(1)(b) and (2)(b) of the Act, each item of Schedule 1B specifies objects or proposed activities of the company specified in the item.

### Part 3—Transitional and application provisions

#### Division 1—Amendments made by the Financial Management and Accountability Amendment (Public Governance) Regulation 2014

###### 23 Definitions

In this Division:

***amending regulation*** means the *Financial Management and Accountability Amendment (Public Governance) Regulation 2014*.

***commencement time*** means the time when the *Financial Management and Accountability Amendment (Public Governance) Regulation 2014* commences.

###### 24 Commonwealth procurement and Guidelines

Despite the repeal of regulations 7, 7A, 7B and 16A (which deal with Commonwealth procurement, and guidelines for Commonwealth grants, cleaning services and fraud) of these Regulations by the amending regulation, regulations 7, 7A, 7B and 16A, and any guidelines that are in force for the purposes of those regulations immediately before the commencement time, continue to apply after that time in relation to any process that is begun before that time.

###### 25 Disposal of property found on Commonwealth premises

Despite the repeal of regulation 23 (which deals with the disposal of property found on Commonwealth premises) of these Regulations by the amending regulation, regulation 23 continues to apply after the commencement time in relation to property found, or disposals that occur, before that time.

###### 26 Transferring leave entitlements

Despite the repeal of Part 11 (which deals with transferring leave entitlements when employees move between Agencies etc.) of these Regulations by the amending regulation, that Part continues to apply after the commencement time in relation to moves that occur before the commencement time.

#### Division 2—Amendments made by the Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Amendment (2018 Measures No. 1) Regulations 2018

###### 27 Power to vary or administer grants or arrangements

Despite the repeal of table items in Schedules 1AA and 1AB by Schedule 1 to the *Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Amendment (2018 Measures No. 1) Regulations 2018*, those items continue in force for the purposes of sections 32B and 32C of the Act in relation to the administration or variation of grants or arrangements made before the repeal, but not so as to authorise any new commitment by the Commonwealth to spend money.

<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To achieve the switchover to digital‑only television through: assisting commercial television broadcasters to provide additional services to viewers in regional and remote licence areas; assisting eligible households to convert to digital via the Viewer Access Satellite Service; and providing practical and technical assistance to those who are most likely to have significant difficulties in switching to digital television</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>405.014</td>
<td colspan="2">Digital Productivity—NBN Demonstrators—includes projects with major national research organisations and major performing arts organisation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To develop new digital economy business models for major performing arts organisations, and online education centres by establishing internet portals to provide 3D learning experiences for students</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>Department of Climate Change and Energy Efficiency</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>406.004</td>
<td colspan="2">Energy Efficiency Programs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide minimum energy performance standards and the labelling of residential and commercial buildings and the implementation of measures agreed by the Council of Australian Governments in relation to the National Strategy on Energy Efficiency</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>406.008</td>
<td colspan="2">GEMS National Legislative Framework</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To implement minimum energy performance standards and labelling of appliances, equipment and products that significantly affect energy use</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>406.018</td>
<td colspan="2">International climate change</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To influence the development of international policies and measures in relation to climate change through the pursuit of broad based international climate action and agreement</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>Department of Education, Employment and Workplace Relations</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.001</td>
<td colspan="2">Support for the Child Care System</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support child care services so that more families can access quality early childhood education and childcare services. This program helps families to participate in the social and economic life of the community</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.002</td>
<td colspan="2">Child Care Services Support</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist Child Care Services to provide support, promote and improve access to quality child care and early learning for children, families and communities; promote and maintain high quality care and inclusion for all children; and to support the development, maintenance and dissemination of information to assist families to make informed decisions about child care</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.003</td>
<td colspan="2">Jobs Education and Training Child Care Fee Assistance (JETCCFA)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide eligible parents with extra financial assistance to help with the cost of approved child care while undertaking activities such as job search, work, study, training or rehabilitation to help them to enter or re‑enter the workforce</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.004</td>
<td colspan="2">Early Childhood Education</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To improve access to early childhood education and child care, to support optimal child development in the early years and prepare children for formal schooling</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.014</td>
<td colspan="2">Helping Children with Autism</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide support for children with autism spectrum disorder, their parents, carers, teachers and other professionals</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.043</td>
<td colspan="2">Employment Services</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To invest in the skills that unemployed Australians need for the future to help them find and retain employment, and to ensure that government assistance supports workforce participation and economic and social inclusion</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.047</td>
<td colspan="2">Pacific Seasonal Workers Program</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To establish a seasonal labour mobility program that will provide workers from Pacific Island countries and East Timor with the opportunity to work in selected Australian industries experiencing unmet demand for labour</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.048</td>
<td colspan="2">Productivity Education and Training Fund</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support projects which drive a focus on leadership and productivity improvement through enterprise bargaining under the Fair Work framework</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.049</td>
<td colspan="2">Regional Education, Skills and Jobs Plans</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To improve participation and outcomes in education, training and employment in regional Australia</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.053</td>
<td colspan="2">Disability Employment Services</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To help individuals with injury, disability or a health condition to secure and maintain sustainable employment through disability employment services and employment assistance</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.054</td>
<td colspan="2">Employment Assistance and Other Services</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support those eligible job seekers with permanent disability who are assessed as needing regular long‑term ongoing support in the workplace</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.055</td>
<td colspan="2">Remote Jobs and Communities Program</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To build jobs and create sustainable communities in Remote Australia</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.058</td>
<td colspan="2">Working Age Payments</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support people to improve their prospects of gaining employment, to acquire labour market skills and knowledge and to participate in society</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.059</td>
<td colspan="2">Compensation and Debt Relief</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide access for eligible recipients to discretionary payments in special circumstances or financial relief from amounts owing to the Commonwealth</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.060</td>
<td colspan="2">Employee Assistance</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide safety‑net support for employees in certain circumstances or, alternatively, supporting long‑standing industry arrangements which deliver employee benefits</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.061</td>
<td colspan="2">General Employee Entitlements and Redundancy Scheme</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: A safety‑net payment scheme established to assist employees who have lost their employment due to the liquidation or bankruptcy of their employer and who are owed certain employee entitlements</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.062</td>
<td colspan="2">Workplace Assistance</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To ensure the successful operation of the workplace relations system, in particular through initiatives designed to demonstrate the benefit of cooperative workplace relations and/or to assist employers and employees understand their rights and obligations under the system</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.063</td>
<td colspan="2">Protected Action Ballots Scheme</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To pay costs incurred by the Australian Electoral Commission in relation to protected action ballots</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.064</td>
<td colspan="2">Home Workers Code of Practice Program</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support the development and promotion of the Home Workers Code of Practice and the ‘Ethical Clothing Australia’ label</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.065</td>
<td colspan="2">International Labour Organisation Subscription</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To enable the Australian Government to participate fully in the development of international labour standards, progress ratification of standards at the national level, report to the ILO on Conventions and workplace relations reforms, and participate as a member of the ILO Governing Body</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.066</td>
<td colspan="2">Social and Community Workers Education and Information Program</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist Queensland social and community services sector employers to meet their obligations under the new Australian Government regulations for back pay to employees in the sector</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.067</td>
<td colspan="2">Workers’ Compensation Payments</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support an early and safe return to work, and access to compensation for injured workers covered by the Comcare scheme, through working in partnership with employers to create best practice in rehabilitation and quick and accurate management of workers’ compensation claims</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.068</td>
<td colspan="2">ABSTUDY</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide support to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students and Australian apprentices to improve access to and participation in secondary and tertiary education and training</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.069</td>
<td colspan="2">Assistance for Isolated Children Scheme</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide financial allowances to help families of primary, secondary, and certain tertiary students with the educational costs incurred due to being geographically isolated</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.071</td>
<td colspan="2">Centre for Workplace Leadership Fund</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To establish the Centre for Workplace Leadership to boost productivity and the quality of jobs by improving leadership and management practices in Australian workplaces</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.073</td>
<td colspan="2">Priority Employment Area Initiative</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support employment and prevent unemployment in priority areas of social and economic disadvantage, including through the provision of Local Employment Coordinators and Jobs and Skills Expos, and the funding of projects and activities to achieve this objective</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.074</td>
<td colspan="2">Parliament and Civics Education Rebate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide benefits to students in the form of a travel subsidy, paid to schools on a per student basis, for those students to undertake excursions to visit national institutions in Canberra</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407.077</td>
<td colspan="2">Labour Mobility and Relocation Assistance Initiative</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide benefits to unemployed persons in the form of financial assistance for such persons to relocate to take up employment or an apprenticeship</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>Safe Work Australia</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>408.001</td>
<td colspan="2">Reform of, and improvements to, Australian work health and safety and workers’ compensation arrangements</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: The objective of Safe Work Australia is to monitor and evaluate harmonised laws, coordinate and develop national policy and strategies, undertake research and collect, analyse and report data to improve work health and safety and workers’ compensation arrangements in Australia</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>Department of Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.002</td>
<td colspan="2">Housing Assistance and Homelessness Prevention</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide rental subsidies for low‑and moderate‑income households, and to fund homelessness prevention initiatives including research and stakeholder engagement to reduce the impact of homelessness</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.003</td>
<td colspan="2">Affordable Housing</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To improve the supply of affordable housing and reduce the cost of new homes available to low‑and moderate‑income households and to invest in local infrastructure projects that support new housing developments in regional cities</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.004</td>
<td colspan="2">Financial Management</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To improve the financial knowledge, skills, capabilities and financial resilience of vulnerable individuals and families and to alleviate the immediate impact of financial stress, and to progress initiatives in relation to problem gambling. Includes funding for research and stakeholder engagement and funding to peak bodies and other stakeholder organisations</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.005</td>
<td colspan="2">Community Investment</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To improve the responsiveness and integration of local community services to increase participation of vulnerable people in community life. Includes funding for research and stakeholder engagement and funding to national peak bodies and other stakeholder organisations</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.006</td>
<td colspan="2">Support for People in Special Circumstances</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To make payments to financially assist eligible people in severe financial hardship who do not have any other means of support, including payments to individuals and families affected by disasters and other crises. Includes making payments to Australians in circumstances beyond their control to support them in overcoming those circumstances and maintain their financial wellbeing</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.007</td>
<td colspan="2">Supplementary Payments and Support for Income Support Recipients</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To make payments and subsidise services to certain income support recipients and low‑income households to assist them financially and to help them continue to participate economically and socially</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.008</td>
<td colspan="2">Allowances, Concessions and Services for Seniors</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To make payments and provide services to senior Australians: to assist with household expenses; to enable them to maintain their standard of living; and to increase their access to information and community resources</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.010</td>
<td colspan="2">Income Support for Carers</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To make payments and allowances to financially assist eligible carers of people with disability or a severe medical condition or of people who are frail aged</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.011</td>
<td colspan="2">Services and Support for People with Disability</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide supported employment and improve access to information, advocacy respite, supported accommodation and services for people with disability, their families and carers so that they can develop their capabilities and actively participate in community and economic life and to develop and implement national policies in relation to disability, including employment and income support policy, the National Disability Agreement, National Disability Strategy, National Carer Strategy and the National Disability Insurance Scheme. Includes funding for research and stakeholder engagement and funding to peak bodies and other stakeholder organisations</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.013</td>
<td colspan="2">National Disability Insurance Scheme</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To improve the wellbeing and social and economic participation of people with disability and their carers by building a National Disability Insurance Scheme that delivers care and support through an insurance approach including any associated capital investment</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.014</td>
<td colspan="2">Early Intervention Services for Children with Disability</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide access to early intervention services and support for children with disability, their parents, carers and families to help eligible children achieve their potential, including education and support for parents, carers and families; to provide information and support to parents, carers and families to help them enable eligible children with disability to achieve their potential. Includes Autism Specific Early Learning and Care Centres that provide early learning programs and specific support to children with Autism Spectrum Disorder</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.015</td>
<td colspan="2">Gender Equality for Women</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To implement strategies in priority areas to achieve gender equality. The priority areas include reducing violence against women and supporting women affected by violence; support for trafficked people; improving economic outcomes for women; and ensuring women’s equal place in society. Includes funding for National Women’s Alliances to engage with women’s groups to ensure that women’s issues are represented in decision‑making and policy outcomes, and includes communication and information designed to change violence‑supportive attitudes and effectively reduce the incidence and impact of violence in Australia</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.022</td>
<td colspan="2">Australian Housing and Urban Research Institute</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To contribute to the research undertaken on housing and homelessness</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.023</td>
<td colspan="2">Longitudinal Studies</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: A program of longitudinal surveys including:</i><br><i>(a) Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia—a survey of the effects of policy and other changes on families and household formation including labour market and education participation and retirement preparation; and</i><br><i>(b) Longitudinal Study of Australian Children—a survey of children and their families to establish an evidence base for future family and child policy formulation; and</i><br><i>(c) Longitudinal Study of Indigenous Children—a survey that records the development of Indigenous children in selected sites over time and collects data on health, family roles and relationships, child care, education, service provision and community issues</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.025</td>
<td colspan="2">Memorial Services for Bali Bombings</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To make payments to assist people to attend memorial services in connection with the Bali bombings</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410.028</td>
<td colspan="2">Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse—community‑based support services</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support people who require assistance with participation in, or as a result of, the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, including:</i><br><i>(a) support before, during or after the Royal Commission; and</i><br><i>(b) support for victims of child sexual abuse (including by providing treatment and follow up for victims of sexual abuse, whether or not they participate in the Royal Commission); and</i><br><i>(c) support for families and others supporting victims; and</i><br><i>(d) support for staff of institutions or organisations in which sexual abuse took place; and</i><br><i>(e) therapeutic support (including by way of the provision of sickness and hospital benefits or medical services) and telephone counselling; and</i><br><i>(f) training and guidance to organisations involved in supporting those engaged with the Royal Commission</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>Department of Finance and Deregulation</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>411.002</td>
<td colspan="2">Electorate and Ministerial Support Costs and Parliamentary Entitlements Support Costs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide funds to support the provision of entitlements to the current Prime Minister, and to former Prime Ministers once they have left the Parliament, the Australian Political Exchange Council and related activities, and political party secretariat training</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>411.003</td>
<td colspan="2">Divestment of Commonwealth property—financial assistance</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide financial assistance to persons acquiring Commonwealth real property, including in relation to:</i><br><i>(a) the acquisition and maintenance of the property; and</i><br><i>(b) compliance with legal requirements associated with the property</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>412.001</td>
<td colspan="2">Foreign Affairs and Trade Operations</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objectives:</i><br><i>(a) to protect and advance the national interest through engaging in advocacy in Australia and overseas that promotes Australia’s foreign, trade, economic, and security interests; and</i><br><i>(b) to promote a whole‑of‑government approach in pursuit of Australia’s interests abroad, including through leadership at overseas missions and coordination of the overseas diplomatic network; and</i><br><i>(c) to ensure the security and protect the dignity of the diplomatic and consular corps serving in Australia by delivering a quality service and upholding Australia’s obligations under the Vienna conventions; and</i><br><i>(d) to deliver high‑quality public diplomacy, international media and cultural visit programs, which improve understanding of Australia and Australian Government foreign and trade policies</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>412.002</td>
<td colspan="2">Payments to International Organisations</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To advance Australia’s foreign, trade, economic, and security interests through membership and participation in international organisations and their various peacekeeping activities</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>412.003</td>
<td colspan="2">Public Information Services and Public Diplomacy</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objectives:</i><br><i>(a) to project a positive and contemporary image of Australia and promote a clear understanding of government policies and objectives through the Department’s public diplomacy, cultural and media activities cultural and media activities and through providing an independent, creditable and reliable voice and image in the region</i><br><i>(b) to promote people‑to‑people links and a contemporary and positive image of Australia and support for the Australian Government’s international policy goals, including through grants and other support to bilateral foundations, councils and institutes</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>412.004</td>
<td colspan="2">Consular Services</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support and assist Australian travellers and Australians overseas through high‑quality consular services, including accurate and timely travel advice, practical contingency planning and rapid crisis response</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>AusAID</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>413.001</td>
<td colspan="2">Official Development Assistance—Papua New Guinea and Pacific</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist Papua New Guinea and other developing countries in the Pacific region to reduce poverty and achieve sustainable development</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>413.002</td>
<td colspan="2">Official Development Assistance—East Asia</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist developing countries in the East Asia region to reduce poverty and achieve sustainable development</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>413.003</td>
<td colspan="2">Official Development Assistance—Africa, South and Central Asia, Middle East and Other</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist developing countries in Africa, South and Central Asia and the Middle East to reduce poverty and achieve sustainable development</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>413.004</td>
<td colspan="2">Official Development Assistance—Emergency, Humanitarian and Refugee Program</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist developing countries to respond to emergencies and assist refugees</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>413.005</td>
<td colspan="2">Official Development Assistance—United Nations, Commonwealth and Other International Organisations</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist developing countries through contributions to the United Nations, Commonwealth and other international organisations</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>413.006</td>
<td colspan="2">Official Development Assistance—Non‑Government Organisation, Volunteer and Community Programs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To assist developing countries through contributions to non‑government organisation, volunteer and community programs</i></td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>414.002</td>
<td colspan="2">Income Management Card</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To support the delivery of income management measures, also known as the Basics Card</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><b><i>Department of Health and Ageing</b></i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415.001</td>
<td colspan="2">Prevention, early detection and service improvement</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objectives: To fund projects aimed at reducing the incidence of chronic disease, to support the early detection and prevention of cancer through screening, and to provide funding for chronic disease management, support and palliative care services</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415.002</td>
<td colspan="2">Communicable disease control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide funding to reduce the incidence of blood‑borne viruses and sexually‑transmitted infections</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415.003</td>
<td colspan="2">Drug strategy</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To reduce the harmful effects of tobacco use and fund the provision of treatment services to reduce the harm to individuals and communities from excessive alcohol consumption, and to combat illicit drug use</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415.004</td>
<td colspan="2">Regulatory policy</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objectives: To support the development of national food and gene technology regulatory policy, maintain and improve the therapeutic goods regulatory framework, and promote the safe and sustainable use of industrial chemicals</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415.005</td>
<td colspan="2">National Immunisation Program</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><i>Objective: To provide vaccines and financial support to strengthen immunisation coverage, reduce the incidence of vaccine‑preventable diseases, and improve the administration of the National Immunisation Program</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415.006</td>
<td colspan="2">Public health</td>
</tr>

## Schedule 1AB—Arrangements, grants and programs

Note: See regulation 16.

### Part 1—Arrangements under which public money is, or may become, payable by the Commonwealth

<table>
<tr>
<td colspan="3">Arrangements</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Name</td>
<td>Purpose</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>Arrangement with Education Services Australia Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to Education Services Australia Limited in conjunction with the States and Territories to:<br>(a) implement interoperability services for school education; and<br>(b) implement the Commonwealth government’s information hub for students, parents and teachers on safety and wellbeing (the Student Wellbeing Hub); and<br>(c) develop and deliver education resources and professional development material for teachers; and<br>(d) provide assistance to, and implement the projects and initiatives of, the forum of Ministers created by National Cabinet to deal with education and related matters.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29);<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Articles 2 and 13); or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>Arrangements to acquire CEA Technologies Pty Limited</td>
<td>To acquire interests in CEA Technologies Pty Limited or any company incorporated for the purpose of acquiring and holding shares in CEA Technologies Pty Limited.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries; or<br>(b) for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and of the States; or<br>(c) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td>Arrangement to acquire shares in Silicon Quantum Computing Pty Ltd</td>
<td>To acquire shares in Silicon Quantum Computing Pty Ltd.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>Arrangements to pay directors of the Bundanon Trust</td>
<td>To pay remuneration and allowances to directors of the Bundanon Trust, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td>Arrangements with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)</td>
<td>To make contributions, including additional or voluntary contributions, towards the operations and projects of ICAO.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6</td>
<td>Arrangement with Snowy Hydro Limited</td>
<td>To provide a loan to Snowy Hydro Limited to finance the construction of the Snowy 2.0 project.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4;<br>(ii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 and 7.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<td>To provide funding to Tasmania for the continued operation of the Mersey Community Hospital.</td>

<td>To establish and fund schemes for making loans to eligible farm businesses.</td>

<td>To provide grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory for the development and delivery of trials that test ways of using technology to improve the safety of women experiencing, or at risk of, violence.</td>

</tr>

<td>To construct a shared biosecurity diagnostic facility in northern Australia.</td>

<td>To establish and fund a scheme for making loans to eligible farm businesses.</td>
</tr>

<td>School education—Tasmania</td>
<td>To provide grants of financial assistance to Tasmania to fund specialist literacy programs and other support programs for Tasmanian students at government and non‑government schools.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>10</td>
<td>Grants for school education reform</td>
<td>To provide grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory to enable the State or Territory to undertake school education reform or implement national policy measures relating to school education.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>11</td>
<td>Family law payments to States and Territories</td>
<td>To provide funding to the States and Territories for:<br>(a) the exercise by State and Territory courts of federal jurisdiction under the <i>Family Law Act 1975</i>, the <i>Child Support (Registration and Collection) Act 1988</i> and the <i>Child Support (Assessment) Act 1989</i>; and<br>(b) the use of State court facilities by the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 1) and the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2).<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in connection with, or incidental to, the investing of any court of a State with federal jurisdiction; or<br>(b) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>12</td>
<td>Grants to improve road safety in Australia</td>
<td>To provide grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory to support activities and projects to reduce deaths and injuries from road crashes in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>13</td>
<td>Payments for activities that counter illicit tobacco</td>
<td>To provide grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory for State or Territory law enforcement agencies to undertake activities to counter illicit tobacco.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>14</td>
<td>Grants for major and community infrastructure projects</td>
<td>To provide grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory for the planning, construction or upgrading of infrastructure, including community infrastructure, and for incidental matters.</td>
</tr>

<table>

<td>Name</td>

<td>2</td>

<td>To establish and fund a scheme for the provision, to general practices in rural and regional Australia, of additional consultation space for teaching and training to provide:<br>(a) benefits to students; and<br>(b) support incidental to the Commonwealth’s provision of sickness and hospital benefits and medical services.</td>

<tr>
<td>3</td>

<td>To establish and fund a National Centre of Excellence in Youth Mental Health to undertake nationally significant research and collaboration with research partnership nodes as activities that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>Voluntary contributions to the Information Sharing Centre established by the Regional Cooperation Agreement on Combating Piracy and Armed Robbery against Ships in Asia</td>
<td>To contribute to the financing of the Information Sharing Centre, in accordance with the Agreement, to enable the Centre to promote close cooperation among the parties to the Agreement in preventing and suppressing piracy and armed robbery against ships.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td>Grants to Life Education Australia</td>
<td>In conformity with Australia’s international obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, to fund research, development, monitoring, evaluation, relationship management, marketing, fundraising and other activities associated with the Life Education programme.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6</td>
<td>Grant to GCFC Limited (ACN 144 555 822)</td>
<td>To fund the construction of a replacement training and administration base for the Gold Coast Suns Australian Football League team at Metricon Stadium so as to enable the site of the team’s existing training and administration base to be used in connection with City of Gold Coast’s hosting of the 2018 Commonwealth Games, a sports initiative of national significance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7</td>
<td>Grants for research and development relating to energy use data</td>
<td>To improve Australia’s national capacity to collect, organise, analyse and communicate energy use data, by contributing to the funding of the following activities:<br>(a) research and investigation into energy use in Australia, energy use data and related data;<br>(b) dissemination of the results of such research and investigation;<br>(c) the development, implementation and operation of supporting systems and governance arrangements;<br>to the extent that:<br>(d) the data is statistical in nature; or<br>(e) the activities are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) the activities will assist Australia to meet its obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8</td>
<td>Australian Children’s Music Foundation</td>
<td>To fund the Australian Children’s Music Foundation to improve the equity of access to, and participation and engagement in, music education by Australian students in:<br>(a) schools with a significant proportion of disadvantaged students; and<br>(b) schools with a significant proportion of students who are Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders; and<br>(c) juvenile justice centres.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 28, 29 and 31);<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Articles 13 and 15); or<br>(b) to benefit Aboriginal persons and Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(c) by providing benefits to students; or<br>(d) in or in relation to a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>9</td>
<td>Grant to Australian Federation of Ethnic Schools Associations Inc (trading as Community Languages Australia)</td>
<td>To fund Australian Federation of Ethnic Schools Associations Inc to improve the provision of community languages to Australian school students.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding by:<br>(a) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Article 29); or<br>(b) collecting data and otherwise conducting research for the purpose of informing the Commonwealth; or<br>(c) developing and providing online educational, research and resource material.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>10</td>
<td>Grants to the Royal Institute for Deaf and Blind Children</td>
<td>To fund the delivery of specialist allied health and education services to children, aged 18 years or under, with hearing or vision impairment, and their families, in remote and regional locations in Australia:<br>(a) as the provision of sickness benefits or benefits to students; or<br>(b) using postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services; or<br>(c) to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>11</td>
<td>Grants to Australian Kookaburra Kids Foundation Incorporated</td>
<td>To fund Australian Kookaburra Kids Foundation Incorporated to develop, deliver and evaluate a national support, respite and education program specifically for children of current and ex‑serving members of the Australian Defence Force who are affected by mental illness as a result of their military service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>13</td>
<td>Grants to The Smith Family</td>
<td>To fund The Smith Family to provide financial and other support to disadvantaged primary and high school students and their families aimed at increasing the students’ long‑term participation in education, including attendance at, and completion of, school, and expanding their opportunities for work and training post‑school, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6(2), 18(2), 28(1) and 29(1);<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>14</td>
<td>Grant to Grower Co‑Operative Limited</td>
<td>To conduct studies to develop initiatives to improve efficiencies for the movement of grain along the supply chain from farms to the Port of Newcastle, for export to other countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>16</td>
<td>Centenary of ANZAC Centre</td>
<td>To assist in the establishment of the Centenary of ANZAC Centre and to support the Centre to provide:<br>(a) a mental health practitioner support service; and<br>(b) a mental health treatment research centre.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to commemorate Australians killed or injured in war, or to support veterans or defence force members or their families or communities; or<br>(b) to provide medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>17</td>
<td>Mental Health in Multicultural Australia</td>
<td>To strengthen the capacity of individuals, communities and health service providers to address the mental health needs of Australia’s culturally and linguistically diverse population (including immigrants and refugees) in a culturally inclusive and responsive manner.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Article 8; or<br>(b) in connection with electronic and telephonic communications; or<br>(c) relating to immigrants or aliens; or<br>(d) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>18</td>
<td>Grant to Surf Life Saving Australia</td>
<td>To fund Surf Life Saving Australia to boost its capacity to deliver preventative safety measures at local beaches by:<br>(a) investing in technology upgrades; and<br>(b) expanding volunteer training opportunities; and<br>(c) improving skills development for existing supervisors, trainers and assessors; and<br>(d) expanding recruitment and recognition of supervisors, trainers and assessors.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>19</td>
<td>National Institute for Forest Products Innovation</td>
<td>To establish and fund the National Institute for Forest Products Innovation in order to develop, fund and promote innovation and research activities relating to forestry products.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities to the extent that such activities are otherwise peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>23</td>
<td>Loan to the University of the Sunshine Coast</td>
<td>To provide a loan to the University of the Sunshine Coast to construct infrastructure to support the delivery of higher education services and innovation.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing a loan:<br>(a) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 13; or<br>(b) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(c) to provide benefits to students.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>24</td>
<td>Grants to the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership Limited</td>
<td>To fund the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership Limited to provide national leadership for the Commonwealth, State and Territory governments in promoting excellence in the profession of teaching and school leadership, including by:<br>(a) working collaboratively with government and non‑government sector employers and authorities, professional associations, education unions and other relevant bodies throughout Australia; and<br>(b) developing and implementing national approaches to:<br>(i) professional standards for teachers and school leaders; and<br>(ii) initial teacher education, school leadership, and teaching; and<br>(iii) principal preparation and certification; and<br>(iv) teacher registration; and<br>(v) measuring teacher effectiveness; and<br>(c) conducting research and developing the evidence base for national education reforms.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Articles 2 and 13); or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29); or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>25</td>
<td>Education Services Australia Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to Education Services Australia Limited in conjunction with the States and Territories to:<br>(a) implement interoperability services for school education; and<br>(b) implement the Commonwealth government’s information hub for students, parents and teachers on safety and wellbeing (the Student Wellbeing Hub); and<br>(c) develop and deliver education resources and professional development material for teachers; and<br>(d) provide assistance to, and implement the projects and initiatives of, the Council of Australian Governments Education Council.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to education measures:<br>(a) relating to postal, telegraphic, telephonic or other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29); or<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Articles 2 and 13); or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of the nation and which cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>26</td>
<td>Dorothea Mackellar Memorial Society</td>
<td>To fund the Dorothea Mackellar Memorial Society to administer the Dorothea Mackellar Poetry Awards.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13; or<br>(b) engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>27</td>
<td>Grant to the Brotherhood of St Laurence</td>
<td>To fund the Brotherhood of St Laurence to develop and implement, in collaboration with stakeholders, measures to promote the employment of young people nationally.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(b) taken in connection with online or electronic communications; or<br>(c) taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>28</td>
<td>Grant to The Smith Family—Let’s Read</td>
<td>To provide funding for The Smith Family’s <i>Let’s Read</i> program to assist children to develop early literacy skills, including by providing their parents, teachers and other caregivers with:<br>(a) children’s books and other learning resources; or<br>(b) information, education and other support to facilitate childhood learning.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures giving effect to Australia’s obligations:<br>(a) in relation to children, including those under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6(2), 17, 18(2), 28 and 29; or<br>(b) under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>29</td>
<td>Grants to the Foundation for Rural and Regional Renewal</td>
<td>To provide funding to contribute to and support the achievement of the object of the Foundation for Rural and Regional Renewal, namely to promote for the public benefit rural and regional renewal, regeneration and development in Australia in social, economic, environmental and cultural areas.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to enabling the Foundation to provide funding:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(c) to or in relation to immigrants or aliens; or<br>(d) for the provision of unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, medical services and benefits to students, and for matters incidental to the provision of those benefits or services; or<br>(e) to or in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(f) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under international agreements, including the following:<br>(i) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 4, 5, and 10;<br>(ii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4;<br>(iii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iv) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 7 and 8;<br>(v) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 11 and 12;<br>(vi) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(vii) the international treaties referred to in the definition of <b><i>relevant international agreement</b></i> in subsection 4(1) of the <i>Water Act 2007</i>; or<br>(g) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(h) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(i) for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(j) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td>Grant to Queensland Fruit & Vegetable Growers Ltd</td>
<td>To provide funding to Queensland Fruit & Vegetable Growers Ltd to foster fair employment practices in the Australian horticulture industry, including through the development and implementation of a national training and certification program for horticultural producers and packing houses.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services; or<br>(c) with respect to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Forced or Compulsory Labour, particularly Article 1(1);<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Labour Administration: Role, Functions and Organisation, particularly Article 6;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 7; or<br>(e) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>31</td>
<td>Grant to Educational Music Tour Bus Foundation Australia Ltd</td>
<td>To fund the establishment and operation of the John Lennon Educational Bus to provide:<br>(a) educational activities in music, the arts and technology for children, including the provision of vocational information and guidance; and<br>(b) activities for the benefit of Indigenous communities.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28, 29 and 31; or<br>(b) for, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>32</td>
<td>Grants to Orygen, the National Centre of Excellence in Youth Mental Health</td>
<td>To support the following activities of the National Centre of Excellence in Youth Mental Health:<br>(a) the provision of advice to the Commonwealth government on improving services to young people affected by mental health issues;<br>(b) the provision of training and information to the mental health workforce;<br>(c) research in the field of youth mental health.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>

<td>33</td>
<td>Grants to Free TV Australia Ltd</td>
<td>To fund Free TV Australia Ltd to distribute Australian television content in the Indo‑Pacific region for transmission by local broadcasters.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>34</td>
<td>Grants to The Bell Shakespeare Company Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to The Bell Shakespeare Company Limited to facilitate performing arts education in schools by:<br>(a) developing theatre productions and:<br>(i) delivering those productions to school students; or<br>(ii) streaming those productions to schools over the internet; and<br>(b) providing discounted tickets to school students to attend theatre productions by the company; and<br>(c) mentoring and training teachers to better equip them to deliver performing arts education in schools; and<br>(d) developing resources, including digital resources, to support performing arts education in schools.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(b) for the provision of benefits to students; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 28, 29 and 31);<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Articles 2 and 15); or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>35</td>
<td>Grants to improve road safety in Australia</td>
<td>To reduce deaths and injuries from road crashes in Australia by providing funding to support or facilitate activities or projects including the following:<br>(a) activities that support the priorities identified in the National Road Safety Strategy 2011‑2020 and associated Action Plans;<br>(b) research into road safety issues and associated matters;<br>(c) education campaigns and other activities to increase public awareness of, and community engagement with, road safety issues;<br>(d) activities or projects to improve road safety (for drivers, passengers, pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists), including in relation to addressing driver distraction, reducing drug driving, increasing the uptake of safer vehicles, and improving road safety in regional and remote areas of Australia;<br>(e) activities to ensure the coordination of effort in relation to road safety throughout Australia;<br>(f) collaboration among entities involved in road safety activities in Australia;<br>(g) participation in road safety awareness and education initiatives by representatives of countries in the Asia Pacific region;<br>(h) international engagement on road safety.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories (within the meaning of paragraph 51(i) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to statistics (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xi) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(f) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia, or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(g) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(h) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(i) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>

<td>Grant to News Corp—Online Spelling Bee</td>
<td>To assist News Corp Australia Pty Limited in the development of an online spelling bee.</td>
</tr>

<td>DP Jones Nursing Home</td>
<td>To provide funding to support:<br>(a) the continued operation of the DP Jones Nursing Home in Murchison, Victoria by the liquidator of Murchison Community Care Inc. while Murchison Community Care Inc. is in liquidation; and<br>(b) the sale of the DP Jones Nursing Home by that liquidator.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to bankruptcy or insolvency (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xvii) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 12.</td>
</tr>

<td>To fund Imparja Television Pty Ltd to support its continued provision of commercial television services in regional and remote Australia.</td>
</tr>

<td>40</td>
<td>Grant to Anti‑Defamation Commission Incorporated—Click Against Hate program</td>
<td>To fund Anti‑Defamation Commission Incorporated to deliver the Click Against Hate program to participating primary and secondary schools, to equip young people with strategies and skills to combat hate experienced online.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 2 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 18 and 19;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>

<td>41</td>
<td>Grant to DemoDAIRY Foundation Limited—Powell Legacy Fund</td>
<td>To provide a grant to DemoDAIRY Foundation Limited to fund the Powell Legacy Fund to provide scholarships to eligible persons as a measure to provide benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 13;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4.</td>

<td>Grants to University of Technology Sydney for Anti‑Slavery Australia—Complex Violence Intervention (Forced Marriage) Project</td>
<td>To provide funding to University of Technology Sydney for Anti‑Slavery Australia to develop and implement measures to prevent forced marriage, including by:<br>(a) establishing and maintaining an online forum to offer information, support and assistance to those at risk of forced marriage; and<br>(b) providing training and resources to community workers to enhance their ability to support and assist those at risk of forced marriage.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 32, 34, 35 and 36;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 23;<br>(iv) the Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery, the Slave Trade, and Institutions and Practices Similar to Slavery, particularly Article 1.</td>

<td>Grants to the International Financial Reporting Standards Foundation</td>
<td>To provide ongoing support to the International Financial Reporting Standards Foundation to assist it in the development and promotion of the International Financial Reporting Standards.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>45</td>
<td>Grant to the Trustee for Raise Foundation</td>
<td>To fund the Trustee for Raise Foundation to develop and deliver a best‑practice early intervention mentoring program aimed at preventing mental illness and reducing suicidal ideation in Year 8 students at public secondary schools in Australia, including by:<br>(a) developing and delivering:<br>(i) services for the early identification of, and intervention strategies for, mental illness in such students; and<br>(ii) school‑based interventions to improve student engagement and increase the mental health awareness, understanding and help‑seeking capacity of such students; and<br>(iii) services for reducing suicidal ideation in, and the effect of bullying on, such students; and<br>(b) developing and disseminating resources to increase mental health awareness and educate young people and their families about the different types of help and support available;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(c) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24;<br>(d) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>

<td>To fund a company, established in conjunction with the States and Territories, to engage in activities that strengthen the national education evidence base for school and early childhood education, including through:<br>(a) collaborating with government, the school and early childhood education sector, the vocational education and training sector, the higher‑education and research sector and philanthropic organisations; and<br>(b) developing and implementing a national agenda relating to research; and<br>(c) mobilising high‑quality resources for school and early childhood education; and<br>(d) supporting teaching and learning in school and early childhood education.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>48</td>
<td>Grant to Islamic Museum of Australia</td>
<td>To support Islamic Museum of Australia, including assisting it to:<br>(a) develop educational resources and online learning platforms; and<br>(b) upgrade its infrastructure and facilities; and<br>(c) deliver education and training;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(d) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 29;<br>(e) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 7;<br>(f) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 27.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>

<td>To provide funding to support the continued operation of working women’s centres, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 3 and 11;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 7;<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Labour Administration: Role, Functions and Organisation, particularly Article 6.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for measures incidental to the execution of the legislative powers vested in the Commonwealth; or<br>(c) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(d) for measures undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>

<td>To provide funding to The Embrace Collective Ltd to promote healthy body image ideas to children under 18 years of age, including by:<br>(a) providing educational and training resources to parents of such children and professionals and volunteers who work with such children; and<br>(b) providing resources to, and community‑based events for, such children, their educators, parents, advisors, ambassadors and community leaders; and<br>(c) conducting a communications campaign; and<br>(d) undertaking evaluation.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4 and 24).</td>
