<td>75</td>
<td>Grants to Royal Children’s Hospital Good Friday Appeal</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Royal Children’s Hospital Good Friday Appeal to support the Royal Children’s Hospital to implement the following initiatives:<br>(a) the Melbourne Children’s Campus Mental Health Strategy;<br>(b) the Enhancing Regional Paediatric Healthcare Access Project to enhance the capacity and capability of regional and rural paediatric health services for children under the age of 18 years by improving access to, and the quality and coordination of, those services, including by doing any of the following:<br>(i) supplying medical or allied health equipment, including equipment for the purposes of training;<br>(ii) providing education and training for medical, allied health and other staff who support or enable the delivery of medical or allied health services;<br>(iii) undertaking research programs;<br>(iv) providing adequate medical, nursing or allied health staffing;<br>(v) building works to deliver health services to paediatric patients;<br>(vi) developing new models of health care;<br>(vii) delivering health care closer to patients’ homes;<br>(viii) improving access to mental health care for priority population groups;<br>(c) the National Paediatric Health Literacy Platform, involving the development, enhancement or operation of an online health platform for children under the age of 18 years and their parents or carers that supports paediatric care or sharing of evidence‑based and age‑appropriate health information, including any of the following:<br>(i) resources, advice and tools for parents or carers to support children’s health;<br>(ii) surveys of paediatric patients, their parents or carers;<br>(iii) resources on health issues facing children, on mental wellbeing and on triaging access to online health resources;<br>(iv) social media content to combat health misinformation and to engage with children on health and mental health issues.<br>This purpose has the objective it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>76</td>
<td>Grant to The Seed Library Incorporated</td>
<td>To support The Seed Library Incorporated to provide seed packs (collections of vegetable and flower seeds) and education materials to government schools, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligation under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 24, 28 and 29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>77</td>
<td>Grants to the Australian Red Cross Society</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Australian Red Cross Society to raise awareness of, and disseminate information about, international humanitarian law, including by:<br>(a) delivering training and briefings; and<br>(b) issuing and contributing to publications and making submissions; and<br>(c) participating in relevant conferences and events, and<br>(d) monitoring and maintaining correct use of the Red Cross emblem;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(e) the Geneva Convention (I) for the Amelioration of the Condition of the Wounded and Sick in Armed Forces in the Field, particularly Article 47;<br>(f) the Geneva Convention (II) for the Amelioration of the Condition of Wounded, Sick and Shipwrecked Members of Armed Forces at Sea, particularly Article 48;<br>(g) the Geneva Convention (III) relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War, particularly Article 127;<br>(h) the Geneva Convention (IV) relative to the Protection of Civilian Persons in Time of War, particularly Article 144;<br>(i) the Protocol Additional to the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949, and relating to the Protection of Victims of International Armed Conflicts (Protocol I), particularly Article 83;<br>(j) the Protocol Additional to the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949, and relating to the Adoption of an Additional Distinctive Emblem (Protocol III), particularly Article 7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>78</td>
<td>Grant to the International Foundation for Ethics and Audit</td>
<td>To support the development and promotion of international auditing and assurance standards, including in relation to sustainability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>79</td>
<td>Grant to the Trustees for the Catholic Diocese of Broken Bay</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Trustees of the Roman Catholic Church for the Diocese of Broken Bay (ABN 79 031 652 544) for capital works in relation to a new preschool in Toukley, NSW as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>80</td>
<td>Grant to Nordoff‑Robbins Music Therapy Australia Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) music therapy programs; and<br>(b) community music programs for veterans, First Nations people, people with disability and children.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to support veterans and their families; or<br>(c) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 25 and 30;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 23, 24, 27, 28 and 29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>81</td>
<td>Grants to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (as administrator of the International Fund for Ukraine)</td>
<td>To provide funding to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland as a financial contribution to the International Fund for Ukraine.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>82</td>
<td>Grant to GO Foundation</td>
<td>To provide funding to the GO Foundation to support young First Nations people through the provision of access to quality education, mentorship and pathways to employment, including by:<br>(a) providing scholarships, mentoring programs and support services; and<br>(b) engaging in partnerships with schools, universities, government agencies, corporate partners and community organisations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>83</td>
<td>Grant to Chain Reaction Foundation Ltd</td>
<td>To provide funding to Chain Reaction Foundation Ltd to continue the Learning Ground in School program, in order to improve student engagement with education by supporting participating schools to support their students, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>84</td>
<td>Grant to the National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education Corporation</td>
<td>To provide funding to the National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education Corporation to support its role as the national education peak body for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) undertaken in the exercise of, or which are incidental to, the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>85</td>
<td>Grant to the Kimberley Land Council Aboriginal Corporation</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Kimberley Land Council Aboriginal Corporation to conduct research to support the listing of the West Kimberley on the World Heritage List, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, particularly Articles 4, 5 and 11.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>86</td>
<td>Grant to the Alcohol and Drug Foundation Incorporated</td>
<td>To give effect to Australia’s obligations under the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, particularly under Article 5, by providing funding to the Alcohol and Drug Foundation Incorporated to:<br>(a) design a vaping prevention education training package directed to sporting clubs, coaches and leaders to assist them to support young people to understand vaping‑related issues such as harms and prevention, and to promote available quit supports; and<br>(b) deliver the training to sporting clubs, coaches and leaders.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>87</td>
<td>Grant to The Project Rozana Foundation Ltd</td>
<td>To fund The Project Rozana Foundation Ltd to deliver The Day After Project:<br>(a) to provide equipment for the new Al Rahma Rehabilitation Hospital in Hebron to address shortfalls in rehabilitation services; and<br>(b) to improve the capacity of the Palestinian health sector and cooperation between Palestinian and Israeli health institutions;<br>as a measure with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>88</td>
<td>Grant to White Box Enterprises Ltd</td>
<td>To provide funding to White Box Enterprises Ltd to contribute to, and support the administration of, the Social Enterprise Loan Fund, which is used to provide loans to social enterprises with a core mission of employing disadvantaged persons, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Article 1;<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Article 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>89</td>
<td>Grant to the Australasian Professional Society on Alcohol & Other Drugs</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Australasian Professional Society on Alcohol & Other Drugs to support the development and availability of scientific research and related materials in the alcohol and other drug field through the publication and distribution of the Drug and Alcohol Review journal over the internet.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(c) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Article 38;<br>(d) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>90</td>
<td>Grant to the Alcohol and Drug Foundation Incorporated—Alcohol and Drug Information Network</td>
<td>To increase the availability of evidence‑based information regarding alcohol and other drugs through the Alcohol and Drug Information Network by providing funding to the Alcohol and Drug Foundation Incorporated to:<br>(a) compile and provide access to print and online evidence‑based information regarding alcohol and other drugs, including information about:<br>(i) the effects of substances; and<br>(ii) harm reduction and prevention; and<br>(b) develop and provide access to online tools and resources regarding alcohol and other drugs; and<br>(c) collect and analyse data to ensure information provided by the Foundation is relevant and continues to meet community needs; and<br>(d) provide alcohol and other drug information that is culturally relevant to Indigenous people.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(iii) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Article 38;<br>(iv) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>91</td>
<td>Grant to the University of Sydney</td>
<td>To provide funding to the University of Sydney to improve the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (<b><i>FASD</b></i>) in Australian children by maintaining the FASD Australian Registry, a central database for collecting national FASD data to monitor FASD trends and outcomes throughout the Australian population.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>92</td>
<td>Grant to the University of Newcastle</td>
<td>To provide funding to the University of Newcastle to deliver the SMS4dads project, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>93</td>
<td>Grant to the Australian National Academy of Music Ltd.</td>
<td>To fund the Australian National Academy of Music Ltd. to redevelop, restore and enhance its South Melbourne Town Hall premises, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>94</td>
<td>Grant to Goanna Foundation Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Goanna Foundation Limited to design, deliver, evaluate and improve prevention and early‑intervention programs to support mental health outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and communities, including through community engagement and co‑design.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>95</td>
<td>Grant to the Rev Bill Crews Foundation Ltd</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Rev Bill Crews Foundation Ltd to support Australians experiencing financial hardship by:<br>(a) providing specialist support for people experiencing family, domestic or sexual violence; and<br>(b) providing play therapy services for children; and<br>(c) providing literacy programs for children and young people; and<br>(d) supporting the provision of medical, dental and other health services.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical and dental services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 19, 23, 24, 27, 28 and 29;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 9 and 17;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(v) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Articles 4 and 38; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>96</td>
<td>Grant to Partnerships for Local Action and Community Empowerment Ltd</td>
<td>To provide funding to Partnerships for Local Action and Community Empowerment Ltd to enable place‑based change through supporting the development and implementation of place‑based approaches, partnerships and solutions (<b><i>place‑based initiatives</b></i>) that improve social and economic outcomes in communities, and advance public welfare, including by:<br>(a) developing, disseminating and promoting the exchange of resources, tools and frameworks, and promoting best practice models, relating to place‑based initiatives; and<br>(b) promoting and enabling strengthened data practices in place‑based initiatives, including generating an evidence base that validates the impact of place‑based initiatives; and<br>(c) building the skills and capabilities of the workforce to better develop and deliver place‑based initiatives; and<br>(d) supporting stakeholders to identify and seek collaborative resolutions to local challenges and to systemic challenges that have a significant or national impact; and<br>(e) promoting the development of policy and funding approaches that support effective place‑based initiatives; and<br>(f) supporting the adoption of place‑based initiatives, including the development and practice of shared decision‑making; and<br>(g) providing the operational infrastructure and other associated costs required to deliver on this purpose.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures, or measures for the delivery of Commonwealth programs:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(d) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, medical and dental services or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(f) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(g) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(h) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more treaties, including the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5, 6, 12 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 27;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18, 19, 24, 27, 28, 29, and 30;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 10 and 12; or<br>(i) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(j) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(k) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(l) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.<br>This purpose also has the effect that it would have if it were limited to measures that are undertaken for the purpose of, or in connection with, any program specified in an item in Part 4 of this Schedule that is supported by any other Commonwealth legislative power.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>97</td>
<td>Grant to Charles Darwin University</td>
<td>To provide funding to Charles Darwin University in the Northern Territory to operate the North Australia and Rangelands Fire Information web service, which provides data, maps and other resources to manage bushfires in rural and remote parts of Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>98</td>
<td>Grant to Capital Health Network Ltd—Alcohol and Other Drugs</td>
<td>To provide funding to Capital Health Network Ltd to support access to health‑related education and information, as well as the prevention and treatment of the abuse of alcohol and other drugs, by delivering a community withdrawal support service, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24;<br>(iii) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Articles 4 and 38;<br>(iv) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>99</td>
<td>Grant to Wentworth Healthcare Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to Wentworth Healthcare Limited to support access to health‑related education and information, as well as the prevention and treatment of the abuse of alcohol and other drugs and mental illness, by delivering comprehensive community‑based addiction services, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(b) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24;<br>(c) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Articles 4 and 38;<br>(d) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>100</td>
<td>Grant to Launceston City Mission Inc</td>
<td>To provide funding to Launceston City Mission Inc to support the operation of residential alcohol and other drug rehabilitation, recovery and support facilities at Serenity House in Burnie, Tasmania, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(c) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Articles 4 and 38;<br>(d) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>101</td>
<td>Grant to the University of New South Wales for the National Centre for Clinical Research on Emerging Drugs</td>
<td>To provide funding to the University of New South Wales to support the National Centre for Clinical Research on Emerging Drugs to undertake research, educational activities and policy development activities relating to methamphetamine and new and emerging drugs, including:<br>(a) research for the purposes of improving treatment and overall health outcomes; and<br>(b) developing and disseminating products for clinical practice and clinical guidance; and<br>(c) developing and piloting new internet‑based therapies; and<br>(d) supporting information‑sharing networks and platforms, such as the Prompt Response Network;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(e) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(f) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(g) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Articles 4 and 38;<br>(h) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>102</td>
<td>Grant to Street Side Medics Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to Street Side Medics Limited to support the provision of mobile health services to people experiencing homelessness.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>103</td>
<td>Grant to Capital Health Network Ltd—Access to Bulk Billing General Practitioners</td>
<td>To provide funding to Capital Health Network Ltd to maintain and increase access to bulk billing general practitioners in the Australian Capital Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>104</td>
<td>Grant to Good to Great Schools Australia</td>
<td>To provide funding to Good to Great Schools Australia to support teachers, people training to be teachers and teaching assistants in regional, rural and remote Australia to obtain accredited credentials to upskill in evidence‑based teaching practices, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>105</td>
<td>Grant to Nafsika Stamoulis Hellenic Museum Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Hellenic Museum to support and enhance Australia’s relationship with Greece and enable Australian audiences to engage with diverse cultural and education experiences by:<br>(a) hosting the <i>Rituals: Gifts for the Gods</i> exhibition; and<br>(b) upgrading the museum’s infrastructure used to support its public programming for the exhibition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>106</td>
<td>Grants to the International Atomic Energy Agency</td>
<td>To contribute to the funding of the International Atomic Energy Agency, including to support the Agency to:<br>(a) undertake the following kinds of activities:<br>(i) activities that support the peaceful application of nuclear science and nuclear technology, including research and development in relation to the application of nuclear science and nuclear technology;<br>(ii) activities that build capacity in relation to the peaceful application of nuclear science and nuclear technology;<br>(iii) activities that support international compliance, and the assessment of international compliance, with nuclear safeguards, including by providing training;<br>(iv) activities that support the development of Australian expertise and capability in relation to nuclear safeguards; and<br>(b) establish, administer and apply nuclear safeguards; and<br>(c) review and, if necessary, modify nuclear safeguards in response to technological change; and<br>(d) carry out research and development in relation to:<br>(i) nuclear safeguards technology; and<br>(ii) nuclear safeguards approaches and methodologies; and<br>(e) implement new and existing techniques and technologies in relation to nuclear safeguards; and<br>(f) provide technical services in relation to nuclear safeguards.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>107</td>
<td>Grant to M Riewoldt Holdings Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to M Riewoldt Holdings Limited to improve outcomes for patients with bone marrow failure syndromes, including by funding the following:<br>(a) research relating to the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of bone marrow failure syndromes;<br>(b) telesupport services and peer support programs;<br>(c) educational outreach services for healthcare providers;<br>(d) the Aplastic Anaemia and other Bone Marrow Failure Syndromes Registry and the Australian Bone Marrow Failure Biobank;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>108</td>
<td>Grant to CareFlight Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to CareFlight Limited to purchase and modify an aircraft to use for emergency aeromedical retrieval services in the Northern Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>109</td>
<td>Grant to FightMND Ltd</td>
<td>To provide funding to FightMND Ltd to undertake activities that support or facilitate:<br>(a) scientific research and development projects, including conferences and opportunities for information sharing, for the diagnosis and treatment of motor neurone disease (<b><i>MND</b></i>); and<br>(b) the Global MND Research Roundtable; and<br>(c) upgrades to its customer relationship management capacity; and<br>(d) the development and distribution of content to raise awareness about MND.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>110</td>
<td>Grant to the Institute of Veterans Advocacy Ltd</td>
<td>To support the operations of the Institute of Veterans Advocacy Ltd to act as the professional body for veterans’ advocates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>111</td>
<td>Grant to the Ballarat City Council for the Ballarat Hub</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Ballarat City Council to establish a facility in Ballarat, Victoria where veterans and their families can be assisted (including by advocates) to access government and non‑government supports and services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>112</td>
<td>Grant to the Executive Council of Australian Jewry</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Executive Council of Australian Jewry to protect Australia’s Jewish community, including by supporting the following:<br>(a) engaging security guards at places or events identified or associated with that community;<br>(b) providing security training, and installing security equipment and infrastructure, to identify and address security or safety risks to that community;<br>(c) activities to identify, assess and respond to security or safety risks to that community;<br>(d) offsetting the operational costs of state‑based Community Security Groups;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(e) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 5;<br>(f) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 18 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>113</td>
<td>Grant to the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists to deliver training for multidisciplinary healthcare teams and hospital staff with responsibility for delivering maternity or maternity‑related services in regional, rural and remote communities, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>114</td>
<td>Grant to the Australian Breastfeeding Association</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Australian Breastfeeding Association to support the Association to provide:<br>(a) a national breastfeeding helpline telephone service; and<br>(b) an online breastfeeding information and support service;<br>as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>115</td>
<td>Grant to FightMND Ltd—Neale Daniher MND Clinical Network</td>
<td>To provide funding to FightMND Ltd to establish the Neale Daniher MND Clinical Network to undertake activities that support or facilitate:<br>(a) clinical trials and scientific research projects in relation to either or both of the following:<br>(i) the diagnosis of motor neurone disease (MND);<br>(ii) the treatment of MND; and<br>(b) the establishment of an MND databank, and related activities to uplift data infrastructure or improve data about MND; and<br>(c) fellowships, scholarships and other supports for researchers, health professionals and students who are working or studying in the field of MND research.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>116</td>
<td>Grants to the National Allergy Council Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to the National Allergy Council Limited to:<br>(a) deliver allergy‑related preventive health and education programs and support services to the public; and<br>(b) implement and improve allergy documentation and reporting systems; and<br>(c) provide allergy‑related training and resources to the public, including health professionals, early childhood educators and persons living with allergies;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>117</td>
<td>Grants to the Murdoch Children’s Research Institute</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Murdoch Children’s Research Institute to facilitate the National Allergy Centre of Excellence continuing to undertake and support research into allergies, including by:<br>(a) undertaking:<br>(i) clinical trials relating to allergies; and<br>(ii) assessments of National Allergy Council programs; and<br>(b) maintaining platforms and resources for collecting and storing information on allergies; and<br>(c) identifying and addressing research gaps in allergy prevention and treatment guidelines;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>118</td>
<td>Grant to the Indigenous Marathon Foundation Limited</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Indigenous Marathon Foundation Limited to continue the Indigenous Marathon Project, including by recruiting, and providing culturally appropriate support to, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and particular groups of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, to undergo marathon training and complete educational and leadership courses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>119</td>
<td>Grant to the Jean Hailes Foundation</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Jean Hailes Foundation to:<br>(a) undertake research and educate health professionals and consumers in the prevention, early detection, and management of diseases affecting women; and<br>(b) fill critical gaps in women’s health care and work towards a more equitable health system for all women;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(c) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 10, and 12;<br>(d) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>120</td>
<td>Grant to Breast Cancer Network Australia</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Breast Cancer Network Australia to deliver consumer representative training.<br>This purpose has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
</table>

### Part 4—Programs

<table>
<tr>
<td colspan="3">Programs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Program</td>
<td>Objective(s)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>Red Meat and Cattle sector—International Co‑operation and Investment Programme</td>
<td>To provide assistance and support to the red meat and cattle sector in overseas countries by measures including:<br>(a) promoting Australian investment in those sectors; and<br>(b) undertaking and supporting collaborative projects, including those involving educational, developmental and capacity building activities; and<br>(c) fostering or assisting with commercial development opportunities and domestic sectoral promotion.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>Empowered Communities</td>
<td>To support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander persons by strengthening local leadership and building strong, safe, healthy and prosperous communities through the design and implementation of a reform model for Indigenous policy and service delivery.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6</td>
<td>School Attendance Strategies</td>
<td>1. To encourage regular attendance of students at schools by providing assistance and services to those students and their families, schools and communities, (including by providing officers to assist school attendance) where:<br>(a) the assistance and services provided would be of benefit to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) the provision of the assistance and services would assist Australia to meet its obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Art 28(1)), or<br>(c) the school concerned is in a Territory.<br>2. To encourage regular attendance of Indigenous students at schools by providing assistance and services to those students and their families, schools and communities, (including by providing officers to assist school attendance).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>9</td>
<td>New Colombo Plan</td>
<td>To provide benefits to Australian undergraduate students by providing financial assistance for the purpose of supporting them to undertake study and internships in the Indo‑Pacific region and, in connection with this, to:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(a) lift knowledge of the Indo‑Pacific region in Australia and strengthen our people‑to‑people and institutional relationships by increasing the number of Australian undergraduate students undertaking study and internships in the region; and<br>(b) deepen Australia’s relationships with the region through the engagement of university, business and other stakeholder networks in supporting the programme and ensuring such experiences are highly valued across the Australian community; and<br>(c) help study in the Indo‑Pacific region become a rite of passage for Australian undergraduate students, and increase the number of Asia‑capable and work‑ready Australian graduates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>13</td>
<td>Manufacturing Industry Support</td>
<td>To provide support to manufacturing.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support to:<br>(a) corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(b) manufacturing in connection with interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(c) manufacturing in connection with the Territories.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>14</td>
<td>Fund for Industry Skills</td>
<td>To support industry diversification and competitiveness by providing, or funding, training and training support services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for:<br>(a) the formal or accredited training of workers; or<br>(b) corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies; or<br>(c) the fostering or promotion of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(d) business enterprises or workers in the Territories; or<br>(e) online training and support services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>15</td>
<td>Entrepreneurs’ Infrastructure Programme</td>
<td>To drive business competitiveness by providing, or funding, support for business improvement and the commercialisation of new ideas.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing, or funding, support for:<br>(a) the fostering or promotion of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) businesses involved in interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(c) corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies; or<br>(d) business enterprises or workers in the Territories; or<br>(e) online support services, advice and information.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>16</td>
<td>Growth Fund—Skills and Training Programme</td>
<td>To address the impact of the decline of the automotive manufacturing sector by providing, or arranging for:<br>(a) formal or accredited education and training for automotive workers to facilitate their transition to other work; and<br>(b) services to assist unemployed former automotive workers to continue with their training to gain employment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>17</td>
<td>Automotive Diversification Programme</td>
<td>To assist Australian automotive supply chain companies to diversify their businesses out of the domestic automotive manufacturing sector by providing funding to:<br>(a) corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies; and<br>(b) entities involved in interstate or overseas trade and commerce.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>18</td>
<td>Growth Fund—Next Generation Manufacturing Investment Programme</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to Australian trading corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies involved in manufacturing to promote the growth of the non‑automotive manufacturing sector.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>19</td>
<td>Regional Infrastructure Programme</td>
<td>To fund suitable applicants in undertaking projects or activities to support and develop infrastructure, stimulate new business activity and enhance economic development.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(a) the fostering or promotion of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) businesses involved in interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(c) corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>21</td>
<td>National Insurance Affordability Initiative</td>
<td>To establish and maintain a website which would compare features of, and premiums for, certain strata and home building and contents insurance products.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>23</td>
<td>Community Heritage and Icons Grants</td>
<td>To provide support for activities to conserve, develop and interpret cultural heritage.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s international obligations under the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) that are carried out in a Territory, in a Commonwealth place, or outside Australia; or<br>(d) that are carried out by a trading corporation to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>24</td>
<td>Orangutan Reintroduction Project</td>
<td>To support the protection and rehabilitation of orangutans in Indonesia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>25</td>
<td>National Climate Change Adaptation Research Facility</td>
<td>To support the development of climate change adaptation policy and risk analysis for the purpose of giving effect to Australia’s international obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, including by:<br>(a) assisting local governments to develop a climate change risk management framework; and<br>(b) synthesising and communicating climate change research across key sectors; and</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(c) coordinating research networks that link researchers with decision‑makers managing climate change risk.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>26</td>
<td>Solar Towns Programme</td>
<td>To provide support for community groups to install solar photovoltaic and solar hot water equipment at their facilities to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in order to give effect to Australia’s international obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>27</td>
<td>Rural Research and Development for Profit</td>
<td>To provide support for research and development activities for Australian rural industries:<br>(a) to increase productivity and enhance profitability in order to meet national and global needs; and<br>(b) to the extent that the activities are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td>A Competitive and Sustainable Fisheries Sector</td>
<td>To provide support for national recreational and commercial fishing peak bodies for the development and promotion of sustainable fishing practices by giving effect to Australia’s international obligations for the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>32</td>
<td>Student Prizes Programme</td>
<td>To benefit students by providing prizes to students for excellence in academic and vocational education.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>33</td>
<td>Relocation Assistance to Take Up a Job Programme</td>
<td>To provide payments of financial assistance to unemployed persons and other eligible individuals to assist them to relocate to other areas of Australia to take up employment, including for the purpose of addressing labour shortages resulting from the coronavirus known as COVID‑19.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) involving the provision of unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Article 1;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning the Organisation of the Employment Service, particularly Article 1;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>34</td>
<td>Work for the Dole</td>
<td>To support the Workforce Australia program by:<br>(a) providing benefits to unemployed persons by giving them the skills and attributes to meet the needs of prospective employers (including in circumstances where training in, or acquisition of, such skills and attributes is a condition of their receipt of payments under the <i>Social Security Act 1991</i>); and<br>(b) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programs to enable persons to realise the right to work, giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; and<br>(c) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment, giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; and<br>(d) providing a free public employment service, giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning the Organisation of the Employment Service, particularly Articles 1 and 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>35</td>
<td>Indigenous Advancement—Jobs, Land and Economy</td>
<td>1. The funding and provision of activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services that promote jobs and economic opportunities for Indigenous persons, families, entities and communities or assist them to gain rights and interests in, or derive economic or social benefits from the use of land and sea, including by:<br>(a) promoting economic and social participation, fostering entrepreneurship and supporting economic, community and business development and opportunities; or<br>(b) providing training, employment and employment‑related opportunities and support; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(c) promoting the development of workforce skills and career pathways; or<br>(d) promoting access to vocational and higher education and training; or<br>(e) supporting entities which engage or assist jobseekers and people preparing to enter the labour market; or<br>(f) promoting and supporting land and sea use, development, protection and management; or<br>(g) supporting the pursuit and exercise of native title rights; or<br>(h) supporting access for Indigenous persons, families, entities and communities to affordable, safe and sustainable accommodation, housing and housing amenity.<br>2. The funding and provision of activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services for remote Australia to do one or more of the following:<br>(a) create and sustain jobs and employment;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(b) support employer engagement and community and economic development;<br>(c) create sustainable communities and support sustainable social and economic participation;<br>(d) facilitate transition to work and provide work experience and participation opportunities;<br>(e) assist with the development of skills and improve work readiness, employability and the capacity of persons to participate in the economy;<br>where the activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(f) are the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(g) are the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(h) are the provision of such activities, assistance, infrastructure, research or services in a Territory; or<br>(i) are provided by way of grants of financial assistance to States and Territories; or<br>(k) would assist Australia to meet its international obligations, including its obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly paragraph 1 of article 28 of the Convention); or<br>(l) are done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(m) are otherwise for the benefit of the nation.<br>3. To provide funding to organisations that provide the activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services referred to in the first objective of this item, in order to:<br>(a) support the organisations by funding the operating costs associated with providing the activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services; and<br>(b) assist the organisations to obtain and to claim insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); and<br>(c) provide financial assistance to the organisations that are insolvent, or are at an imminent risk of becoming insolvent; and<br>(d) assist the organisations that are insolvent to deal with the consequences of insolvency.</td>
</tr>

</tr>

The funding and provision of activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services to do one or more of the following:<br>(a) assist Indigenous persons to develop and promote their culture and raise cultural awareness;<br>(b) assist in developing the capabilities of Indigenous persons, families, entities and communities;<br>including by:<br>(c) promoting Indigenous leadership, governance, mentoring, engagement, representation, reconciliation and resilience; or<br>(d) assisting Indigenous persons to gain recognition as first Australians and to develop, communicate, protect and promote awareness of their heritage, culture, language, expression and knowledge; or<br>(e) providing access to, and supporting and enhancing, broadcasting and communication services for Indigenous persons, communities and entities; or</td>

<td></td>
<td>(f) promoting respect and recognition for Indigenous persons; or<br>(g) building the capabilities of Indigenous persons, families, communities and entities to participate in the economy and engage and communicate with broader society.<br>2. <td>1. The funding and provision of activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services that address social and economic disadvantage in remote Australia, including by:<br>(a) creating and sustaining jobs and employment; or<br>(b) supporting employer engagement and community and economic development; or<br>(c) creating sustainable communities and supporting social and economic participation; or<br>(d) facilitating transition to work and providing work experience and participation opportunities; or<br>(e) assisting with the development of skills and improving work readiness, employability and the capacity of persons to participate in the economy; or</td>

To provide funding to organisations that provide the activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services referred to in the first objective of this item, in order to:<br>(a) support the organisations by funding the operating costs associated with providing the activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services; and<br>(b) assist the organisations to obtain and to claim insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); and<br>(c) provide financial assistance to the organisations that are insolvent, or are at an imminent risk of becoming insolvent; and<br>(d) assist the organisations that are insolvent to deal with the consequences of insolvency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>40</td>
<td>Families and Children</td>
<td>To do the following:<br>(a) support families to improve the wellbeing of children and young people;<br>(b) enhance family and community functioning;<br>(c) increase the participation of vulnerable people in community life;<br>including by providing funding as follows:<br>(d) to family law services that provide alternatives to formal legal processes for families who are separated, separating or in dispute to improve their relationships and make arrangements in the best interests of their children;<br>(e) to family and relationship services to strengthen family relationships, prevent family breakdown and ensure the wellbeing and safety of children through the provision of broad‑based counselling and education to families of different forms and sizes;<br>(f) to develop and facilitate whole‑of‑community approaches to support and enhance early childhood development and wellbeing for children from birth to 12 years;<br>(g) to provide early intervention and prevention services and resources that are aimed at improving the development and wellbeing of children aged from birth to 12 years and to support the capacity of those in parenting roles;<br>(h) for community‑based interventions for vulnerable young people who are at risk of disengaging with family and community, including those at risk of homelessness;<br>(i) for specialist adult support services to improve outcomes and enhance wellbeing for people adversely affected by past institutional and child‑welfare practices and policies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) by providing medical services, family and maternity allowances, child endowment, unemployment and sickness benefits and benefits to students; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to children, in particular those under the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(d) in a Territory; or<br>(e) by providing assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(f) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(g) in relation to marriage; or<br>(h) in relation to divorce; or<br>(i) in connection with divorce—in relation to parental rights or the custody or guardianship of infants; or<br>(j) to assist persons who are insolvent or bankrupt to manage their insolvency or bankruptcy; or<br>(k) by providing grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(l) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(m) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>41</td>
<td>Transition to Independent Living Allowance</td>
<td>To support eligible young people exiting out‑of‑home care to meet some of the costs of moving from care to independent living and promote long‑term economic and social stability by providing one or more of the following:<br>(a) funding for goods and services:<br>(i) necessary to support the transition to independence in line with the goals outlined in a transition to independence plan (under which the exact use of payments is agreed upon by the young person concerned and his or her case worker); and<br>(ii) which may include funding for costs associated with securing stable accommodation or the purchase of essential household items;<br>(b) support to access education, training or transport.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) by providing family allowances, child endowment, unemployment benefits and benefits to students; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to children, in particular those under the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(c) in a Territory; or<br>(d) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>42</td>
<td>Settlement Services</td>
<td>To provide settlement support for humanitarian entrants and other eligible migrants in their first 5 years of life in Australia to become self‑reliant and participate equitably in Australian society and to minimise longer‑term reliance on Commonwealth provided social services by providing funding for the following:<br>(a) humanitarian settlement services that deliver early practical support (during the 6 to 12 months following arrival) to enable humanitarian entrants to become self‑reliant and participate equitably in Australian society;<br>(b) settlement services activities that deliver services to humanitarian entrants and other migrants in their first 5 year in Australia;<br>(c) support services to enable persons with complex needs to become self‑reliant and to participate equitably in Australian society;<br>(d) peak bodies involved in the settlement of persons who arrive in Australia;<br>(e) pre‑arrival orientation and information services to persons who have been granted humanitarian visas;<br>(f) free interpreting services for persons settling in Australia;<br>(g) the translation of settlement‑related documents;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(h) to:<br>(i) set and maintain national standards for translating and interpreting; and<br>(ii) support the ongoing development of credentialed translators and interpreters;<br>(i) to support Australian residents not fluent in English to access mainstream services;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(j) research and stakeholder engagement, including funding for national peak bodies and other stakeholder organisations.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) by engaging in measures in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(b) by providing unemployment benefits and benefits to students; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>43</td>
<td>Financial Wellbeing and Capability</td>
<td>To:<br>(a) improve the financial knowledge, skills and capabilities and financial resilience of vulnerable individuals and families; and<br>(b) in relation to problem gambling:<br>(i) alleviate the immediate impact of financial stress; and<br>(ii) progress initiatives and assist those at risk of homelessness;<br>by providing funding for the following:<br>(c) crisis support, financial capability‑building services, financial counselling and access to microfinance products;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(d) research and consultation, engagement activities and expert advice to inform the Commonwealth on issues relating to problem gambling.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing finding:<br>(a) by providing unemployment benefits; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to children, in particular those under the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(d) in a Territory; or<br>(e) by providing assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(f) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(g) to assist persons who are insolvent or bankrupt to manage their insolvency or bankruptcy; or<br>(h) by providing grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(i) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(j) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>44</td>
<td>Civil Society</td>
<td>To do the following:<br>(a) support charities and non‑government and not‑for‑profit organisations through education, training and fostering innovation to continue to focus on their work in the community;<br>(b) foster a culture of philanthropic giving, cross‑sector partnering, volunteering and corporate social responsibility;<br>(c) help build a strong civil society.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) by providing grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>45</td>
<td>Families and Communities Service Improvement</td>
<td>To support and encourage the continuous improvement of Commonwealth‑funded social services, by providing funding as follows:<br>(a) to support peak community organisations;<br>(b) for sponsorship activities, informed research and innovation, policy development, information sharing, new pilots and trials of service models and evaluations.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) by providing medical services, family and maternity allowances, child endowment, unemployment and sickness benefits and benefits to students, and by engaging in measures incidental to their provision; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(b) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>47</td>
<td>National Initiatives</td>
<td>To achieve positive outcomes for families, women and children by working across sectors to:<br>(a) improve the safety and wellbeing of children; and<br>(b) advance gender equality; and<br>(c) reduce violence against women and children; and<br>(d) support women affected by violence; and<br>(e) support trafficked people; and<br>(f) provide communication and information designed to change violence‑supportive attitudes and effectively reduce the incidence and impact of violence in Australia; and<br>(g) reducing child abuse and neglect; and<br>(h) support research and stakeholder organisations to assist in making the protection of children everyone’s responsibility.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) by providing medical services, family and maternity allowances, child endowment, unemployment and sickness benefits and benefits to students; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to women, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to children, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(d) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(e) by engaging in measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(f) in a Territory; or<br>(g) by providing assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(h) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(i) in relation to marriage; or<br>(j) in relation to divorce; or<br>(k) in connection with divorce—in relation to parental rights or the custody or guardianship of infants; or<br>(l) by providing grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(m) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(n) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>48</td>
<td>Housing and Homelessness Service Improvement and Sector Support</td>
<td>To fund:<br>(a) homelessness prevention initiatives to reduce the impact of homelessness; and<br>(b) activities that improve housing affordability; and</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(c) research and activities of peak bodies to do one or more of the following:<br>(i) build the research base for effective policy that addresses homelessness and housing affordability over the long term;<br>(ii) identify best practice models that can be promoted and replicated and that will enhance existing housing and homelessness policies and programs;<br>(iii) build the capacity of the community sector to improve linkages and networks;<br>(iv) raise awareness of housing, housing affordability and homelessness issues at all levels of government and across the community.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) by providing medical services, family and maternity allowances, child endowment, unemployment and sickness benefits and benefits to students, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those matters; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly article 11; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>49</td>
<td>Disability Employment</td>
<td>To help individuals with an injury, disability or health condition to secure and maintain sustainable open employment by:<br>(a) providing medical and dental services and unemployment, pharmaceutical, hospital and sickness benefits; and<br>(b) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>50</td>
<td>Employment Assistance and Other Services</td>
<td>To provide funding to:<br>(a) support employers to employ people with disabilities; and<br>(b) assist people with disabilities to resolve complaints relating to providers of disability services; and<br>(c) support a hotline for the reporting of abuse and neglect of people with disabilities;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly articles 4, 16 and 27.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>51</td>
<td>Disability and Carer Support</td>
<td>To improve access, support and services for people with disabilities and their carers as follows:<br>(a) by providing and improving access to services and support through stakeholder engagement and sector development;<br>(b) by providing services and support for carers, including services to support carers aged 25 and under;<br>(c) by providing support, services and funding to enable people with disabilities and carers to participate in forums;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(d) by providing support to develop a robust sector to meet the needs of people with disabilities and carers;<br>(e) by providing for the delivery of appropriate and timely advocacy for people with disabilities and carers that addresses instances of abuse, discrimination and neglect.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) by providing medical and dental services, family and maternity allowances, unemployment, pharmaceutical, hospital and sickness benefits and benefits to students; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to children, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(d) in a Territory; or<br>(e) by providing assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(f) by providing grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(h) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>52</td>
<td>Disability and Carer Service Improvement and Sector Support</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) research and stakeholder engagement; and<br>(b) peak bodies and other persons and entities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) by providing medical and dental services, family and maternity allowances, unemployment, pharmaceutical, hospital and sickness benefits and benefits to students, and engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those matters; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to children, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(d) in a Territory; or<br>(e) by providing assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(f) by providing grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(h) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(i) in connection with electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>53</td>
<td>Community Mental Health</td>
<td>To provide early intervention and other support through community‑based initiatives for people with mental illness and their families and carers, so that they can develop their capabilities, increase their wellbeing and actively participate in community and economic life, including by providing the following:<br>(a) assistance for people severely impacted by mental illness, including services with an employment focus for those who have employment as a primary goal;<br>(b) early intervention support to vulnerable families with children and young people who are showing early signs of, or are at risk of developing, mental illness;<br>(c) a range of flexible support options for carers and families of people with severe mental illness;<br>(d) funding and support to increase awareness and understanding of mental health issues;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(e) education and advocacy.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) by providing medical and dental services, family and maternity allowances, unemployment, pharmaceutical, hospital and sickness benefits and benefits to students; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to children, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(d) in a Territory; or<br>(e) by providing assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(f) by providing grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(h) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>54</td>
<td>NDIS Transitioning</td>
<td>To improve the wellbeing and social and economic participation of people with disabilities and their families and carers as follows:<br>(a) by building a National Disability Insurance Scheme;<br>(b) by providing a better start for children with disabilities and helping children with autism by providing them with early access to early intervention services;<br>(c) by providing supported employment services to enable people with disabilities to participate fully in employment;<br>(d) by providing outside school hours care for teenagers with disabilities;<br>(e) by providing immediate and short‑term respite support for carers of young people with severe or profound disabilities whose needs are not being met through existing government initiatives;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(f) by providing young carers respite and information services to assist young carers who need support to complete their secondary education or vocational equivalent due to the demands of their caring role.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) by providing medical and dental services and pharmaceutical, hospital and sickness benefits; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>55</td>
<td>Stronger Relationships Programme</td>
<td>To provide education and counselling to couples who are:<br>(a) married, or engaged or intending to be married; or<br>(b) in a de facto relationship; or<br>(c) in a same‑sex relationship;<br>relating to their relationship, including education and counselling relating to any of the following:<br>(d) conflict resolution;<br>(e) parenting;<br>(f) financial management.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>56</td>
<td>Young Carer Bursary Programme</td>
<td>To provide benefits to students through the payment of bursaries to caregivers who are aged 25 and under, and who are currently enrolled in secondary school or in tertiary education.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>57</td>
<td>Primary Health Networks</td>
<td>To provide support for the establishment of organisations (to be known as Primary Health Networks) that will work to integrate the care of patients across the health system and improve health outcomes for communities where that support is incidental to the Commonwealth’s provision of sickness and hospital benefits and medical services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>58</td>
<td>Good Sports Programme</td>
