<td>To provide support to the Australian Drug Foundation to work with sporting codes, organisations and clubs to provide activities to change behaviours and attitudes around alcohol consumption where the activities:<br>(a) are incidental to the Commonwealth’s provision of pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits and medical services; or<br>(b) are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>59</td>
<td>Water Safety</td>
<td>To provide support for activities to reduce incidences of drowning and promote water safety, including activities that:<br>(a) are carried out by a trading or foreign corporation to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies; or<br>(b) are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>60</td>
<td>Ensuring the Supply of Antivenoms, Q fever vaccine and Pandemic Influenza vaccines</td>
<td>To provide support for activities to ensure the regular, ongoing availability of Q fever vaccine, antivenoms and pandemic influenza vaccines where those activities are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>61</td>
<td>Community Development Grants Programme</td>
<td>To provide grants for regional and community infrastructure projects.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(b) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) to or in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to commemorate Australians killed or injured in war, and support veterans and defence force members and their families and communities; or<br>(e) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(f) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(g) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under international agreements; or<br>(h) to provide medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, benefits to students, and measures incidental to the provision of those matters; or<br>(i) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(j) to provide assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(k) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(l) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>62</td>
<td>National Stronger Regions Fund</td>
<td>To provide grants to support the construction, expansion and enhancement of infrastructure across regional Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(b) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) to or in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to commemorate Australians killed or injured in war, and support veterans and defence force members and their families and communities; or<br>(e) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(f) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(g) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under international agreements; or<br>(h) to provide medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, benefits to students, and measures incidental to the provision of those matters; or<br>(i) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(j) to provide assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(k) for the construction or extension of railways in any State with the consent of that State; or<br>(l) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(m) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>63</td>
<td>Australian Government Innovation and Investment Fund</td>
<td>To establish and fund a scheme to encourage new sustainable economic growth and jobs in Tasmania by providing regulated assistance to trading, financial or foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the activities of the corporations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>64</td>
<td>Industry Growth Centres Initiative</td>
<td>To support, and to establish, Industry Growth Centres to facilitate nationally significant research, collaboration, sharing of knowledge, development and deployment of technology, and projects for the benefit of the nation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding and support:<br>(a) for the promotion or development of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>65</td>
<td>Stronger Biosecurity and Quarantine programme—grants to external parties to conduct biosecurity response and preparedness activities</td>
<td>To provide funding to respond to biosecurity threats, including by doing the following:<br>(a) employing personnel and equipping them to carry out biosecurity functions;<br>(b) adopting measures to prepare for biosecurity threats;<br>(c) building capacity to respond to biosecurity threats.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) in connection with quarantine; or<br>(b) that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>66</td>
<td>Improved Access to Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals Programme</td>
<td>To support and encourage uses of agricultural and veterinary chemicals consistent with the National Registration Scheme for Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals (NRS), and to support international initiatives for improving information about and access to agricultural and veterinary chemicals.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) supporting and encouraging uses of agricultural and veterinary chemicals consistent with the Commonwealth registration scheme for agricultural and veterinary chemicals, being a scheme based on laws made for the Australian Capital Territory; or<br>(b) implementing or giving effect to the agreements referred to in section 9A of the <i>Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals (Administration) Act 1992</i>; or<br>(c) providing funding or support for the fostering or promotion of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(d) providing funding for activities relating to aliens; or<br>(e) providing funding or support in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>67</td>
<td>National Assessment Reform</td>
<td>To deliver the National Assessment Program online, including the National Assessment Program—Literacy and Numeracy (NAPLAN) test and other assessments of sample populations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>68</td>
<td>Australian Small Business Advisory Services programme</td>
<td>To support small business advisers in providing advisory services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing regulated assistance to small business advisers that are trading, financial or foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporation; or<br>(b) providing assistance to small business advisers in relation to a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>69</td>
<td>Community Assistance Support—Transitional Support</td>
<td>1. To manage unlawful non‑citizens and holders of bridging visas in the community to an immigration outcome through early intervention and provision of needs‑based support and assistance.<br>2. To support holders of substantive visas to transition into the community through the provision of needs‑based support and assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>70</td>
<td>Tasmanian Jobs and Growth Package</td>
<td>To provide grants for projects that support economic growth and jobs in Tasmania.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) as financial assistance to Tasmania; or<br>(b) to or in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(d) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under international agreements; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(e) to provide medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, benefits to students, and measures incidental to the provision of those matters; or<br>(f) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(g) to provide assistance to trading, financial and foreign corporations to which paragraph 51(xx) of the Constitution applies where the assistance relates to the existing activities of the corporations; or<br>(h) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(i) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>71</td>
<td>Global Infrastructure Hub</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Global Infrastructure Hub as a result of agreements reached by the Commonwealth Government with the members of the Group of 20 (G20) forum and with the objectives of:<br>(a) developing a knowledge‑sharing platform and network between governments, the private sector, development banks and other international organisations; and<br>(b) fostering collaboration among these groups to improve the functioning and financing of infrastructure markets.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>72</td>
<td>Training for Employment Scholarships Pilot Programme</td>
<td>To support employers to provide training to new employees.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for training to students and the unemployed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>73</td>
<td>Youth Employment Pathways Pilot Programme</td>
<td>To support community service organisations to provide training and other assistance to unemployed youth to assist them to find employment or undertake further education or training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>74</td>
<td>Sector Development Fund</td>
<td>To provide support for activities:<br>(a) to assist the disability sector (including people with disability, their families, carers and service providers) in transitioning to the National Disability Insurance Scheme; or<br>(b) to assist those in the disability sector (including people with disability, their families, carers and service providers) who are unable to transition to the National Disability Insurance Scheme.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(b) by providing medical services, sickness benefits and hospital benefits, and by engaging in measures incidental to their provision; or<br>(c) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>75</td>
<td>Mathematics by Inquiry</td>
<td>To create and improve mathematics curriculum resources for primary and secondary school students:<br>(a) to meet Australia’s international obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights; and<br>(b) as activities that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>76</td>
<td>Coding across the Curriculum</td>
<td>To encourage the introduction of computer coding and programming across different year levels in Australian schools:<br>(a) to meet Australia’s international obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights; and<br>(b) as an activity that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>77</td>
<td>Piloting a P‑TECH Styled Education Facility</td>
<td>To support the piloting of an Australian education facility modelled on the “Pathways in Technology Early College High School” (P‑TECH) in the United States of America, by:<br>(a) providing benefits to students and engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits; and<br>(b) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights and the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy and Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>78</td>
<td>Summer Schools for STEM</td>
<td>To support the attendance of female, disadvantaged or marginalised school students, including Indigenous students and students living in regional or remote areas, at national science and mathematics summer schools, with the aim of increasing the participation of these students in the learning areas of science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), by:<br>(a) providing benefits to students and engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits; and<br>(b) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>80</td>
<td>Duke of Edinburgh’s International Award—Australia</td>
<td>To provide support for the Duke of Edinburgh’s International Award—Australia, to the extent that providing such support:<br>(a) increases access to, and representation in, the Award nationally:<br>(i) for people under 18 who are disadvantaged, or who have a mental or physical disability, so as to contribute to their development and enjoyment of a full and decent life; or<br>(ii) for young people of 18 or over who have a mental or physical disability, so as to contribute to their independence, ability and inclusion in all aspects of life; and<br>(b) would assist Australia to meet its obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4, 6(2) and 23(1)); or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (particularly Article 26(1)).<br>Note: The Duke of Edinburgh’s International Award—Australia encourages young people to volunteer their time in their communities, participate in sport and recreation activities, develop their teamwork and leadership competence, and develop their personal interests and social skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>81</td>
<td>Grants in Aid Sub‑Programme</td>
<td>To support organisations, including key national educational research and representative organisations, to carry out the following activities in relation to education and schooling:<br>(a) to conduct research, and gather community and industry views, for the purpose of informing the Commonwealth;<br>(b) to develop and maintain websites, and otherwise send and receive information through the use of online communication services;<br>(c) to conduct and disseminate the results of research, to the extent that these activities are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.;<br>(d) to conduct research and undertake pilot programs, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 2, 4, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>82</td>
<td>Australian Research Alliance for Children and Youth Limited</td>
<td>To support the Australian Research Alliance for Children and Youth Limited to carry out the following activities in relation to parent engagement and child and youth wellbeing:<br>(a) to conduct research for the purpose of informing the Commonwealth;<br>(b) to develop and maintain websites, and otherwise send and receive information through the use of online communication services;<br>(c) to disseminate information about Commonwealth research, policies and programmes relating to Indigenous parents, children and youth;<br>(d) to conduct and disseminate the results of research, to the extent that these activities are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>83</td>
<td>Financial Wellbeing and Capability—Commonwealth Financial Counselling and Financial Capability—Capability Building</td>
<td>1. To provide funding for an entity to:<br>(a) develop and provide online information and resources for financial counsellors, financial capability workers and consumers; and<br>(b) provide the national 1800 financial counselling and financial capability Helpline telephone service (the <b><i>Helpline</b></i>), including the development of national standards and materials for the Helpline.<br>2. To provide funding for services to be provided by an entity directed at supporting:<br>(a) attendance at national financial counselling and financial capability conferences by the following:<br>(i) financial counsellors and financial capability workers for the Helpline;<br>(ii) residents of a Territory; and<br>(b) the presentation of sessions at national financial counselling and financial capability conferences that relate to any of the following:<br>(i) bankruptcy or insolvency;<br>(ii) invalid or old‑age pensions within the meaning of paragraph 51 (xxiii) of the Constitution;<br>(iii) allowances, pensions, endowments, benefits or services to which paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution applies;<br>(iv) immigrants or aliens;<br>(v) the Helpline;<br>(vi) online information or resources relevant to financial counselling or financial capability;<br>(vii) particular issues confronting the residents of Territories.<br>3. To provide funding for services to be provided by an entity directed at supporting the presentation of sessions at national financial counselling and financial capability conferences, to the extent that the presentation amounts to a measure designed to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child; or<br>(b) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(c) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women; or<br>(d) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.<br>4. To provide funding for services to be provided by an entity directed at supporting the following:<br>(a) attendance at national financial counselling and financial capability conferences by the following:<br>(i) Indigenous persons;<br>(ii) persons who provide financial counselling and financial capability services predominantly to Indigenous persons;<br>(b) the presentation of sessions at national financial counselling and financial capability conferences that relate to particular issues confronting Indigenous persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>85</td>
<td>Australian Apprenticeship Support Network</td>
<td>To support the Commonwealth’s employment and vocational education and training policies by providing support to apprentices, and in relation to connecting with, undertaking, and completing apprenticeships, to the extent that:<br>(a) the support is the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students; or<br>(b) the provision of the support will give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, the Human Resources Development Convention, and the Employment Policy Convention.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>86</td>
<td>Infrastructure investment</td>
<td>To facilitate the construction of infrastructure by providing funds for the making of loans:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) for the construction or extension of railways in any State with the consent of that State; or<br>(d) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(e) to the extent that the construction, or the making of the loan, is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>87</td>
<td>Justice Services—Community Legal Services Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to organisations to:<br>(a) provide legal information and legal assistance services (including legal advice and legal representation):<br>(i) to persons in relation to matters in the federal jurisdiction or in relation to Commonwealth laws; or<br>(ii) specifically targeted to assist Indigenous Australians; or<br>(iii) to persons in a Territory; or<br>(b) provide legal assistance services and deliver and receive mental health training through the use of telephone and online communication services; or<br>(c) provide for communication between legal assistance organisations; or<br>(d) collect data, conduct research, and provide advice for the purpose of informing the Commonwealth in relation to legal services; or<br>(da) provide legal assistance services to individuals in relation to disputes with insurers, other than disputes in relation to State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) evaluate or improve the matters referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d) or (da) above.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities:<br>(a) incidental to the legislative powers vested in the Commonwealth; or<br>(b) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(c) with respect to telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(d) with respect to statistics; or<br>(e) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(ea) with respect to insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); or<br>(f) with respect to a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>88</td>
<td>Arts and Cultural Development—National Programme for Excellence in the Arts</td>
<td>To allocate funding for the arts on a national basis through the following types of grants:<br>(a) endowment incentive grants that assist organisations to undertake projects through partnerships and collaborations or to support capital projects;<br>(b) grants that support international touring, exchanges and cultural diplomacy, with a focus on significant initiatives with demonstrable benefits for Australia;<br>(c) strategic grants that support projects by arts organisations;<br>(d) grants that support arts festivals in metropolitan or regional areas;<br>(e) grants that support touring of exhibitions to or from regional or remote Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(c) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(d) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>89</td>
<td>Arts and Cultural Development—Matched Funding Programme</td>
<td>To encourage private sector support for the arts by supporting projects that develop the arts sector’s capacity to use innovative funding strategies and build partnerships with the corporate and philanthropic sectors.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>91</td>
<td>Digital Technologies and Communications Services: Spatial Data</td>
<td>To provide open and free public access to national geocoded address data.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support to engage in measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>92</td>
<td>Stronger Communities Programme</td>
<td>To provide grants for community projects to strengthen and benefit local communities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(c) to or in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to commemorate Australians killed or injured in war, and support veterans and defence force members and their families and communities; or<br>(e) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(f) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under international agreements; or<br>(g) to provide medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits and benefits to students, and for measures incidental to the provision of those matters; or<br>(h) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(i) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(j) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>93</td>
<td>Drought Communities Programme</td>
<td>To provide grants:<br>(a) to support, and to enable support for, drought‑affected communities, particularly to address unemployment caused by drought; and<br>(b) to support and enhance the viability and competitiveness of drought‑affected agriculture;<br>including by providing grants for local infrastructure projects.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(c) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) to commemorate Australians killed or injured in war, and support veterans and defence force members and their families and communities; or<br>(e) for the construction or extension of railways in any State with the consent of that State; or<br>(f) to or in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(g) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under international agreements, including the following:<br>(i) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 4, 5, and 10;<br>(ii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4;<br>(iii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iv) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 7 and 8;<br>(v) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 11 and 12;<br>(vi) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(h) to provide medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits and benefits to students, and for measures incidental to the provision of those matters; or<br>(i) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(j) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(k) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>94</td>
<td>General Practice Rural Incentives Programme</td>
<td>To encourage medical practitioners (including general practitioners, general practice registrars and specialists) to practise in regional and remote areas:<br>(a) for the purpose of providing medical services; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>95</td>
<td>Haemopoietic Progenitor Cells Programme</td>
<td>To support the location and procurement of haemopoietic progenitor cells from overseas for Australian patients as the provision of sickness benefits and medical services, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits and services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>96</td>
<td>Improve Safety and Quality in Health Care Programme</td>
<td>To establish and maintain clinical quality registries to assess and improve the quality of health care:<br>(a) as the provision of medical services, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those services; or<br>(b) by collecting, analysing, disseminating and using statistics; or<br>(c) to meet Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>97</td>
<td>Junior Medical Officer Programme</td>
<td>To support clinical training positions for junior medical practitioners, prior to the commencement of specialist training, as the provision of benefits to students, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>98</td>
<td>National Bowel Cancer Screening Programme</td>
<td>To support the prevention and early detection of bowel cancer, and reduce morbidity and mortality from the disease:<br>(a) as the provision of medical services, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those services; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights; or<br>(c) by engaging in scientific research for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>99</td>
<td>Improving Immunisation Coverage Rates</td>
<td>To improve the uptake of vaccines under the National Immunisation Programme, including through the collection of data, the provision of financial incentives to immunisation providers, and communication activities relevant to that Programme, as the provision of pharmaceutical benefits and medical services, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits and services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>100</td>
<td>Health Workforce Scholarship Programme</td>
<td>To increase participation in, and promote better distribution of, health workforces by providing, and supporting the provision of:<br>(a) scholarships to health students, to the extent that the scholarships are benefits to students; or<br>(b) scholarships to health students who are Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>101</td>
<td>National Cancer Screening Register</td>
<td>To establish, maintain and publicise a national register of cancer screening data that will inform clinical decisions across current and future cancer screening programmes:<br>(a) as the provision of medical services, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those services; or<br>(b) by collecting, analysing, disseminating and using statistics; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(d) to meet Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>102</td>
<td>Organ and Tissue Donation for Transplantation</td>
<td>To fund measures to improve organ and tissue donation rates and access to organ and tissue transplantation services:<br>(a) as the provision of sickness benefits, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(c) to meet Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>103</td>
<td>Professional pharmacy programmes and services under the Community Pharmacy Agreement</td>
<td>To support access to, and the quality use of, Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme medicines, and the delivery and development of professional services that will improve health outcomes, by providing funding and allowances to community pharmacies:<br>(a) as the provision of pharmaceutical and sickness benefits and medical services, and by engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits and services; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(b) to benefit Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(c) to meet Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>105</td>
<td>Health Peak and Advisory Bodies Programme</td>
<td>To provide funding to health peak and advisory bodies for such a body to carry out one or more of the following activities:<br>(a) to disseminate information and raise awareness about the following matters relating to the body’s sector:<br>(i) Commonwealth policies and programmes;<br>(ii) medical services;<br>(b) to disseminate information and raise awareness about the following matters relating to the body’s sector, to the extent that these activities would assist Australia to meet its obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights:<br>(i) health services that are provided to persons in the event of sickness;<br>(ii) the prevention, treatment and control of diseases;<br>(c) to develop and publish information, and raise awareness, about matters relating to the body’s sector, by means of electronic communications;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(d) to conduct inquiries, investigations and consultations in relation to:<br>(i) matters affecting public health; and<br>(ii) diseases and the provision of health services, to the extent that these activities would assist Australia to meet its obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights;<br>(e) to collect, compile, analyse and disseminate statistics about matters relating to the body’s sector;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(f) to provide telephone information services;<br>(g) to provide education and training to medical practitioners working in the body’s sector (including general practitioners, nurses and allied health professionals), to the extent that the education and training:<br>(i) is directed at improving the quality of medical services; or<br>(ii) would assist Australia to meet its obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>106</td>
<td>Parent Engagement Campaign</td>
<td>To deliver a communication campaign:<br>(a) to raise awareness of the importance of parent engagement in children’s education, and the significant benefits that this brings; and<br>(b) to inform parents about, and assist parents with, different ways of engaging in their child’s education.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to delivering a communication campaign:<br>(a) using postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(b) for the collection, compilation, analysis and dissemination of statistics and related information; or<br>(c) in connection with assisting Australia to meet its obligations under international agreements, including the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights; or<br>(d) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>107A</td>
<td>Closure of Hunter River and Port Stephens Fisheries—Assistance to Individuals and Businesses</td>
<td>To provide targeted assistance, to eligible fishers and businesses affected by the closure of Hunter River and Port Stephens fisheries in response to contamination attributed to activities at RAAF Base Williamtown, to manage adjustment pressures and remain viable in the long term.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>110</td>
<td>Support for the Child Care System—Child Care Services Support—Community Child Care Fund</td>
<td>To:<br>(a) support approved and transitioning child care services to implement innovative solutions to ensure their viability; and<br>(b) improve access to child care for disadvantaged children;<br>to meet Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>111</td>
<td>Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education</td>
<td>To support:<br>(a) the delivery of the Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education online and, for eligible persons with a disability, the delivery of the test through non‑online means; and<br>(b) the administration of the test.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 24.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>113</td>
<td>Managing established pest animals and weeds</td>
<td>To support the management and control of pest animals and weeds to assist in meeting Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (particularly Article 8(h)) by:<br>(a) providing financial assistance to organisations to develop and promote new and improved technologies and tools for controlling pest animals and weeds; and<br>(b) developing national consultative and collaborative arrangements for government, community and industry action on pest animals and weeds.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>115</td>
<td>International Geography Olympiads</td>
<td>To fund, as part of Australia’s participation in the International Geography Olympiads, student participation in the international event, including:<br>(a) organising, promoting and managing the national selection event, Geography’s Big Week Out; and<br>(b) meeting student costs for attendance at, and participation in, the events.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities that:<br>(a) are in connection with Australia’s participation in an international event (including where such events are held at locations external to Australia); or<br>(b) are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) are the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>116</td>
<td>World Schools Debating Championships</td>
<td>To fund:<br>(a) as part of Australia’s participation in the World Schools Debating Championships, student participation in the international event, including:<br>(i) organising and managing selection and participation of students; and<br>(ii) meeting student costs for attendance and participation; and<br>(b) student participation at the National Schools Debating Championships, including meeting student costs for attendance and participation; and<br>(c) the provision of teaching, coaching and development programs to foster an understanding of debating techniques for schools and students.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution; or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligation under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 29; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>117</td>
<td>Educating Against Domestic Violence</td>
<td>To support Australia‑wide education of school students from Foundation to Year 12 on respectful relationships countering domestic violence, through:<br>(a) the development of curriculum and teaching resources for delivery online; and<br>(b) the development of a mobile application for the delivery of curriculum and teaching resources online; and<br>(c) the delivery of curriculum and teaching resources online via a website and mobile application.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities:<br>(a) in connection with online communications; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s international obligations in relation to women (particularly Articles 2, 5 and 16 of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>118</td>
<td>Safe Technology for Women</td>
<td>To enable women experiencing, or at risk of, domestic or family violence to keep safe by providing access to new smart phones and safe technology information, as a measure:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Articles 2, 5 and 16); or<br>(b) involving electronic communications; or<br>(c) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>119</td>
<td>Keeping Women Safe in Their Homes</td>
<td>To provide assistance to enable States, Territories, organisations and other entities to conduct risk assessments and improve or upgrade the security of the homes of women experiencing, or at risk of, domestic or family violence, as measures:<br>(a) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Articles 2, 5 and 16); or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 3 and 19); or<br>(c) providing services in a Territory; or<br>(d) involving electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>120</td>
<td>Funding for MensLine Australia</td>
<td>To deliver support, resources and counselling for men with family and relationship concerns (including via telephone, videoconferencing and other online media), as measures:<br>(a) involving electronic communications; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>121</td>
<td>Better Responses from Frontline Staff</td>
<td>To deliver training to enable frontline personnel (including police, medical personnel, and social and community workers) to provide better responses to women experiencing, or at risk of, domestic or family violence, as a measure:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16); or<br>(b) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>122</td>
<td>Local Support Coordinators</td>
<td>To fund local support coordinators to coordinate support (including housing, safety and budgeting services) for women experiencing, or at risk of, domestic or family violence, as a measure:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Article 3); or<br>(b) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>123</td>
<td>jobactive</td>
<td>To help job seekers find and keep a job, and to move from welfare to work, by:<br>(a) providing employment and related services which assist job seekers to find and keep a job with suitable employers; and<br>(b) providing Work for the Dole activities in not‑for‑profit and government organisations to help prepare job seekers for the work environment;<br>as measures:<br>(c) providing allowances, benefits, endowments and services of the kind described in paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution; or<br>(d) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(e) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(f) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(g) meeting Australia’s international obligations in relation to persons with disabilities, in particular obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; or<br>(h) providing benefits or services to Indigenous persons, families, entities or communities; or<br>(i) providing benefits or services to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(j) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>124</td>
<td>Labour Market Support Stream</td>
<td>To provide additional services to retrenched workers and job seekers to help them to find and keep employment, as measures:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(e) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>125</td>
<td>National Wage Subsidy Pool</td>
<td>To provide for a programme of wage subsidies and other incentives to employers who employ unemployed persons (including mature age and young job seekers, long‑term unemployed persons, Indigenous job seekers and parents seeking to rejoin the workforce), as measures:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(e) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>126</td>
<td>National Work Experience Programme</td>
<td>To provide for a programme of unpaid work experience in order to provide stronger incentives for employers to offer work experience and employment opportunities to job seekers, as measures:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(e) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>127</td>
<td>New Enterprise Incentive Scheme</td>
<td>To provide persons with small business training, mentoring and assistance to help create a financially viable business and to become self‑employed business owners.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or that are incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 6 and 13(2)(b); or<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Employment Policy Convention, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Human Resources Development Convention, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4; or<br>(c) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>128</td>
<td>Harvest Trail Services and Harvest Trail Information Service</td>
<td>To provide unemployed persons and other eligible individuals with information and support to undertake work that meets the requirements of employers in the agricultural industry:<br>(a) during periods of peak labour demand; or<br>(b) during labour shortages resulting from the coronavirus known as COVID‑19.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) involving the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Article 1;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning the Organisation of the Employment Service, particularly Article 1;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>129</td>
<td>Corporate Champions</td>
<td>To provide assistance to employers to move towards better practices in relation to employing mature age job seekers, as a measure:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(e) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>130</td>
<td>Engaging Early School Leavers</td>
<td>To encourage early school leavers to actively seek employment if they are not participating in full‑time education or to participate in a combination of education, part‑time work and other approved activities, as measures:<br>(a) providing benefits to students; or<br>(b) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(c) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(d) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(e) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(f) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>131</td>
<td>Intensive Support—Transition to Work</td>
<td>To provide assistance to young people who have disengaged from education and are at risk of becoming long‑term unemployed by providing intensive early intervention to prepare them for work, as a measure:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(e) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>132</td>
<td>Empowering YOUth Initiatives</td>
<td>To provide innovative localised solutions that support at‑risk young people to find a job, as a measure:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(e) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>133</td>
<td>Automotive Industry Structural Adjustment Programme</td>
<td>To provide assistance to workers in the automotive manufacturing industry (including component manufacturers and suppliers) who have been made redundant, as a measure:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(e) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>134</td>
<td>Forestry Industry in Tasmania Structural Adjustment Programme</td>
<td>To provide assistance to workers in the forestry industry in Tasmania who have been made redundant, as a measure:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(c) providing a free public employment service; or<br>(d) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>135</td>
<td>Beacon Foundation Real Futures Generation Programme</td>
<td>To provide assistance to the Beacon Foundation for its Real Futures Generation programme, as a measure:<br>(a) promoting full, productive and freely chosen employment; or<br>(b) providing technical and vocational guidance and training programmes to enable persons to realise the right to work; or<br>(c) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>136</td>
<td>Development of vocational education and training (VET) packages</td>
<td>To fund organisations:<br>(a) to develop nationally endorsed training packages to guide training and assessment in the VET sector in Australia; and<br>(b) to develop resources and products for use by VET providers to ensure the effective implementation of those training packages; and<br>(c) to promote the uptake of those training packages and the use of those resources and products.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for the purpose of meeting Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Article 1;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4; or<br>(b) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>137</td>
<td>WorldSkills Australia</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to WorldSkills Australia to promote skill‑based career pathways by:<br>(a) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources; and<br>(b) promoting and conducting a national skills competition, to the extent that these activities are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; and<br>(c) conducting research for the purpose of informing the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>139</td>
<td>ParentsNext</td>
<td>To provide assistance to parents who are not employed, or who are substantially underemployed, to do the following:<br>(a) develop an employment plan that will facilitate their obtaining sustainable employment;<br>(b) take the steps set out in the employment plan.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or that are incidental to the provision of, family allowances, child endowment, unemployment benefits, benefits to students, hospital and sickness benefits, and medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 12;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 18 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>140</td>
<td>Dementia and Aged Care Services Fund</td>
<td>To do the following:<br>(a) enable older people with dementia, or who are at risk of dementia, to access appropriate aged care services;<br>(b) enable older people with diverse social and cultural needs who are sick to access appropriate aged care services;<br>(c) provide aged care services that are specifically targeted to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People;<br>(d) strengthen the capacity of the health and aged care sectors to provide services to older people with dementia, or who are at risk of dementia, including people experiencing behavioural and psychological symptoms that are extreme or very severe;<br>(e) provide support for the health and aged care sectors using online or other technology platforms;<br>(f) support reform, including by way of structural change, in the aged care sector so that medical services are available to older people who:<br>(i) are sick; or<br>(ii) are experiencing or living with a medical condition;<br>(g) undertake activities for the purpose of the Commonwealth informing itself about aged care or matters relating to aged care.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, medical and dental services and family allowances; or<br>(b) providing assistance to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(c) providing assistance or undertaking activities using postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(d) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s international obligations, including under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 25, 26 and 28;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 12; or<br>(e) undertaking activities in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>142</td>
<td>Funding for quantum computing research</td>
<td>To fund world‑leading quantum computing research to develop a silicon quantum integrated circuit.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to funding measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>143</td>
<td>Global Innovation Strategy</td>
<td>To support science, technology and innovation collaboration between Australian businesses and researchers and their international counterparts.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) for the fostering or promotion of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(c) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>144</td>
<td>Expanding Opportunities for Women in STEM</td>
<td>To provide funding for the following:<br>(a) measures that promote the free choice of profession and employment by encouraging and supporting girls and women to pursue a career in the fields of science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), including by providing vocational guidance;<br>(b) measures that teach women how to start a business;<br>(c) measures that provide vocational training to women;<br>(d) measures that assist employers to eliminate discrimination against women;<br>(e) the development and implementation of gender equity accreditation processes;<br>(f) the evaluation of any of the above measures;<br>to the extent that these activities would assist Australia to meet its obligations under the following:<br>(g) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 4,10, 11 and 24;<br>(h) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4;<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>145</td>
<td>Prime Minister’s Prizes</td>
<td>To provide national prizes and awards to individuals and institutions, recognising achievement in science and innovation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) to provide benefits to students; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>146</td>
<td>Science and Mathematics Olympiads</td>
<td>To support the selection of students to represent Australia at international events, through funding for the Science and Mathematics Olympiads.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>148</td>
<td>International Science Competitions</td>
<td>To provide funding for individual young Australians to participate in, and represent Australia at, international science competitions.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(b) by engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>149</td>
<td>STEM Community Engagement</td>
<td>To provide funding for the following:<br>(a) an annual National Youth Science Forum;<br>(b) science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) events for primary and secondary school students;<br>(c) scholarships that enable students to attend STEM events.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Article 29; or<br>(b) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(c) to provide benefits to students; or<br>(d) to engage in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>150</td>
<td>Early Learning STEM Australia</td>
<td>To fund measures that are aimed at engaging children in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) in the preschool and primary school years, including:<br>(a) developing and delivering online content, through the use of telecommunication services, for STEM education to preschool and primary school students; and<br>(b) providing training to early childhood educators and primary school teachers;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(c) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(d) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>151</td>
<td>Inspiring school students and youth to engage in STEM‑related activities</td>
<td>To fund initiatives that are aimed at engaging school students and youth in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), including:<br>(a) building partnerships between STEM industries and schools; and<br>(b) specialist information technology teachers providing training and classroom support to teachers in disadvantaged schools.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities that are engaged in to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(a) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Article 3;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Article 1;<br>(c) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 28 and 29;<br>(d) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>152</td>
<td>Tackling the digital divide</td>
<td>To improve digital literacy in schools by funding the following initiatives:<br>(a) a national competition of coding challenges and related activities;<br>(b) support for teachers to implement the Australian Curriculum: Digital Technologies through the use of online communication services;<br>(c) developing online content for computer coding education for school students;<br>(d) support for school students, particularly in disadvantaged areas, to attend information and communications technology summer schools;<br>(e) support for school leaders to promote digital literacy in schools, including by partnering with other schools.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities that:<br>(a) are in connection with online communications; or<br>(b) are the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students; or<br>(c) are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) are engaged in to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>153</td>
<td>Continuity of Support—Block‑funded Activities</td>
<td>To provide continuity of disability support services for older people who are receiving State or Territory administered disability services and are ineligible for the National Disability Insurance Scheme, as a measure directed to meeting Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>154</td>
<td>Continuity of Support—Individual Support Packages</td>
<td>To fund the provision of disability support packages for individual older people who are receiving State or Territory administered disability services and are ineligible for the National Disability Insurance Scheme, as a measure directed to:<br>(a) meeting Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; and<br>(b) the provision of sickness benefits and medical services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>155</td>
<td>Farm Co‑operatives and Collaboration Pilot Program</td>
<td>To provide training and support to farmers and farmers’ advisers, and financial assistance to farmers, to assist farmers to identify and make use of opportunities to network, collaborate and identify alternative business approaches, for accessing new supply chains.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing, or funding, support for:<br>(a) the fostering or promotion of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) businesses involved in interstate or overseas trade and commerce.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>159</td>
<td>National Science Week and strategic science communication activities</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) activities that are part of National Science Week; and<br>(b) activities that enhance the community’s understanding of, and interest in, science, technology, engineering or mathematics (STEM), including:<br>(i) measures that will support science tourism; and<br>(ii) measures that will assist in educating people under 18 years of age and assist them to reach their fullest potential by stimulating their interest in, and understanding of, STEM; and<br>(iii) citizen science projects; and<br>(iv) the development of quality assurance standards for a citizen science project and documents that provide guidance on how to undertake a citizen science project; and<br>(v) one or more national prizes that celebrate excellence in science; and<br>(vi) the development of software applications for smart phones and tablets; and<br>(vii) activities that will enhance the scientific literacy of individuals who are leaders in the Australian community; and<br>(viii) the development and delivery of national outreach programs delivered by or on behalf of the Commonwealth, acting through Questacon, that focus on delivering educational activities in the fields of STEM.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for the fostering or promotion of interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) for measures that involve the use of telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(c) for measures that involve the making or recording of astronomical and meteorological observations; or<br>(d) for the collection, analysis, dissemination or use of statistics; or<br>(e) for the provision of assistance to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(f) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Article 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 6 and 15;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 7, 12 and 13;<br>(v) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4 and 6;<br>(vi) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Article 4;<br>(vii) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 5, 17 and 19; or<br>(g) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(h) by way of grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(i) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(j) for activities done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(k) for measures engaged in that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of a nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>160</td>
<td>Citizen Science Projects</td>
<td>To provide funding for citizen science projects.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for measures involving the use of telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(b) for measures that involve the making or recording of astronomical and meteorological observations; or<br>(c) for the collection, analysis, dissemination or use of statistics; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Article 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 15;<br>(iii) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 7, 12 and 13;<br>(iv) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4 and 6;<br>(v) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Article 4;<br>(vi) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 5, 17 and 19; or<br>(e) in relation to places, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(f) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>161</td>
<td>Maker Projects</td>
<td>To provide funding for measures that will assist people to engage in Maker Projects, being the design, creation or development of technological products.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Article 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 15; or<br>(b) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>162</td>
<td>Biomedical Translation Fund</td>
<td>To invest in promising biomedical discoveries and assist in their commercialisation, and to encourage the development of companies that are commercialising biomedical research and development, as measures:<br>(a) with respect to the provision of medical and dental services; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>163</td>
<td>Commonwealth Home Support Programme</td>
<td>To support frail older people who are living in the community to stay in their homes and to maximise their independence by:<br>(a) providing entry level support services to assist them to live independently at home and in the community; and<br>(b) providing them with respite care to support their relationships with their carers; and<br>(c) assisting those who are homeless, or at risk of homelessness, to access appropriate and sustainable housing, as well as community care and other support services; and<br>(d) supporting the development of the community aged care service system in a way that meets the aims of the programme and the aged care system more broadly; and<br>(e) providing a standardised assessment process that encompasses a holistic view of the needs of people seeking to access services under the programme, and conducting assessments of those people.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing sickness benefits and medical services, and engaging in measures incidental to the provision of those benefits and services; or<br>(b) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s obligations under international agreements, including the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 11; or<br>(c) undertaking activities in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>164</td>
<td>Countering Violent Extremism</td>
<td>To reduce the risk of home‑grown terrorism by acting domestically and internationally to strengthen Australia’s resilience to violent extremism, assist individuals to disengage from violent extremist influences, and address the impacts of violent extremism, including by:<br>(a) undertaking research and evaluating activities; and<br>(b) gathering and analysing information; and<br>(c) developing and disseminating information and resources; and<br>(d) developing and delivering training and capacity building initiatives; and<br>(e) developing and delivering intervention and diversion programs; and<br>(f) developing and providing information, assistance, advice, support and services to individuals, families, organisations and communities; and<br>(g) responding to and disrupting extremist propaganda and ideologies.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing grants of financial assistance to States and Territories; or<br>(b) measures for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and of the States; or<br>(c) measures utilising, or in respect of, telegraphic, telephonic or other like services; or<br>(d) measures in relation to aliens and immigrants; or<br>(e) measures in relation to external affairs; or<br>(f) measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation, including research for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(g) measures undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>165</td>
<td>International Education Innovation Fund</td>
