<td>To provide funding for activities directed to promoting, strengthening and growing Australia’s international education sector, including activities designed to:<br>(a) enhance Australia’s quality international education and training system; and<br>(b) build connections between any one or more of the following:<br>(i) students;<br>(ii) researchers;<br>(iii) education institutions;<br>(iv) Australian and overseas governments; and<br>(c) improve the global competitiveness of Australia’s international education sector; and<br>(d) identify opportunities to develop and improve Australia’s international education sector.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(d) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(f) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(g) with respect to Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(h) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>166</td>
<td>Centre for Defence Industry Capability</td>
<td>To support defence sector enterprises to meet the capability needs of the Department administered by the Minister administering section 1 of the <i>Defence Act 1903</i> (including the Australian Defence Force), and to promote the export of products and services of Australia’s defence industry sector, including by providing funding:<br>(a) for the provision of advisory and facilitation services to defence sector enterprises, or to enable those enterprises to access such services; and<br>(b) for grants to defence sector enterprises; and<br>(c) for projects directed to enhancing the capability of the defence industry sector generally.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities to be carried out:<br>(a) for the purposes of the defence of Australia; or<br>(b) in connection with trade or commerce:<br>(i) between Australia and other countries; or<br>(ii) among the States; or<br>(iii) between Territories or between a Territory and a State; or<br>(c) for purposes relating to matters incidental to the execution of any of the legislative powers of the Parliament or the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>167</td>
<td>Exploring for the Future</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities directed to producing a nationally significant minerals, energy and groundwater resources prospectus for areas of Australia, including by:<br>(a) acquiring and analysing geoscience data, including by using geophysical, geochemical and stratigraphic and other tools and techniques; and<br>(b) developing and delivering data products, including through an online portal.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to funding activities that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation, including research for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>168</td>
<td>Licensing of international vocational education and training courses</td>
<td>To develop and license vocational education and training courses for marketing and delivery overseas by Australian training providers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>169</td>
<td>Early Learning Languages Australia</td>
<td>To deliver, through the use of online communication services, language education to children, including by:<br>(a) maintaining and developing language learning applications for download onto tablet devices; and<br>(b) developing and providing support materials and professional development to educators; and<br>(c) funding the purchase of tablet devices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>171</td>
<td>Sustainable Rural Water Use and Infrastructure Program</td>
<td>To support activities relating to the implementation of the <i>Basin Plan 2012</i> by funding:<br>(a) the recovery of environmental water from the Basin water resources through the funding of irrigation infrastructure programs and the purchase of water access entitlements to implement long‑term average sustainable diversion limits; and<br>(b) measures to protect and restore environmental assets of the Murray‑Darling Basin, or to assist in achieving the Basin Plan environmental outcomes relating to ecosystem function, biodiversity, water quality and salinity and water resource health; and<br>(c) the compilation and online publication of information relating to the market price of water entitlements in the Murray‑Darling Basin.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) making grants of financial assistance to States and Territories; or<br>(b) funding activities done for the collection, compilation, analysis and dissemination of statistics and related information; or<br>(c) funding activities done to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the international treaties referred to in the definition of <b><i>relevant international agreement</b></i> in subsection 4(1) of the <i>Water Act 2007</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>173</td>
<td>Try, Test and Learn Fund</td>
<td>To conduct trial policy interventions for select cohorts of persons at high risk of long‑term welfare dependency.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) the provision of unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>174</td>
<td>Youth Jobs PaTH</td>
<td>To help young job seekers to obtain the skills to find and keep a job, and to move off income support, by:<br>(a) funding employability skills training for young job seekers; and<br>(b) providing financial incentives to the following:<br>(i) young job seekers who undertake internships;<br>(ii) businesses that host young job seekers as interns;<br>(iii) providers that place young job seekers as interns; and<br>(c) providing an online portal to connect young job seekers and businesses that may host job seekers as interns; and<br>(d) providing Youth Bonus wage subsidies to employers who hire young job seekers.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) measures in connection with online communications; or<br>(b) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(c) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Employment Policy Convention, Human Resources Development Convention and Employment Service Convention;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6; or<br>(d) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>175</td>
<td>Encouraging Entrepreneurship</td>
<td>To encourage entrepreneurship among unemployed and other persons, including by funding entrepreneurship facilitators, workshops, the provision of information and other activities to educate unemployed and other persons about entrepreneurship and self‑employment as alternatives to paid work as an employee.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) engaging in measures to meet Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(ia) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning the Organisation of the Employment Service, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(ib) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 13; or<br>(c) providing services in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>176</td>
<td>Rural General Practice Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to existing general practices in rural and regional Australia to build or purchase additional infrastructure or equipment to support the delivery of health services and to support the practices in providing clinical placements to students training to become health practitioners.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits, hospital benefits or medical services; or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>178</td>
<td>Protecting Australians from Antimicrobial Resistance</td>
<td>To improve Australia’s capacity to detect, prevent and respond to antimicrobial resistance in support of the National Antimicrobial Resistance Strategy 2015‑19 by:<br>(a) continuing and enhancing existing surveillance activities relating to antimicrobial resistance; and<br>(b) collecting and reporting data relating to antimicrobial resistance in Australia, including reporting data to the World Health Organization; and<br>(c) identifying risks and trends relating to antimicrobial resistance; and<br>(d) developing a plan and resources for general practitioners to support improved antimicrobial stewardship in general practice; and<br>(e) developing and maintaining a website (including developing content for the website) to improve public knowledge about antimicrobial resistance, including about its causes and effects.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) involving the collection, compilation, analysis or dissemination of statistics; or<br>(c) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical services, sickness benefits, hospital benefits or pharmaceutical benefits; or<br>(d) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(ii) the International Health Regulations, particularly Articles 5‑10 and 44; or<br>(e) taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>179</td>
<td>Drug and Alcohol Program</td>
<td>To reduce the impact of substance misuse on individuals, families, carers and communities, by:<br>(a) the provision of drug and alcohol treatment services, including through prevention, diagnosis and early intervention activities; and<br>(aa) developing or revising a tool that may be used:<br>(i) to diagnose Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (<b><i>FASD</b></i>); or<br>(ii) to assess the impairment caused by FASD; and<br>(b) treating health conditions arising from drug or alcohol misuse (including conditions in children arising from alcohol or drug use during pregnancy); and<br>(c) supporting individuals, families, carers and communities affected by drug or alcohol misuse or the effects of such misuse; and<br>(d) the development of data to support evidence‑based treatment, national policy development and service delivery; and<br>(e) supporting drug and alcohol treatment services, including to better integrate those services with broader health services; and<br>(f) training and educating health professionals and other health service providers, including by fostering the development of clinical and technical networks and supporting professional development and information sharing; and<br>(fa) developing and disseminating resources for teachers and support staff who work in schools or early childhood services that will assist them:<br>(i) to identify whether a child may have FASD; or<br>(ii) to maximise the academic and social development of a child with FASD; and<br>(fb) developing and disseminating resources that promote employment opportunities for people with FASD by providing guidance on how to assist people with FASD to find, obtain and maintain employment, including by combatting stereotypes and prejudices that relate to people with FASD; and<br>(g) supporting organisations representing the interests of, and providing services to, individuals, communities and families affected by drug or alcohol misuse or the effects of such misuse; and<br>(h) raising awareness of, providing education and advice on, and developing and disseminating information about drug and alcohol misuse (including prevention, treatment, management, control and the health effects of misuse); and<br>(i) supporting research relating to drug and alcohol misuse; and<br>(j) supporting capital works for infrastructure (including upgrading existing infrastructure) to provide treatment and support services for drug and alcohol misuse.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) measures in connection with communications; or<br>(aa) the collection, analysis, dissemination or use of statistics; or<br>(ab) providing assistance to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits, pharmaceutical benefits, hospital benefits or medical services; or<br>(c) providing assistance to Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(d) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(ii) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs (as amended), particularly Article 38;<br>(iii) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(iv) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14;<br>(v) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8, 24, 25, 26 and 27;<br>(vi) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 23 and 24; or<br>(e) measures undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(f) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) measures carried out in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>180</td>
<td>Primary Health Care Development Program</td>
<td>To strengthen health care outcomes through facilitating access to, and improving the quality, efficiency and availability of, health and medical services in the community by:<br>(a) providing and commissioning health care services, including developing and implementing new or revised models of care delivery or payment approaches; and<br>(b) providing health care advice, information and support through a range of communication channels; and<br>(c) facilitating the coordination and integration of health care services offered for selected patient cohorts in the community and across other sectors such as acute care, ambulatory care, specialist care and residential aged care services; and<br>(d) supporting the development and implementation of accreditation processes and standards for health professionals and other health service providers; and<br>(e) establishing and facilitating data collection, data sharing and associated quality improvement processes in general practices and Aboriginal medical services; and<br>(f) providing support to general practice, health professionals and other health service providers:<br>(i) to improve patient health outcomes; and<br>(ii) to enhance the practice and organisation of care; and<br>(g) training and educating health professionals, general practice staff and other health service providers; and<br>(h) providing support to general practice, health professionals and other health service providers in enhancing the practice and organisation of care; and<br>(i) informing the public about health services and programs; and<br>(j) undertaking evaluation activities to inform decisions relating to existing or potential new Commonwealth health programs and measures.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) involving the collection, compilation, analysis or dissemination of statistics; or<br>(c) providing, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits, hospital benefits or medical services; or<br>(d) providing assistance to Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(e) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 23 and 24:<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8, 25 and 26;<br>(iv) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs (as amended), particularly Article 38;<br>(v) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(vi) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14; or<br>(f) taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(g) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(h) carried out in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>181</td>
<td>Health Policy Research and Data Program</td>
<td>To build a strong evidence base to inform the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of health policy and improved practice in Australia, including by funding universities and other organisations and persons to conduct:<br>(a) research on a range of subject matters relevant to health policy (including activities supporting the dissemination of research and knowledge exchange); and<br>(b) evaluation activities to inform decisions relating to existing or potential new Commonwealth health programs or measures; and<br>(c) data activities, including the following:<br>(i) developing and operating data infrastructure;<br>(ii) developing data definitions;<br>(iii) the collection, development and management of data;<br>(iv) data analysis and interpretation;<br>(v) data dissemination, reporting and use.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) involving the collection, compilation, analysis or dissemination of statistics; or<br>(c) relating to the health of, or provision of health services to, immigrants or aliens; or<br>(d) incidental to the provision of medical services, sickness benefits, hospital benefits or pharmaceutical benefits; or<br>(e) relating to the health of, or provision of, health services to Aboriginal persons and Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(f) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(g) taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(h) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(i) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(j) carried out in a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>182</td>
<td>Health Protection Program</td>
<td>To support activities that strengthen the nation’s capacity and capability to detect, prepare for and respond to health emergencies and communicable diseases, including by:<br>(a) maintaining laboratory capacity and capability for, and providing laboratory services in the event of, a health emergency; and<br>(b) maintaining a register of biological agents of security concern; and<br>(c) developing and implementing measures to support health emergency response activities; and<br>(d) providing emergency response training and support to health personnel; and<br>(e) developing, and implementing as necessary, a communications campaign for responding to health emergencies; and<br>(f) maintaining a stockpile of pharmaceuticals, vaccines and other health resources for distribution in health emergencies; and<br>(g) commissioning research relating to potential or emerging public health threats; and<br>(h) developing and implementing quarantine and biosecurity measures; and<br>(i) developing and implementing communicable disease related surveillance, controls, data collection, research, analysis and reporting, including in countries from which diseases could spread to Australia; and<br>(j) supporting activities aimed at reducing the incidence of communicable diseases, including blood‑borne viruses and sexually transmissible infections; and<br>(k) informing the public, affected persons and health practitioners about communicable diseases and their prevention and treatment; and<br>(l) commissioning research about health issues arising from environmental factors.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) relating to the defence of the Commonwealth; or<br>(c) relating to quarantine; or<br>(d) involving the collection, compilation, analysis or dissemination of statistics; or<br>(e) relating to the health of, or provision of health services to, immigrants or aliens; or<br>(f) providing, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits, hospital benefits or medical services; or<br>(g) providing assistance to Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(h) giving effect to Australia’s obligations, including those under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(ii) the International Health Regulations, particularly Articles 5‑10 and 44; or<br>(i) relating to matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries and international organisations; or<br>(j) taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(k) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(l) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>183</td>
<td>Public Health and Chronic Disease Program</td>
<td>To address the rising burden of chronic disease and improve public health by:<br>(a) improving the quality of existing health services; and<br>(b) supporting the development of new health services, controls and practices; and<br>(c) raising awareness of, providing education and advice on, and developing and disseminating information about health conditions (including their prevention, treatment, management and control), health services and family planning; and<br>(d) training and educating health professionals and other health service providers; and<br>(e) informing the public about health policy, programs, research and best practice; and<br>(f) providing support services to persons with health conditions and their families; and<br>(g) conducting health checks for particular groups; and<br>(h) implementing, developing and promoting food and nutrition policy, including a health star rating system for food labelling; and<br>(i) enhancing the quality of, improving access to, and supporting, palliative care, end of life care and advance care planning services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) involving the collection, compilation, analysis or dissemination of statistics; or<br>(c) providing, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students, sickness benefits, pharmaceutical benefits, hospital benefits or medical services; or<br>(d) providing assistance to Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(e) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(f) taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>184</td>
<td>Emergency Management Volunteer Scholarships</td>
<td>To establish and administer a scholarship program supporting emergency management volunteer education, to provide benefits to students in the form of scholarships.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>185</td>
<td>Family Relationships Services Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for the following:<br>(a) family law services, including funding for:<br>(i) family relationship centres to assist families with relationship issues, including by way of mediation services in relation to property matters; and<br>(ii) family dispute resolution services, including in regional areas, to assist families to settle parenting and property arrangements following separation; and<br>(iii) family counselling services to assist families with relationship issues following separation; and<br>(iv) a family relationship advice line providing advice (including legal advice) and non‑face‑to‑face dispute resolution services over the telephone and online; and<br>(v) services to assist separating families in high conflict over parenting arrangements; and<br>(vi) services to assist children from separating families to deal with issues arising from their parents’ separation; and<br>(vii) children’s contact services to assist children of separated parents to establish and maintain relationships with the parent, and other family members, with whom the child does not reside;<br>(b) the Family Law Pathways Networks to improve collaboration and coordination between organisations and professionals working with separating and separated families in the family law system to help those families obtain appropriate services;<br>(c) Family Law System Projects to enhance the family law system’s capacity to respond to the needs of separating and separated families.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in connection with telephonic or electronic communications; or<br>(b) in relation to marriage; or<br>(c) in relation to divorce, including in relation to parental rights or the custody or guardianship of infants; or<br>(d) to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Article 23;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 10 and 12; or<br>(e) to meet Australia’s obligations in relation to children, including those under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 9, 12, 18, 19, 24 and 27; or<br>(f) to meet Australia’s obligations in relation to women, in particular those under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women; or<br>(g) in relation to matters referred to the Parliament of the Commonwealth by the Parliament or Parliaments of any State or States; or<br>(h) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(i) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>186</td>
<td>Safer Communities Fund</td>
<td>To address crime and antisocial behaviour, and to protect community centres, pre‑schools, schools and places of worship that are at high risk of attack, harassment or violence as a result of racial or religious intolerance.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities that:<br>(a) are in connection with online or telephonic communications; or<br>(b) are engaged in to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Article 18;<br>(ii) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>187</td>
<td>Status Resolution and Support Services</td>
<td>To provide needs‑based support and assistance to eligible asylum seekers and other non‑citizens (both in immigration detention and living in the Australian community):<br>(a) as they seek to resolve their immigration status; and<br>(b) as, once their immigration status has been resolved (whether by the grant of a substantive visa or otherwise), they transition to mainstream services in the Australian community or make preparations to depart Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>188</td>
<td>Onshore Education Program</td>
<td>To fund access to education and associated needs‑based support for certain persons in Australia without authority, including unauthorised maritime arrivals. The funding is primarily, but not exclusively, for school aged children:<br>(a) in immigration detention; or<br>(b) covered by a residence determination within the meaning of the <i>Migration Act 1958</i>; or<br>(c) who are unauthorised maritime arrivals and hold Bridging E visas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>189</td>
<td>English as a Second Language Program</td>
<td>To provide access to introductory level English as a second language course for unauthorised maritime arrivals:<br>(a) covered by a residence determination within the meaning of the <i>Migration Act 1958</i>; or<br>(b) who hold Bridging E visas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>190</td>
<td>Regional Jobs and Investment Package</td>
<td>To encourage investment, employment, productivity and innovation in regions affected by structural economic change and foster the capacity of such regions to participate in international and domestic trade, by providing grants for projects which support economic diversification, growth and employment in regions.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(c) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(d) to provide medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, benefits to students, and measures incidental to the provision of those services or benefits; or<br>(e) to, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(f) to meet its obligations under international agreements, including under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6; or<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy; or<br>(g) for the construction or extension of railways in any State with the consent of that State; or<br>(h) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(i) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(j) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(k) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>191</td>
<td>Building Better Regions Fund</td>
<td>To support regional and remote communities by providing grants for infrastructure and community investment projects which create jobs and encourage economic growth in such communities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(c) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(d) to provide medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, benefits to students, and measures incidental to the provision of those services or benefits; or<br>(e) to, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(f) to meet its obligations under international agreements, including under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6; or<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy; or<br>(g) for the construction or extension of railways in any State with the consent of that State; or<br>(h) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(i) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(j) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(k) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>192</td>
<td>National Support for Child and Youth Mental Health</td>
<td>To improve the mental health of children and young people by:<br>(a) developing and disseminating the evidence base for strategies and interventions that improve the outcomes of children who have a mental illness or who are at risk of developing a mental illness; and<br>(b) developing programs that can be implemented by early childhood services, primary schools and secondary schools that promote good mental health and early intervention for children who have or may have a mental illness or who are at risk of developing a mental illness; and<br>(c) increasing the capacity of early childhood services, primary schools and secondary schools to implement evidence‑based approaches to improving the mental health of students, including by developing, publishing and distributing resources; and<br>(d) delivering training that improves the skills of professionals who work with children who have or who may be at risk of developing a mental illness; and<br>(e) promoting the inclusion and coverage of mental health in the curricula delivered by universities and vocational educational providers for trainee teachers and other students who intend to work in schools or early childhood services; and<br>(f) strengthening referral pathways for children who have or may have a mental illness or who are at risk of developing a mental illness by facilitating relationships between early childhood services, primary schools and secondary schools and providers of health and community services; and<br>(g) delivering activities directed at reducing the incidence of suicide amongst children, including by delivering postvention services to secondary schools; and<br>(h) developing and disseminating guidance to parents and guardians on steps they can take to promote the mental health of their child; and<br>(i) developing a communications strategy to promote the mental health of children and young people which will be delivered through the Student Wellbeing Hub.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for measures in connection with the use of telegraphic, telephonic and other like services; or<br>(b) for the provision of medical services and measures incidental to the provision of those services; or<br>(c) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following international agreements:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18 and 24;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) for measures undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(e) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>193</td>
<td>Early Psychosis Youth Services Program</td>
<td>To provide early intervention and intensive support for those young people accepted into the Early Youth Psychosis Services Program who are experiencing, or who are at risk of, first episode psychosis, including by:<br>(a) providing medical and psychological assessment and treatment; and<br>(b) providing a case management approach to continuing care of young people by health professionals and social workers; and<br>(c) providing vocational and educational assistance; and<br>(d) providing a peer support program, and a group program that addresses personal issues such as lack of confidence, low self‑esteem, anger or anxiety; and<br>(e) supporting family members and caregivers; and<br>(f) providing community education to improve mental health literacy related to first episode psychosis; and<br>(g) providing development for healthcare workers and other workers who provide relevant services; and<br>(h) providing support for organisations that provide relevant healthcare services to partner with, and provide referrals to, other organisations providing services that support young people, including housing, educational, vocational, financial and legal services; and<br>(i) engaging the National Centre of Excellence in Youth Mental Health to provide expert advice to Primary Health Networks on models of care for young people with severe mental illness.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for the provision of medical services, unemployment, pharmaceutical, hospital and sickness benefits or benefits to students; or<br>(b) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following international agreements:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18, 24, 27, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 12;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 16, 19, 26, 27 and 28;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(v) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; or<br>(c) for measures undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(d) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>194</td>
<td>Improving your Local Parks and Environment Program</td>
<td>To provide support for local councils, environmental and community groups and others to undertake measures for the protection of the environment in their local areas, in particular by:<br>(a) protecting, conserving and rehabilitating natural ecosystems and habitats; and<br>(b) undertaking activities and adopting practices aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(a) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 7(c), 8(d), (f), (h) and (l) and 13(a); or<br>(b) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4(1)(b), (c) and (f) and 4(2)(a).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>195</td>
<td>Solar Communities Program</td>
<td>To provide support for community groups to install solar photovoltaic equipment, solar hot water equipment and solar‑connected batteries at facilities that they own, lease or use to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, to the extent that these measures give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(a) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change; or<br>(b) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>196</td>
<td>Food Rescue Charity Program</td>
<td>To provide support for food rescue charities to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, in particular by:<br>(a) installing solar photovoltaic equipment, solar‑connected batteries and energy efficient refrigeration equipment at facilities that they own, lease or use; or<br>(b) purchasing energy efficient refrigeration vehicles.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(a) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change; or<br>(b) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>198</td>
<td>Digital Literacy for Older Australians</td>
<td>To develop the digital literacy and online safety of older Australians by providing funding:<br>(a) to develop and deliver a national online portal for older Australians, including developing digital and smart device training materials and online safety tools for inclusion on the portal; and<br>(b) for service providers to develop and deliver:<br>(i) a national telephone helpline to provide training and support to older Australians who make, or who attempt to make, digital communications or to community organisations to assist such older Australians; and<br>(ii) educational and training resources for community organisations to use in supporting older Australians to make digital communications; and<br>(iii) training workshops for people working with older Australians to assist older Australians in making digital communications; and<br>(iv) training sessions to facilitate school children assisting older Australians to acquire the skills needed to make digital communications; and<br>(c) for particular community organisations to support older Australians to make digital communications, including by:<br>(i) delivering training courses to older Australians; and<br>(ii) purchasing smart devices and internet connection services for the benefit of older Australians; and<br>(d) for a service provider to administer the funding referred to in paragraph (c); and<br>(e) to develop and deliver a communications and marketing strategy to promote the measures described in paragraphs (a) to (c); and<br>(f) for an independent evaluation of the measures described in paragraphs (a) to (e).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities:<br>(a) in relation to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) in exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>199</td>
<td>Prevention of Domestic Violence</td>
<td>To provide funding:<br>(a) to develop guides and resources to assist local communities to implement strategies to prevent domestic violence; and<br>(b) to develop a framework for shared understanding and collaborative action in relation to preventing violence against Indigenous women and children; and<br>(c) for community‑led strategies to prevent domestic violence, particularly in culturally and linguistically diverse communities; and<br>(d) to develop educational resources to enable witnesses of violence against women and children to take safe and appropriate action; and<br>(e) to develop and disseminate information and advice to men who have become fathers for the first time about the importance of their involvement in the development and care of their child, including by positive role‑modelling; and<br>(f) for local projects aimed at supporting men who perpetrate, or are at risk of perpetrating, domestic violence in order to reduce the likelihood that they will perpetrate such violence; and<br>(g) to develop resources to raise awareness of non‑physical forms of abuse and the misuse of power and control insofar as these behaviours can lead to domestic violence; and<br>(h) for domestic violence prevention strategies focussing on education, employment and empowerment, particularly for women from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities:<br>(a) in relation to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(c) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(d) to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Article 6(2)); and<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (particularly Article 7); and<br>(iii) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Articles 2, 3, 5(a) and 16); and<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4, 18 and 19).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>200</td>
<td>Domestic Violence Frontline Services</td>
<td>To provide funding:<br>(a) for alternative accommodation for women escaping domestic violence, with a particular focus on mothers with teenage sons; and<br>(b) for workers in the financial counselling and financial capability sector to equip them to better recognise, and respond to the needs of, women who have experienced domestic violence; and<br>(c) to develop and deliver service delivery models to meet the needs of women with disabilities, and women who are non‑citizens or migrants, for integrated, wrap‑around services relating to domestic violence; and<br>(d) to develop and deliver training to disability sector workers in identifying, and supporting, the needs of women with disabilities who experience violence.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities:<br>(a) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Articles 2, 3, 5(a) and 16); and<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4 and 19); and<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (particularly Article 6(2)); and<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (particularly Article 7).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>201</td>
<td>Revenge pornography complaints mechanism and countering the impact of pornography on young people</td>
<td>To establish a complaints mechanism for revenge pornography and to counter the influence of pornography, particularly on young people, insofar as it contributes to domestic and sexual violence by:<br>(a) establishing an online mechanism for persons to report instances of their intimate images being disseminated without their consent; and<br>(b) providing support to such persons; and<br>(c) developing and implementing strategies to change the attitudes and behaviours of young people with respect to the dissemination of intimate images.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities:<br>(a) in relation to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Articles 2, 5(a) and 16); and<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4 and 19).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>202</td>
<td>Rural outreach dental services</td>
<td>To fund the provision of dental services in regional, rural and remote areas, to the extent that these measures:<br>(a) provide, or are incidental to the provision of, medical and dental services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Articles 2 and 12); or<br>(c) are carried out in a Territory or relate to residents of a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>203</td>
<td>Suicide Prevention Research Fund</td>
<td>To fund an organisation to:<br>(a) provide, in a nationally coordinated manner, grants for research into the prevention of suicide; and<br>(b) develop and maintain an online hub of evidence‑based suicide prevention resources (including developing content for the hub).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) to support veterans and defence force members and their families; or<br>(c) to support Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Article 12); or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Article 24); or<br>(iii) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Article 12); or<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (particularly Article 25); or<br>(e) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(f) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>204</td>
<td>Suicide Prevention Trials</td>
<td>To fund Primary Health Networks to conduct trials of suicide prevention models and practices which may include the provision of treatment for individuals who have attempted suicide.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) to support veterans and defence force members and their families; or<br>(c) to provide pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits and medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution) and incidental to the provision of those benefits or services; or<br>(d) to support Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Article 12); or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Article 24); or<br>(iii) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (particularly Article 12); or<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (particularly Article 25); or<br>(f) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(g) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>205</td>
<td>Headspace</td>
<td>To provide funding for youth‑friendly community‑based mental health services for young Australians aged 12 to 25 with, or at risk of developing, mental illness and associated drug and alcohol problems, including by:<br>(a) providing a Centre of Excellence to promote evidence‑based practice; and<br>(b) leading the design and delivery of early identification and intervention strategies; and<br>(c) fostering community awareness of youth mental health and drug and alcohol issues; and<br>(d) implementing a grants program to support local, integrated approaches to enhance and facilitate the coordination of services; and<br>(e) developing and disseminating evidence‑based education, training and resources for general practitioners and other service providers; and<br>(f) establishing and delivering eheadspace, a national telephone and web‑based support service; and<br>(g) maintaining centralised management and support to service sites by the headspace national office, including standardised data collection, clinical expertise and staff training; and<br>(h) implementing a framework for ongoing independent evaluation and data training.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution) and incidental to the provision of those services; or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Articles 2 and 12); or<br>(c) carried out in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(d) for the collection, analysis, dissemination or use of statistics (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xi) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) in connection with telephonic or electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>206</td>
<td>Lifeline text service</td>
<td>To fund the development, delivery and evaluation of a trial text message‑based support service for people needing crisis or suicide prevention support.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with telephonic or electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>207</td>
<td>Digital technologies for mental health</td>
<td>To fund:<br>(a) the development of resources and support tools relating to mental health for delivery online; and<br>(b) the development of smart applications and websites for the delivery online of resources and support tools relating to mental health services; and<br>(c) the delivery, online or by telephone, of mental health services including by means of smart applications, websites and third party messenger services; and<br>(d) the development and trial of information technology solutions to better deliver online mental health services; and<br>(e) the delivery, online or by telephone, of counselling services and peer‑support services to individuals who are experiencing distress or grief, or who are at increased risk of suicide; and<br>(f) the evaluation of the efficacy of any of the resources, tools, applications, websites or services referred to in paragraphs (a) to (e);<br>as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>208</td>
<td>Digital Mental Health Gateway</td>
<td>To provide funding:<br>(a) to use digital technology (including online communications and telephone) to provide evidence‑based information and advice to the community on mental health and digital mental health service options; and<br>(b) to develop and implement a certification framework for digital mental health services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with telephonic or electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>210</td>
<td>Loan to NBN Co Limited</td>
<td>To provide additional funding to NBN Co Limited, through a loan to be fully repaid with interest, to assist the company to roll out, operate and maintain a wholesale‑only national broadband network.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support to engage in measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>211</td>
<td>Mobile Black Spot Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for investment in telecommunications infrastructure to improve mobile voice and data coverage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>212</td>
<td>Feasibility study for submarine telecommunications cable</td>
<td>To provide support to the Sunshine Coast Regional Council to conduct a feasibility study to:<br>(a) assess the benefits and costs of connecting an international submarine telecommunications cable to Australia on the Sunshine Coast; and<br>(b) examine how to leverage private sector investment to unlock the economic value from such a cable.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) in connection with measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>213</td>
<td>Protecting the Rights of Older Australians</td>
<td>To provide funding for the following:<br>(a) research relating to the nature and prevalence of elder abuse;<br>(b) a national awareness campaign about older persons’ rights and capabilities;<br>(c) research into the need for, and the delivery of, a national hotline to inform, assist and support people who have experienced, or who are at risk of experiencing, elder abuse;<br>(d) pilot training for persons (including staff in Commonwealth government agencies) who deliver services to older persons about elder abuse, its identification and appropriate responses to it;<br>to the extent that the provision of the funding:<br>(e) is within the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(f) involves the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(g) assists Australia to meet its obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (in particular Articles 7, 17(1) and 26) and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (in particular Articles 8(1)(b) and 16).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>214</td>
<td>Surf Life Saving Cleaner Outboard Engines Scheme</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to surf life saving clubs that will support them to upgrade their outboard engines to more efficient models that use less fuel and produce lower greenhouse gas emissions.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to supporting activities that would assist Australia to meets its obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change;<br>(b) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change;<br>(c) the Paris Agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>215</td>
<td>Launch Into Work</td>
<td>To provide support for jobseekers:<br>(a) to improve their skills, experience and confidence; and<br>(b) to help them to find and keep employment.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing unemployment or sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) providing funding for measures giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 5; or<br>(c) providing services in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>216</td>
<td>Quality Use of Pathology</td>
<td>To provide funding to ensure the quality and accessibility of pathology services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>217</td>
<td>Youth Cancer Services</td>
<td>To provide funding:<br>(a) to assist multidisciplinary teams to provide information and support to young people living with cancer and to link them with appropriate services; and<br>(b) to provide facilities for treatment and support for young people living with cancer, including social and emotional support; and<br>(c) to implement a national minimum data set on young people living with cancer; and<br>(d) to facilitate access to clinical trials by young people living with cancer; and<br>(e) to develop and implement national and local strategies to support the delivery of high quality youth cancer services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) involving the collection, compilation, analysis or dissemination of statistics; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>218</td>
<td>Health Workforce Program</td>
<td>To strengthen the capacity of the health workforce to deliver high quality care by:<br>(a) facilitating the appropriate supply of health professionals, including general practitioners, nurses and allied health professionals; and<br>(b) fostering the capability and qualification of health professionals; and<br>(c) supporting health professionals and students who are Aboriginal persons, Torres Strait Islanders or aliens; and<br>(d) addressing health workforce shortages in regional, rural and remote Australia;<br>to the extent that these measures:<br>(e) provide assistance to Aboriginal persons, Torres Strait Islanders or aliens; or<br>(f) provide, or are incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, medical services and benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(g) are taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(h) give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12, or<br>(i) are in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(j) involve the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>219</td>
<td>Promoting a Sustainable and Flexible Mental Health Care Nursing Workforce</td>
<td>To fund an organisation to deliver:<br>(a) an education program to improve mental health knowledge and skills in the primary health care nurse workforce; and<br>(b) a program to facilitate the transition of specialist mental health nurses between acute, community and primary health care settings.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>221</td>
<td>Vocational Education and Training Information Strategy</td>
<td>To provide funding to raise awareness about vocational education and training programs in Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) directed to meeting Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Article 6); or<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy and Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>222</td>
<td>Explicit Instruction Teaching</td>
<td>To fund training for teachers at educationally disadvantaged primary schools to enable them to adopt explicit instruction teaching methods in relation to literacy, numeracy and science to improve the skills and knowledge of students (particularly Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students), to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>223</td>
<td>Australian Early Development Census</td>
<td>To develop, implement, analyse and disseminate the results of a population measure of the state of development Australian children have reached by the time they commence their first year of full‑time schooling.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) in connection with collecting, analysing, disseminating or using statistics; or<br>(c) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(d) funded by way of grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>224</td>
<td>Smart Cities and Suburbs Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to local governments, or to entities collaborating with local governments, to:<br>(a) apply smart technologies (being technologies that generate, store, communicate or process data) to improve the liveability of cities and their suburbs; or<br>(b) develop knowledge of, or the capability to apply, such smart technologies;<br>to the extent that these activities involve or are incidental to:<br>(c) using electronic communications; or<br>(d) collecting, analysing, disseminating or using statistics; or<br>(e) engaging in measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>225</td>
<td>Indigenous Advancement—Safety and Wellbeing (addressing violence and support to victims)</td>
<td>The funding and provision of activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services that promote the safety and wellbeing of Indigenous persons, families and communities by addressing violence and supporting victims of violence, including through:<br>(a) victim support services; and<br>(b) family‑focused case management; and<br>(c) services to change perpetrator behaviour; and<br>(d) therapeutic child‑focused initiatives.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>227</td>
<td>Tobacco Control Initiatives and Activities to Reduce Tobacco Prevalence and Harm</td>
<td>To provide funding for tobacco control initiatives and activities that support the Commonwealth’s tobacco control priorities, including by:<br>(a) developing, implementing and evaluating tobacco control measures, including graphic health warnings; and<br>(b) contributing to the work carried out under the auspices of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control; and<br>(c) improving and supporting collaboration and cooperation among stakeholders, including through:<br>(i) the sponsorship of international and national conferences relating to tobacco control; and<br>(ii) the funding of stakeholders (including tobacco control organisations such as non‑government organisations working to promote tobacco control and cessation) to assist them to carry out their functions.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>228</td>
<td>The Australian Children’s Television Foundation</td>
<td>To fund The Australian Children’s Television Foundation to support the development, production and dissemination of Australian screen content for Australian children.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to funding activities:<br>(a) connected with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, or other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>229</td>
<td>AusFILM International Incorporated</td>
<td>To fund AusFILM International Incorporated to increase foreign interest in Australia as a destination for screen production and post, digital and visual effects services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to funding activities:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States; or<br>(b) connected with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, or other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>230</td>
<td>Defence Cooperative Research Centres</td>
<td>To provide funding for grants to Defence Cooperative Research Centres to undertake research on, and to develop, technologies relevant to Australia’s defence and national security sectors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>231</td>
<td>National Collaborative Research Infrastructure Strategy</td>
<td>To fund national collaborative research infrastructure facilities and projects to establish, maintain and operate national research infrastructure, in order to do one or more of the following:<br>(a) deliver facilities and projects of a national character, with nationally significant purposes and outcomes, as identified over time;<br>(b) support high quality, priority research to facilitate greater discovery and innovation in the Australian research sector and the Australian economy more broadly;<br>(c) enable Australian researchers to address key national and global challenges;<br>(d) support collaboration between researchers and research infrastructure facilities and projects, both nationally and internationally;<br>(e) support collaboration between researchers and end users (including governments and industry) both nationally and internationally;<br>(f) foster Australian innovation, economic development, national security, social wellbeing and environmental sustainability;<br>(g) enable Australia to meet its reporting obligations under international agreements and to maintain international collaborative research relationships.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to research infrastructure funding measures:<br>(a) relating to interstate and overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) relating to postal, telegraphic, telephonic or other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and the States; or<br>(d) relating to astronomical and meteorological observations; or<br>(e) relating to quarantine; or<br>(f) relating to fisheries in Australian waters beyond territorial limits; or<br>(g) relating to the use of statistical information; or<br>(h) relating to the provision of pharmaceutical, sickness or hospital benefits, medical or dental services, or benefits to students, within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution; or<br>(i) relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(j) for the purpose of enabling Australia to meet its research, implementation or reporting obligations under international agreements; or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>(k) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(l) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of the nation and which cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(m) that are done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(n) relating to a grant of financial assistance to a State.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>232</td>
<td>Industry Specialist Mentoring for Australian Apprentices</td>
<td>To provide support for industry specialist mentoring services for apprentices and trainees:<br>(a) to improve retention and completion rates; and<br>(b) to support the supply of skilled workers in industries undergoing structural change.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities that are the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>233</td>
<td>Data Integration Partnership for Australia</td>
<td>To provide funding for initiatives that will facilitate the analysis of data by collecting, sharing and linking data from multiple sources by electronic means, including by:<br>(a) creating integrated data analytical units; and<br>(b) creating integrated datasets; and<br>(c) enhancing the Data Exchange, which is a platform used by certain entities that receive government funding to report on their performance; and<br>(d) enhancing the Enterprise Data Warehouse, which is a platform which holds data for health and aged care programs; and<br>(e) implementing a National Education Evidence Base; and<br>(f) providing trusted third parties with access to integrated datasets; and<br>(g) promoting public understanding of the benefits of analysing data from multiple sources.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities:<br>(a) involving the use of telegraphic, telephonic, or other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the collection, analysis, dissemination or use of statistics (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xi) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) that are incidental to the provision of invalid or old‑age pensions (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiii) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) that are incidental to the provision of maternity allowances, widows’ pensions, child endowment, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness or hospital benefits, medical or dental services, benefits to students or family allowances (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>234</td>
<td>New Disability Employment Framework—Employer‑Nominated Initiatives</td>
<td>To provide funding for improved employer practices in the employment of persons with disabilities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to meet Australia’s international obligations under Article 27 of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>235</td>
<td>New Disability Employment Framework—Targeted Communications</td>
<td>To provide funding to promote employment of persons with disabilities, including by:<br>(a) raising the profile of employers that implement strategies to improve employment outcomes for persons with disabilities; and<br>(b) disseminating information to improve employment outcomes for persons with disabilities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to meet Australia’s international obligations under Article 27 of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>236</td>
<td>Boosting the Local Care Workforce</td>
<td>To facilitate an adequate and appropriate supply of disability, aged care and veterans’ care service providers, including for the purposes of the National Disability Insurance Scheme, the <i>Aged Care Act 1997</i> and the <i>Veterans’ Entitlements Act 1986</i>, by:<br>(a) funding regional coordinators to provide assistance to existing and potential new disability, aged care and veterans’ care service providers; and<br>(b) funding specialist coordinators to monitor disability, aged care and veterans’ care service provision and to identify issues that may affect the adequate supply of such services; and<br>(c) assisting disability service providers to prepare to provide services under the National Disability Insurance Scheme, by making grants to them and providing them with access to services provided by third parties that are relevant to the preparation of those providers.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to support veterans and defence force members and their families; or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment, sickness or hospital benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 19, 20, 25, 26 and 27;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>237</td>
<td>Prime Minister’s Veterans’ Employment Program</td>
<td>To fund activities under the Prime Minister’s Veterans’ Employment Program, including:<br>(a) managing the Prime Minister’s Veterans’ Employment Annual Awards, including an annual event to confer the Awards; and<br>(b) establishing and supporting an Industry Advisory Committee responsible for developing practical measures to provide greater employment opportunities for veterans; and<br>(c) establishing an ex‑service organisation industry partnership register to facilitate employment initiatives for veterans; and<br>(d) establishing a framework that encourages businesses to commit to supporting the employment of veterans and the spouses of serving defence force members.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to the following:<br>(a) activities using electronic communications;<br>(b) commemorating Australians killed or injured in war;<br>(c) supporting any or all of the following:<br>(i) veterans;<br>(ii) defence force members;<br>(iii) the families of veterans and defence force members;<br>(iv) the communities of veterans and defence force members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>240</td>
<td>National Facial Biometric Matching Capability</td>
<td>To facilitate the secure and accountable sharing of facial images and associated identity information between Commonwealth, State and Territory agencies to promote identity security, national security and law enforcement by funding the establishment and ongoing costs of the Interoperability Hub and National Driver Licence Facial Recognition Solution, to the extent that the measures:<br>(a) are in connection with online and electronic communications; or<br>(b) are for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and the States; or<br>(c) relate to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(d) relate to a Territory; or<br>(e) are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) are undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>241</td>
<td>General Practitioners Healthy Heart Partnership</td>
<td>To fund the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners to develop education and training material for general practitioners and their patients.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) in connection with electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>242</td>
<td>Prime Minister’s Walk for Life Challenge</td>
