<td>To fund the Prime Minister’s Walk for Life Challenge.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures giving effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(b) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 24 and 29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>243</td>
<td>Livestock Global Assurance Program</td>
<td>To support the Australian livestock export industry in demonstrating compliance with requirements for the Exporter Supply Chain Assurance System, by establishing and supporting an entity to implement an independent certification and assurance scheme used by overseas importers and facilities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) relating to, or promoting, interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(c) incidental to the execution of any of the legislative powers of the Parliament.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>244</td>
<td>Agricultural Trade and Market Access Cooperation Program</td>
<td>To support measures for opening, improving or maintaining access to overseas markets for Australian agricultural products by building stronger relationships with international trading partners and international organisations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>245</td>
<td>Television Coverage for Women’s Sport and Niche Sport</td>
<td>To provide funding for television and online coverage of women’s sporting events and niche sporting events, including the development, preparation and promotion of content to be broadcast.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>246</td>
<td>US‑Australia International Multidisciplinary University Research Initiative</td>
<td>To improve Australia’s defence capabilities by providing grants to Australian universities to participate in research projects funded under the Multidisciplinary University Research Initiative of the United States Department of Defense.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>247</td>
<td>Bali Lifetime Rehabilitation Assistance Program</td>
<td>To provide assistance for out‑of‑pocket expenses for rehabilitation care to eligible Australians injured in the Bali Bombings that occurred on 12 October 2002 or 1 October 2005.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits and medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Article 26.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>248</td>
<td>Strong and Resilient Communities—Community Resilience</td>
<td>To provide grants for projects in high needs communities directed at addressing actual or potential, or early signs of, low social cohesion or racial, religious or cultural intolerance that could ultimately pose a risk to Australia’s national security. Such projects may include a multicultural arts or festival event and a Harmony Day event.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (particularly Articles 2 and 7); or<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (particularly Articles 2, 18, 19 and 27).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>249</td>
<td>Strong and Resilient Communities—Inclusive Communities</td>
<td>To support the social and economic participation of people in their communities by providing grants for projects that:<br>(a) support the development of children under 18 who are disengaged or marginalised, at risk of marginalisation or at risk of poor educational outcomes, through:<br>(i) early intervention, mentoring, volunteering, sport or recreational activities; or<br>(ii) activities that encourage school attendance and retention; or<br>(iii) mentoring and support programs; or<br>(b) are directed at eliminating racial, cultural or ethnic discrimination within the community, including through educational and awareness activities, community workshops or forums; or<br>(c) are directed at addressing issues of discrimination against women in order to support women in exercising their rights and freedoms on an equal basis with men; or<br>(d) are directed at people with disabilities (including people with mental health issues) in order to support their full and equal participation in society on an equal basis with others, and to support them to become and remain independent, including through skills training; or<br>(e) are directed at unemployed people in order to provide them with technical and vocational guidance and training programs, including opportunities which will provide them with a pathway to paid employment and improve work skills; or<br>(f) support the social and economic participation of non‑citizens in their communities; or<br>(g) are delivered online to support the social and economic participation of people in their communities; or<br>(h) support the social and economic participation of Indigenous Australians within their communities;<br>and that may include a multicultural arts or festival event and a Harmony Day event.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child (particularly Articles 4, 6, 28, 29 and 31);<br>(ii) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (particularly Articles 2 and 7);<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (particularly Articles 2, 18, 19 and 27);<br>(iv) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (particularly Article 3);<br>(v) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (particularly Articles 4, 19, 26 and 27);<br>(vi) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (particularly Article 6);<br>(vii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy (particularly Article 1); or<br>(b) providing unemployment or sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) in relation to aliens; or<br>(d) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) to benefit Aboriginal persons or Torres Strait Islanders; or<br>(f) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>250</td>
<td>Assisting to Prevent Suicides at Hotspot Locations</td>
<td>To fund Lifeline to deliver and promote the Suicide “Hotspot” Crisis Line Service.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with telephonic or electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>251</td>
<td>English Language Learning for Indigenous Children</td>
<td>To deliver, through the use of online communication services, English language education to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, including by:<br>(a) maintaining and developing English language learning applications for download onto tablet devices; and<br>(b) developing and providing support materials and professional development to educators; and<br>(c) funding the purchase of tablet devices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>252</td>
<td>Rural and Regional Enterprise Scholarships</td>
<td>To provide:<br>(a) scholarships to students from rural and regional areas to undertake undergraduate, postgraduate or vocational education and training studies; and<br>(b) payments to such scholarship holders who arrange and undertake internships relevant to their studies, and to employers who provide such internships to such scholarship holders.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 6 and 13;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>253</td>
<td>Reef Guardian Grants Program</td>
<td>To fund activities that protect and conserve the heritage and the environment of the Great Barrier Reef World Heritage Area (the <b><i>heritage area</b></i>) and the Great Barrier Reef catchment area (the <b><i>catchment area</b></i>), including the following:<br>(a) activities to engage communities in the catchment area to enable stewardship of the heritage and catchment areas;<br>(b) research projects designed to address priority planning and management issues in the heritage and catchment areas that are undertaken by eligible students or researchers;<br>(c) activities carried out in the heritage and catchment areas to address one or more of the key threats to the Great Barrier Reef;<br>(d) activities carried out in the heritage area to support reef resilience.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, particularly Articles 4, 5(a), 5(c) and 5(d).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>254</td>
<td>Antarctic Science Foundation</td>
<td>To support Antarctic scientific research by providing funding (including loans) to the Antarctic Science Foundation for purposes relating to the establishment and initial operations of the Foundation, including the following:<br>(a) employing key staff members;<br>(b) meeting the preliminary travel costs of those staff members;<br>(c) publicly launching the Foundation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities:<br>(a) that are carried out in the Australian Antarctic Territory; or<br>(b) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>255</td>
<td>Quality assurance of data relating to students with disabilities</td>
<td>To ensure the quality and consistency of data provided by approved authorities about students with disabilities for the purposes of the <i>Australian Education Act 2013</i> by funding:<br>(a) activities that relate to quality assurance in relation to such data, including contributions to a national quality assurance program; and<br>(b) the publication of educational materials for schools.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to activities:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) involving the collection, analysis, dissemination or use of statistics; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (particularly Article 24(2)); or<br>(d) done in exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(e) funded by way of grants of financial assistance to States and Territories.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>256</td>
<td>Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study and Progress in International Reading Literacy Study</td>
<td>To fund Australia’s involvement in the following international assessments conducted by the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement:<br>(a) Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study;<br>(b) Progress in International Reading Literacy Study.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities relating to external affairs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>258</td>
<td>Water and Snow Safety</td>
<td>To provide support for activities to reduce the impact and incidence of water and snow related injury and death in Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with online communications; or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18, 24 and 31; or<br>(c) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>259</td>
<td>Mental Health—Research</td>
<td>To support infrastructure and research targeted at mental health, and the translation of research into early intervention and prevention strategies, through the funding of activities including:<br>(a) providing capital support for an integrated health care and research facility; and<br>(b) medical research; and<br>(c) public awareness‑raising campaigns in relation to depression; and<br>(d) trials of community‑based and industry sector interventions for depression, anxiety and suicidal behaviour; and<br>(e) developing and implementing online products, including:<br>(i) training and educational products; and<br>(ii) online screening, monitoring and referral tools.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24; or<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8 and 25; or<br>(c) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>260</td>
<td>Naval Shipbuilding College</td>
<td>To facilitate a supply of capable and skilled naval shipbuilding and sustainment workers, including by providing funding for the establishment, development and operation of the Naval Shipbuilding College.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>261</td>
<td>Regional Journalism Scholarships</td>
<td>To provide funding to universities and media training institutions for scholarships to students located in, or connected with, regional areas to undertake study in journalism.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>262</td>
<td>Regional and Small Publishers Cadetships</td>
<td>To provide payments to regional media organisations and small metropolitan publishers to create new jobs in journalism through the provision of cadetships.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>263</td>
<td>Civics and Citizenship Education Initiatives</td>
<td>To support civics and citizenship education in schools and help students to become active and informed citizens by funding the following:<br>(a) the Simpson Prize, an annual competition which encourages students in years 9 and 10 to submit essays and presentations on an Anzac‑related theme, and allows one student from each State and Territory to attend Anzac Day commemorations overseas;<br>(b) the National History Challenge, an annual competition for primary and secondary school students involving a history research challenge, with a number of winners identified, including a Young Historian of the Year;<br>(c) the National Schools Constitutional Convention, held annually in Canberra for selected students in secondary school.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 15;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 31; or<br>(c) in relation to persons, places, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>264</td>
<td>National Career Education Strategy</td>
<td>To assist students to make informed decisions about their study and work options and to enable their effective participation in working life, by funding the development and delivery of training and resources to assist teachers, school leaders and parents to provide career education to children.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support for activities:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services; or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under any of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; or<br>(c) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>265</td>
<td>Primary Connections</td>
<td>To strengthen student interest and engagement in science education and improve the skills and confidence of science teachers by funding the Australian Academy of Science to:<br>(a) further adapt, develop and enhance online curriculum resources for primary schools; and<br>(b) hold professional learning workshops for teachers to support effective use of such resources; and<br>(c) promote the use of such resources in schools.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>266</td>
<td>Science by Doing</td>
<td>To strengthen student interest and engagement in science education and improve the skills and confidence of science teachers by funding the Australian Academy of Science to further develop and enhance online curriculum resources for secondary schools.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>268</td>
<td>Transition support services</td>
<td>To provide (including in cooperation with employers) persons with support and training services relating to transitioning into new employment, including:<br>(a) advisory services in respect of career options, skills in demand, and skills and training assessments; and<br>(b) resilience, health and wellbeing support; and<br>(c) language, literacy and numeracy skills training; and<br>(d) funding for training; and<br>(e) financial education.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to provide unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 6 and 13(2)(b); or<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Employment Policy Convention, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Human Resources Development Convention, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>270</td>
<td>Integrated Carer Support Service</td>
<td>To support carers, including by providing, or facilitating the provision of, the following:<br>(a) information and advice;<br>(b) peer support;<br>(c) education and training;<br>(d) counselling;<br>(e) coaching and mentoring;<br>(f) respite services;<br>(g) financial support.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits, sickness benefits or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 28;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(e) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>271</td>
<td>Social Impact Investment Sector Readiness Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding to build the capability of non‑government organisations and the private sector to create opportunities for, and participate in, the social impact investing market.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) providing, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) to support Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(e) to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5(a) and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6(2), 18(2), 19, 27(3), 28(1) and 29(1);<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8, 16, 19, 26(1) and 27;<br>(iv) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(v) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 7;<br>(vi) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2(1), 6, 11(1), 12(2) and 13(2);<br>(vii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Article 1(1);<br>(viii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1(1) and 2;<br>(ix) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs (as amended), particularly Article 38;<br>(x) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14(4); or<br>(f) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>272</td>
<td>Trialling Innovative Technology</td>
<td>To provide assistance to enable States, Territories, organisations and other entities to develop and deliver trials that test ways of using technology to improve the safety of women experiencing, or at risk of, violence.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) involving electronic communications; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, particularly Articles 2, 5 and 16; or<br>(c) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>273</td>
<td>Redress Scheme for Institutional Child Sexual Abuse—legal services</td>
<td>To:<br>(a) engage a service provider to provide legal services to survivors of institutional child sexual abuse to assist those survivors to access information and advice on their legal options and apply for redress under the Scheme; and<br>(b) provide funding for these services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures undertaken in the exercise of, or which are incidental to, the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>274</td>
<td>Fostering Integration Grants Scheme</td>
<td>To provide funding for the Fostering Integration Grants Scheme, which will assist new migrants to Australia to integrate into Australian social and civil life, while understanding and practising Australian values.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in relation to aliens or immigrants; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 7; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>275</td>
<td>Regional Growth Fund</td>
<td>To support regional and remote communities by providing grants in relation to infrastructure projects that create jobs and encourage economic growth in such communities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6; or<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(c) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(d) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(e) for the construction or extension of railways in any State with the consent of that State; or<br>(f) in relation to postal, telegraphic, telephonic or other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>275A</td>
<td>National Energy Security Assessments</td>
<td>To undertake regular assessments of the resilience of the National Electricity Market, and other energy markets across Australia, to human and environmental threats.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures that are:<br>(a) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>276</td>
<td>Development of improved climate information for the energy sector</td>
<td>To:<br>(a) identify gaps in climate information; and<br>(b) update and maintain Australian national climate change data; and<br>(c) develop and provide resources to support climate risk management.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to providing support for activities:<br>(a) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under any of the following:<br>(i) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4 and 6;<br>(ii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 and 12; or<br>(b) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>277</td>
<td>Skills Checkpoint for Older Workers Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for career guidance and training for older workers to help them remain in the workforce.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6; or<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>278</td>
<td>High Achieving Teachers Program</td>
<td>To fund providers to deliver alternative pathways into teaching, to address teacher shortages and increase the quality of teaching, including by:<br>(a) recruiting and selecting high achieving individuals to be trained as teachers; and<br>(b) partnering with education authorities to place those individuals in preschools, primary schools and secondary schools with identified needs; and<br>(c) providing training and support to the individuals.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13; or<br>(b) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>280</td>
<td>Higher Education Admissions Information Platform</td>
<td>To fund the development, maintenance and ongoing operation of a website which will:<br>(a) provide information about higher education admissions policies and processes; and<br>(b) enable comparison of higher education courses; and<br>(c) enable a centralised national application process for tertiary admissions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>281</td>
<td>Papua New Guinea—cyber security</td>
<td>To establish a sustained partnership on cyber security with Papua New Guinea, including by supporting:<br>(a) Papua New Guinea’s information and communications security preparedness for the 2018 meeting of Asia‑Pacific Economic Cooperation; and<br>(b) other enhancements to Papua New Guinea’s cyber security capabilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>282</td>
<td>MH17 Dutch national prosecution—travel assistance</td>
<td>To provide assistance with travel expenses for the following to observe or participate in the Dutch national prosecution relating to the downing of Malaysia Airlines flight MH17:<br>(a) next of kin of Australians on that flight;<br>(b) nominated support persons of persons mentioned in paragraph (a).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>283</td>
<td>Financial Wellbeing and Capability—commencing 1 January 2019</td>
<td>To support financially vulnerable individuals and families, including Indigenous Australians, by providing funding in relation to:<br>(a) financial and material support for people in financial crisis; and<br>(b) financial counselling, including online and telephone counselling; and<br>(c) measures to improve financial capability, including in relation to budgeting and financial literacy; and<br>(d) facilitating access to microfinance products, including loans, savings programs, business planning and development programs and employment development opportunities; and<br>(e) research and consultation activities, engagement activities and expert advice for the purposes of informing the Commonwealth on issues relating to the financial wellbeing of the Australian community, including issues relating to problem gambling;<br>to the extent that those measures:<br>(f) are with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(g) are with respect to banking, other than State banking (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiii) of the Constitution); or<br>(h) are to assist persons in relation to bankruptcy or insolvency; or<br>(i) are with respect to naturalization or aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(j) are with respect to or incidental to invalid or old‑age pensions (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiii) of the Constitution); or<br>(k) are with respect to or incidental to the provision of maternity allowances, widows’ pensions, child endowment, unemployment benefits, sickness benefits, benefits to students or family allowances (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(l) are to assist Indigenous Australians; or<br>(m) are with respect to immigration or emigration; or<br>(n) give effect to Australia’s obligations under any of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 3 and 4;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4(1)(a) and 28(2);<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18(2), 19 and 27(1);<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2(1), 6(2), 9 and 11(1);<br>(v) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, in particular Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(o) are undertaken by way of grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(p) are undertaken in, or are in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(q) are undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>284</td>
<td>Biosecurity systems improvement, capacity building and training</td>
<td>To strengthen biosecurity in Australia and other countries by addressing biosecurity threats overseas, including by improving the capacity of Australia’s trading partners and other countries to respond to biosecurity threats by assisting officials from those countries to:<br>(a) attend international biosecurity fora in Australia and overseas; and<br>(b) participate in capacity‑building training and other related activities in Australia and overseas.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for activities relating to:<br>(a) interstate or overseas trade and commerce; or<br>(b) quarantine; or<br>(c) aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(e) matters affecting Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>285</td>
<td>Priority pest and disease planning, surveillance and response</td>
<td>To support the following measures to reduce the likelihood of an exotic pest or disease entering Australia and mitigate the impacts of any such pest or disease that succeeds in breaching Australia’s borders:<br>(a) developing and implementing national action plans for Australia’s priority pests and diseases, including developing diagnostic tools and approaches to improve surveillance techniques;<br>(b) intelligence gathering, surveillance and capacity building in other countries for pest and disease control;<br>(c) developing Australia’s diagnostic capacity for identifying plant and animal pests and diseases, including by providing support for the operational costs of the Australian Animal Health Laboratory;<br>(d) the Australian foot and mouth disease vaccine bank;<br>(e) biosecurity‑related activities in areas of Commonwealth responsibility, including certain Territories and Commonwealth‑held land.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in relation to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) for measures in connection with quarantine; or<br>(c) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 8(h); or<br>(e) by way of grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(f) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(g) in, or in relation to, a Commonwealth place; or<br>(h) for activities done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(i) for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>286</td>
<td>Guaranteeing Access to Dental, Mental Health and Emergency Aeromedical Services through the Royal Flying Doctor Service</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Royal Flying Doctor Service to increase the availability of services in rural and remote Australia, including funding to:<br>(a) increase the availability of dental services; and<br>(b) provide access to mental health professionals; and<br>(c) ensure the reach of ambulance services to rural and remote Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical or dental services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>288</td>
<td>Increasing Knowledge—Spinal Muscular Atrophy</td>
<td>To provide funding for resources and training to increase knowledge among medical practitioners and the public about spinal muscular atrophy and referral pathways, including genetic testing, available to persons diagnosed with that condition.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24; or<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>289</td>
<td>Increasing Knowledge—Endometriosis</td>
<td>To fund measures to increase awareness of the condition of endometriosis, its symptoms and possible treatments, including measures to:<br>(a) develop and deliver educational materials about endometriosis for medical professionals; and<br>(b) ensure the professional development of medical professionals in relation to the diagnosis and treatment of endometriosis; and<br>(c) increase the delivery of information about endometriosis in the course of consultations with general practitioners; and<br>(d) disseminate information about endometriosis via electronic communications.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 11 and 12; or<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24; or<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>290</td>
<td>Improving Long‑Term Health in Women with Gestational Diabetes and their Children</td>
<td>To fund measures to improve the long‑term health of women with gestational diabetes and their children, including by:<br>(a) developing and distributing educational materials to encourage such women to undergo testing for type 2 diabetes or the risk of developing type 2 diabetes; and<br>(b) supporting the development and effective delivery of those materials, including by:<br>(i) tailoring and translating the materials for priority cultural groups; and<br>(ii) developing a mobile application; and<br>(iii) undertaking relevant research activities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with telephonic or electronic communications; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) providing, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>291</td>
<td>Healthy Pregnancies</td>
<td>To fund measures to improve the long‑term health of the Australian population, including measures to:<br>(a) develop, disseminate and promote resources and educational materials for pregnant women in relation to managing weight, improving dietary habits and increasing physical activity; and<br>(b) commission research to inform the development of safe pregnancy physical activity guidelines.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>292</td>
<td>Rural and Remote Health Infrastructure Projects</td>
<td>To provide grants for health infrastructure projects in regional and remote areas.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) to or in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(ii) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 5; or<br>(c) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) in or in relation to a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>293</td>
<td>Biosimilar Education and Electronic Prescribing</td>
<td>To fund the following:<br>(a) an organisation to develop information and educational materials and modules for clinicians, pharmacists and consumers to support the uptake of biosimilar medicines;<br>(b) an organisation to develop and deliver information and educational activities for health professionals, other health service providers and consumers to support the uptake of biosimilar medicines;<br>(c) the development of software to support the uptake of generic and biosimilar medicines;<br>(d) the enhancement of software to improve quality prescribing and enhance management of the availability of medicines, pharmacovigilance, safety reporting and compliance with the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme;<br>(e) the enhancement of software to support the safe management and supply of controlled drugs.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 11; or<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(iii) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs (as amended), particularly Articles 2 and 4; or<br>(d) taken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>294</td>
<td>Elder Abuse Service Trials</td>
<td>To fund trials of the following specialist services to prevent, identify and respond to elder abuse:<br>(a) specialist elder abuse units comprising lawyers and social workers who provide services tailored to individuals’ needs (which may include legal advice, counselling, or referral and support to access other services);<br>(b) health justice partnerships, which would assist older persons in the health care system, identified by health care workers or social workers as being at risk or potentially subjected to elder abuse, to access specialised legal support services;<br>(c) case management and mediation services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8 and 16;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 17 and 26; or<br>(b) for services that are specifically targeted to assist Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people; or<br>(c) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>295</td>
<td>Location Incentive Funding Program</td>
<td>To fund the Location Incentive Funding Program to attract large‑budget film and television productions to Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to funding activities:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, or other like services; or<br>(c) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>296</td>
<td>Indigenous Languages and Arts Program</td>
<td>To assist Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to access and participate in Indigenous cultural expression by funding activities relating to Indigenous languages and Indigenous arts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>297</td>
<td>Supporting Sustainable Access to Drinking Water</td>
<td>To assist individuals and businesses affected by per‑ and poly‑fluoroalkyl substance contamination resulting from activities at Army Aviation Centre Oakey, Royal Australian Air Force Base Williamtown, Royal Australian Air Force Base Tindal and Royal Australian Air Force Base Pearce by funding the provision of sustainable access to drinking water and necessary water infrastructure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>298</td>
<td>Jobs and Market Fund</td>
<td>To promote the effective operation of the National Disability Insurance Scheme, the <i>Aged Care Act 1997</i> and the <i>Veterans’ Entitlement Act 1986</i> by funding activities directed to:<br>(a) increasing the number and capability of disability support, aged care and veterans’ care service providers and workers; and<br>(b) ensuring that there are sufficient disability support, aged care and veterans’ care service providers and workers to service all areas of need.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to support veterans and their families; or<br>(c) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical, sickness and hospital benefits, medical services and dental services, and benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 3, 4, 9, 19, 20, 25 and 26; or<br>(e) that are specifically targeted to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people; or<br>(f) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>299</td>
<td>Endeavour Leadership Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance for the following:<br>(a) persons within the tertiary sector to study or undertake research overseas;<br>(b) non‑citizens to study or undertake research at Australian institutions or organisations.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>300</td>
<td>Prioritising mental health—aftercare following a suicide attempt</td>
<td>To fund Primary Health Networks and beyondblue to deliver, in partnership with Local Hospital Networks, the Way Back Support Service across Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to support veterans and defence force members and their families; or<br>(b) to provide services to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) to provide services to individuals living in a Territory; or<br>(e) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>301</td>
<td>Prioritising mental health—suicide prevention campaign</td>
<td>To provide funding to SANE Australia to develop and trial a suicide prevention campaign aimed at people who are contemplating suicide, including funding to:<br>(a) develop a campaign based on real‑life stories from people who have attempted suicide to convey positive messages of hope; and<br>(b) disseminate campaign materials and messaging via social media, television and radio communications; and<br>(c) test the efficacy of peer to peer storytelling as a suicide prevention strategy; and<br>(d) disseminate information about suicide and resources to support families, friends, carers and colleagues of people who are contemplating suicide.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>302</td>
<td>Prioritising mental health—Lifeline Australia—enhanced telephone and online crisis service</td>
<td>To fund Lifeline Australia for the delivery and enhancement of a 24‑hour telephone and online crisis support and suicide prevention service.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with telephonic or electronic communications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>303</td>
<td>Regional Airport Security Screening Funding</td>
<td>To provide funding to regional airports to meet security screening requirements, including through grants for:<br>(a) purchasing security screening technology; and<br>(b) infrastructure costs associated with accommodating new security screening technology.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and of the States; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on International Civil Aviation, particularly Annex 17.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>304</td>
<td>Regional Employment Trials Program</td>
<td>To undertake measures directed at assisting job seekers in particular areas of disadvantage through providing employment and related services that assist job seekers to find and keep a job with suitable employers, including:<br>(a) training, mentoring and support services; and<br>(b) engaging employment facilitators to assist with the delivery of these measures.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2(1) and 6(2);<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>305</td>
<td>National Return of Unwanted Medicines Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for a national collection and disposal service to consumers for expired or unwanted medicines, including:<br>(a) to coordinate the collection, and subsequent transport and disposal, of returned medicines from community pharmacies; and<br>(b) to ensure the proper and safe disposal of medicines; and<br>(c) to increase awareness amongst consumers, pharmacists and other health professionals regarding the availability of the service.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits or medical services; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>306</td>
<td>Quality use of Diagnostics, Therapeutics and Pathology Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to improve the way in which health technologies, medicines and medical tests are prescribed and used, including:<br>(a) to develop and deliver educational materials on the appropriate use of medicines; and<br>(b) to provide appropriate healthcare interventions to promote the appropriate use of subsidised diagnostics, therapeutics and pathology; and<br>(c) to promote free access to information about the judicious and safe use of diagnostics, therapeutics and pathology; and<br>(d) to develop and provide tools and resources aimed at ensuring the appropriate, safe and efficacious use of medicines and health technologies; and<br>(e) to provide education and awareness activities, events, conferences and symposiums on the safe and appropriate use of medicines.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>308</td>
<td>Community Skills and Development Program</td>
<td>To support the community that is selected to host the National Radioactive Waste Management Facility (the <b><i>Facility</b></i>) as follows:<br>(a) to build economic resilience, capacity and skills for the purposes of:<br>(i) realising benefits from the construction of the Facility; or<br>(ii) supporting the Facility’s long‑term operation;<br>(b) to protect and promote local Indigenous culture and heritage.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to measures:<br>(a) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under the Joint Convention on the Safety of Spent Fuel Management and on the Safety of Radioactive Waste Management, particularly Articles 1 and 11; or<br>(b) in relation to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>309</td>
<td>National Aerial Firefighting Program</td>
<td>To fund a national firefighting body to provide, in association with the States and Territories, the national aerial firefighting program, including:<br>(a) to procure, maintain and coordinate a fleet of specialised firefighting aircraft, to be used by the States and Territories in combating bushfires across Australia; and<br>(b) to fund costs directly or indirectly associated with procuring, maintaining or coordinating those aircraft; and<br>(c) to develop national protocols and systems for aerial firefighting.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>310</td>
<td>Communities Combating Pests and Weed Impacts During Drought</td>
<td>To fund local councils or consortia of local councils to employ people to undertake pest and weed management activities in drought‑affected areas.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with quarantine; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(i) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 8(h);<br>(ii) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa, particularly Article 5; or<br>(c) provided by way of grants of financial assistance to States and Territories; or<br>(d) peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>312</td>
<td>Preparing for Automated Vehicles</td>
<td>To prepare Australia for, and support, the timely and safe introduction of automated vehicles in Australia, including by:<br>(a) facilitating Australian industry development in vehicle automation and related technologies; and<br>(b) facilitating the establishment of appropriate physical and digital infrastructure for automated vehicles; and<br>(c) increasing public awareness about automated vehicles and the impacts (including social and economic) of the introduction of automated vehicles.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to supporting arrangements:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(c) involving places, matters or things outside the geographical limits of Australia or Australia’s relations with other countries; or<br>(d) in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(e) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>313</td>
<td>Visions of Australia</td>
<td>To increase access for Australian audiences to exhibitions of quality Australian arts and cultural material, with a particular focus on regional and remote Australia.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>314</td>
<td>Festivals Australia</td>
<td>To fund individual arts projects that are part of a festival or significant one‑off community celebration in regional or remote Australia, so as to promote access to arts projects, support partnerships and collaboration across the arts sector and encourage community participation in arts projects at those festivals and celebrations.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>315</td>
<td>Indigenous Visual Arts Industry Support</td>
<td>To support:<br>(a) the Indigenous visual arts industry; and<br>(b) the continued production, exhibition, critique, purchase and collection of Indigenous visual art;<br>including through funding Indigenous arts centres, marketing events, regional hubs and service organisations, and supporting professional opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists and arts workers.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>316</td>
<td>Emerging Markets Impact Investment Fund</td>
<td>To help small and medium‑sized enterprises in developing countries to access finance, thereby assisting such countries to reduce poverty and achieve sustainable development.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>317</td>
<td>Specialist Dementia Care Program</td>
<td>To provide grants to organisations and the States and Territories to deliver care and services or other support to eligible care recipients, including specialist care for people exhibiting very severe behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to provide, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 25, 26 and 28; or<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>318</td>
<td>beyondblue National Depression and Anxiety Initiative</td>
<td>To fund Beyond Blue Limited to reduce the impact of depression, anxiety and related disorders in Australia, including by:<br>(a) implementing measures to increase awareness of, and reduce stigma associated with, depression, anxiety and related disorders; and<br>(b) implementing measures to enhance the capacity of individuals and communities to respond to depression, anxiety and related disorders, including by the following:<br>(i) developing and delivering tools, resources, information and workplace mental health programs;<br>(ii) providing advice and support services;<br>(iii) encouraging people to seek support and to access primary mental health care;<br>(iv) entering into and promoting partnerships with other entities (including businesses, the community sector and the media);<br>(v) providing advice and support to other entities that are conducting public awareness raising campaigns or initiatives which encourage people to seek treatment for depression, anxiety and related disorders; and<br>(c) developing and delivering training and support for professionals providing services to people experiencing depression, anxiety and related disorders; and<br>(d) commissioning research into, and disseminating knowledge of, the causes of, and treatments for, depression, anxiety and related disorders; and<br>(e) undertaking research and providing advice to the Commonwealth in relation to depression, anxiety and related disorders; and<br>(f) conducting trials of ways of preventing, detecting, treating and managing depression, anxiety and related disorders; and<br>(g) commissioning an independent evaluation of Commonwealth funded activities conducted by Beyond Blue Limited.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) supporting activities in connection with telephonic or electronic communications; or<br>(b) collecting data and otherwise conducting research for the purpose of informing the Commonwealth; or<br>(c) giving effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 5, 8 and 25; or<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>319</td>
<td>Fisheries Assistance and User Engagement Funding Program</td>
<td>To provide ongoing funding and support for fishers and other users of areas of sea that, under the <i>Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999</i>, are declared as Commonwealth reserves, where:<br>(a) the areas of sea are outside Australia and are in Commonwealth marine areas; and<br>(b) the funding and support is for the fishers and other users to:<br>(i) adjust to changes in access and regulatory requirements resulting from new or revised zoning arrangements in those Commonwealth reserves; or<br>(ii) engage in projects that further the objects of those Commonwealth reserves.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>320</td>
<td>Murray‑Darling Basin Economic Development Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to communities in the Murray‑Darling Basin to offset the detrimental economic effects on those communities associated with the following:<br>(a) measures to protect and restore environmental assets of the Murray‑Darling Basin;<br>(b) measures to assist in achieving the environmental outcomes of the <i>Basin Plan 2012</i> relating to ecosystem function, biodiversity, water quality and salinity and water resource health;<br>(c) the recovery of environmental water from the Basin water resources, including through the purchase of water access entitlements to implement long‑term average sustainable diversion limits.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of Japan for the Protection of Migratory Birds and Birds in Danger of Extinction and their Environment, particularly Articles III(1), IV(3), V and VI(a);<br>(b) the Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of the People’s Republic of China for the Protection of Migratory Birds and their Environment, particularly Articles III(3) and IV(a) and (b);<br>(c) the Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of the Republic of Korea on the Protection of Migratory Birds, particularly Articles 3(3), 4 and 5(a);<br>(d) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6(b) and 8(a), (b), (d) and (f);<br>(e) the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals, particularly Article III;<br>(f) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Articles 3(1) and 4;<br>(g) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 4(2) and 5;<br>(h) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4(1)(d), (e) and (f).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>321</td>
<td>Established Pest Animals and Weeds Management Pipeline</td>
<td>To support activities directed at combating Australia’s established pest animal and weed species, including the following:<br>(a) research and development;<br>(b) the implementation of measures to support the control of established pest animals and weeds;<br>(c) national coordination;<br>(d) the provision of key infrastructure.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(c) for measures in connection with quarantine; or<br>(d) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 8(h); or<br>(e) for activities done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(f) by way of grants of financial assistance to States or Territories; or<br>(g) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(h) for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>322</td>
<td>Biosecurity Innovation Program</td>
<td>To support the identification, development and implementation of innovative technologies to enhance the capacity of Australia’s national biosecurity system to manage biosecurity risk.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(c) for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>323</td>
<td>Environmental Biosecurity Protection Fund</td>
<td>To support investment in projects that support planning and preparedness for management of the environmental biosecurity risks relating to the following:<br>(a) priority diseases;<br>(b) invasive pests that threaten native ecosystems, habitats or species.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) in connection with quarantine; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 8(h).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>324</td>
<td>Biosecurity Incident Contingency Funding</td>
<td>To support the following measures directed at strengthening Australia’s capacity to respond to biosecurity incidents:<br>(a) biosecurity‑related activities in areas of Commonwealth responsibility, including certain Territories and Commonwealth‑held land;<br>(b) grants of financial assistance to States and Territories to support cost‑shared activities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in, or in relation to, a Commonwealth place; or<br>(b) by way of grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>325</td>
<td>Advanced Welding Training Centre</td>
<td>To support the establishment and operation of an advanced welding training centre as a measure to train and upskill apprentices and workers.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to engaging in measures to meet Australia’s obligations under the following:<br>(a) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, in particular Articles 1 and 2;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, in particular Articles 1, 2 and 4;<br>(c) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, in particular Articles 2 and 6(2).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>326</td>
<td>High Level Panel for a Sustainable Ocean Economy</td>
<td>To participate in and contribute to the work of the High Level Panel for a Sustainable Ocean Economy (the <b><i>Panel</b></i>), including by funding activities related to the following:<br>(a) addressing the issue of marine plastic pollution, including by removing plastics from the supply chain and supporting alternatives to plastic;<br>(b) supporting development of environmental‑economic ocean accounts;<br>(c) supporting the engagement of representatives of participating countries in the work of the Panel.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for:<br>(a) activities relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries, or<br>(b) measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>327</td>
<td>National online safety awareness campaign</td>
<td>To conduct an awareness campaign focused on keeping children safe online, and to promote the role of the eSafety Commissioner.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 17, 19, 34 and 36.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>328</td>
<td>Television retransmission at Stroud</td>
<td>To provide funding for television transmission infrastructure to address reception issues relating to atmospheric ducting at Stroud.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>329</td>
<td>Career Revive Initiative for Regional Women—supporting women to continue their careers after caring‑related breaks</td>
<td>To facilitate women in regional areas to transition back into the workforce following a caring‑related break, by:<br>(a) providing assistance to specific employers in regional areas to identify barriers in their workplaces to women returning to the workforce and to develop employer action plans to address those barriers; and<br>(b) funding the development of publicly available resources to guide other employers to take the actions referred to in paragraph (a); and<br>(c) engaging an employer peak body or business chamber to promote the Career Revive Initiative and encourage employers to take steps to assist women to return to work, including those steps identified in the publicly available resources referred to in paragraph (b).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; or<br>(b) to meet Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3, 11 and 14;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>330</td>
<td>Australian Apprenticeships Incentives Program</td>
<td>To provide payments to apprentices, employers of apprentices and registered training organisations, to encourage and support the commencement and completion of apprenticeships.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) to provide sickness benefits, and benefits to students; or<br>(b) that gives effect to Australia’s obligations under any of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 27;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>331</td>
<td>Positive Partnerships Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to improve the educational outcomes of children with autism spectrum disorder by providing:<br>(a) training and resources for teachers and other school staff, to assist them to facilitate the development of those children; and<br>(b) training and resources for parents and carers of those children, to assist them to facilitate the development of those children; and<br>(c) a website containing online learning modules and other resources.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18, 23, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 5, 7, 8 and 24.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>332</td>
<td>Music and Arts Education Initiatives</td>
<td>To promote participation and engagement in music education by Australian students, and to improve the quality of music and arts education and the skills of music and arts teachers by:<br>(a) funding Music Australia to deliver the ‘Music: Count Us In’ initiative, which provides the following:<br>(i) an opportunity for student participation in music education programs and a national event at which students sing a song at the same time;<br>(ii) professional support for music classes;<br>(iii) online resources and support services; and<br>(b) funding The Song Room Limited to deliver the ‘Engaged Learning through the Arts’ project which involves:<br>(i) the development of online curriculum resources for all schools through a digital education platform; and<br>(ii) the implementation of arts education programs in disadvantaged schools without music or arts teachers.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services; or<br>(b) for the provision of benefits to students; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 15;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Article 31; or<br>(d) for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>333</td>
<td>Social Impact Investing</td>
