<td>To facilitate social impact investing by:<br>(a) conducting; and<br>(b) evaluating; and<br>(c) undertaking research related to;<br>social impact investing activities directed to one or more of the following outcomes:<br>(d) providing support to Indigenous Australians;<br>(e) preventing or addressing issues of discrimination and violence against women;<br>(f) providing unemployed and underemployed people with the skills and training necessary to find paid employment or additional paid employment;<br>(g) providing unemployed and underemployed people with loans to assist them to set up microenterprises;<br>(h) reducing homelessness;<br>(i) supporting the education and development of children, including by assisting their parents and legal guardians in the performance of their child‑rearing responsibilities;<br>(j) supporting people with disability to ensure and promote the full realisation of all human rights and fundamental freedoms;<br>(k) providing support to non‑citizens to improve their wellbeing and encourage their independence;<br>(l) preventing, treating and reducing the impact of substance misuse.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xi) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to banking, other than State banking (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiii) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) providing, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits and medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(f) to support Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(g) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under any of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5, 10, 11 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18, 19, 27, 28 and 29;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8, 16, 19, 26 and 27;<br>(iv) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(v) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 7;<br>(vi) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 11, 12 and 13;<br>(vii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(viii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4;<br>(ix) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs (as amended), particularly Articles 4 and 38;<br>(x) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14; or<br>(h) with respect to matters incidental to the execution of any of the legislative powers of the Parliament or the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(i) in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(j) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>335</td>
<td>Delivery of an integrated information service for Australian Apprenticeships</td>
<td>To provide funding to an entity:<br>(a) to provide information about apprenticeships and traineeships, including through a website, social media, email, mobile phone applications and an 1800 free‑call service; and<br>(b) to explain how to use those services to access information about apprenticeships and traineeships; and<br>(c) to compile and publish statistics on apprenticeships and traineeships.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xi) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>336</td>
<td>Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific</td>
<td>To support the development or enhancement of infrastructure that will be, or is:<br>(a) located wholly or substantially in the Pacific region (excluding Australia) or Timor‑Leste; or<br>(b) used wholly or substantially in the Pacific region (excluding Australia) or Timor‑Leste<br>(irrespective of where the infrastructure is located).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>337</td>
<td>Overseas Adoption Services</td>
<td>To provide support for:<br>(a) persons ordinarily resident in Australia who were adopted from a foreign country; and<br>(b) children who are being adopted from a foreign country by adoptive families ordinarily resident in Australia; and<br>(c) the adoptive families of persons mentioned in paragraphs (a) and (b);<br>by providing the following:<br>(d) counselling, relationship education and support to address family relationship issues arising in connection with undertaking an overseas adoption process;<br>(e) counselling, relationship education and support to address past adoption experiences that can be characterised as preventing or treating a mental illness;<br>(f) information, counselling and support to overseas adoptees and their adoptive families in relation to the process of tracing biological family.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) in relation to the provision of sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 7, 18, 21 and 23;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Protection of Children and Co‑operation in Respect of Intercountry Adoption, particularly Articles 5 and 9;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 10 and 12;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 23; or<br>(d) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>338</td>
<td>Continuity of Support—Community Mental Health Services</td>
<td>To fund Primary Health Networks to provide support and care for persons with mental illness who are ineligible for the National Disability Insurance Scheme.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) which provide, or are incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 19, 25 and 26;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>339</td>
<td>Social Impact Investing—Payment by Outcomes Trials (supporting employment opportunities for unemployed or underemployed persons)</td>
<td>To provide funding to non‑government or private sector organisations to conduct and evaluate the effect of measures that are directed to achieving either or both of the following outcomes:<br>(a) supporting unemployed and underemployed persons into employment by providing those persons with educational and training programs, and other support, directly related to helping them to find paid employment;<br>(b) supporting the development of microenterprises by, and therefore employment opportunities for, unemployed and underemployed persons.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under any of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 11 and 12;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning the Organisation of the Employment Service, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>340</td>
<td>Social Impact Investing—Payment by Outcomes Trials (supporting the development and wellbeing of children)</td>
<td>To give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6(2), 18(2), 19, 27(3), 28(1) and 29(1), by providing funding to non‑government or private sector organisations to conduct and evaluate the effect of projects that support the development and wellbeing of children, including by building skills of parents and guardians to further the development of the children in their care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>341</td>
<td>Safe places for women and children affected by domestic and family violence</td>
<td>To fund:<br>(a) the construction, alteration, extension or renovation of emergency accommodation for women and children affected by domestic and family violence; and<br>(b) the supply or installation of facilities or equipment related to such accommodation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 19, 34 and 36;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 11;<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 6, 15 and 16; or<br>(b) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>342</td>
<td>Specialised family violence services</td>
<td>Both of the following:<br>(a) to prevent domestic and family violence and to support victims of such violence by delivering:<br>(i) support and assistance to victims of domestic and family violence; and<br>(ii) assistance to perpetrators of domestic and family violence to change their violent behaviour; and<br>(iii) education campaigns directed at preventing domestic and family violence; and<br>(iv) education to individuals and groups about domestic and family violence, including by delivering education programs about being in healthy and non‑violent relationships; and<br>(v) support for families affected by domestic and family violence;<br>(b) to prevent domestic and family violence in Indigenous communities and to support Indigenous victims of such violence by delivering the support, assistance and education mentioned in subparagraphs (a)(i) to (iv) in a manner targeted to Indigenous persons.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) which provide, or are incidental to the provision of, medical services, or unemployment, or sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 19, 34 and 36;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 11 and 12;<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 6, 15 and 16;<br>(v) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7 and 9; or<br>(e) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(f) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>343</td>
<td>Conducting and disseminating research into domestic, family and sexual violence</td>
<td>Conducting research for the Commonwealth into the prevalence of, attitudes towards and interventions that reduce domestic and family violence, and sexual violence, and disseminating such research, including online.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 19, 34 and 36;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7 and 9;<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 6, 15 and 16; or<br>(d) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(e) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>344</td>
<td>Support for Trafficked People Program</td>
<td>To provide legal, medical, housing and other support to people who are reasonably suspected of being victims, and people who are reasonably considered to be at risk of becoming victims, of offences under Division 270 or 271 of the <i>Criminal Code</i>, including where those people are referred from a community service provider or from the Australian Federal Police.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for measures:<br>(a) which provide, or are incidental to the provision of, medical services, or unemployment, pharmaceutical or sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to immigration or emigration; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the United Nations Convention Against Transnational Organized Crime, particularly Articles 1, 25, 26, 27 and 31;<br>(ii) the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children, supplementing the United Nations Convention Against Transnational Organized Crime, particularly Articles 1, 6 and 9;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 19, 32, 34, 35 and 36;<br>(v) the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on the Sale of Children, Child Prostitution and Child Pornography, particularly Articles 8 and 9;<br>(vi) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 8 and 23;<br>(vii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 10 and 11;<br>(viii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention Concerning Forced or Compulsory Labour, particularly Article 1;<br>(ix) the International Convention to Suppress the Slave Trade and Slavery, particularly Article 2;<br>(x) the Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery, the Slave Trade, and Institutions and Practices Similar to Slavery, particularly Article 1; or<br>(f) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>345</td>
<td>Implementation of the Fourth Action Plan to Reduce Violence against Women and Children</td>
<td>To prevent domestic, family and sexual violence and reduce the effect of such violence by the following:<br>(a) developing a national strategy to prevent domestic, family and sexual violence, in coordination with the States and Territories and non‑government organisations;<br>(b) establishing a prevention hub to bring together governments, experts, the community sector and corporate partners to oversee, coordinate and target prevention measures;<br>(c) funding measures designed to change attitudes supportive of domestic, family and sexual violence against women and children, and effectively reduce the incidence and impact of such violence in Australia;<br>(d) delivering training for students, workers and volunteers to assist them to support women and children who are at risk of, or are victims of, domestic, family and sexual violence;<br>(e) supporting the development of community‑led strategies to prevent domestic, family and sexual violence, including for women and children, disabled people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and Indigenous people;<br>(f) providing training, advice and resources to journalists and media professionals to improve reporting of domestic, family and sexual violence;<br>(g) developing, disseminating and promoting national standards:<br>(i) for first responders, other workers and volunteers to use when responding to victims of sexual violence; and<br>(ii) for the support of victims of sexual violence; and<br>(iii) for the rehabilitation of perpetrators of sexual violence.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) with respect to immigrants or aliens; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 19, 34 and 36;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7 and 9;<br>(iv) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 6, 15 and 16; or<br>(e) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(f) taken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>348</td>
<td>Regional Connectivity Program</td>
<td>To provide funding:<br>(a) for telecommunications infrastructure; and<br>(b) for a trial of the provision of telephone services in regional and remote areas through innovative technologies; and<br>(c) for the provision of assistance and advice relating to the use of digital technologies and applications, through the development of websites, the delivery of online resources and tools, and by a telephone service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>349</td>
<td>New Employment Services Trial</td>
<td>To conduct a trial of a new employment services model to help job seekers find and keep a job.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to a measure:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) involving the provision of unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution), or incidental to the provision of those benefits; or<br>(c) taken in or in relation to a Territory; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning the Organisation of the Employment Service, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6(2).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>350</td>
<td>Prime Minister’s Literary Awards and Prize for Australian History</td>
<td>To support, and to promote participation and reward excellence in, Australian arts and culture in the field of literature, by providing national prizes and awards for achievement, including:<br>(a) the Prime Minister’s Literary Awards; and<br>(b) the Prize for Australian History.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to engaging in measures for these purposes that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>351</td>
<td>Prevention of Financial Abuse of Women</td>
<td>To fund measures directed at preventing and responding to the financial abuse of women, and supporting women’s economic independence, including by providing funding to do the following:<br>(a) identify resources currently being used, and measures currently being undertaken, to achieve these objectives;<br>(b) engage with community, public and private sector organisations around measures to achieve these objectives;<br>(c) implement appropriate measures to achieve these objectives on a national scale;<br>(d) develop community education initiatives (including through online channels) to achieve these objectives.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under Articles 2(e) and (f), 5(a) and 16 of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>352</td>
<td>Energy Efficient Communities Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to support businesses and community organisations to reduce energy use, improve energy productivity and deliver carbon abatement, including through:<br>(a) upgrading equipment to reduce energy consumption; and<br>(b) undertaking energy management activities and assessments, such as energy systems assessments and feasibility studies; and<br>(c) investing in energy monitoring and management systems; and<br>(d) supporting the use of renewable energy by community organisations.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to supporting activities that would assist Australia to give effect to its obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4;<br>(b) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 3 and 10;<br>(c) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>353</td>
<td>Australian Heritage Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide grants for activities to assist in the protection and promotion of the following places and properties:<br>(a) National Heritage places (within the meaning of the <i>Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999</i>);<br>(b) Commonwealth Heritage places (within the meaning of that Act);<br>(c) Australian properties on the World Heritage List kept under Article 11 of the Convention for the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage (the <b><i>Convention</b></i>).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention, particularly Articles 4 and 5; or<br>(b) for activities that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(d) of financial assistance to a State; or<br>(e) for activities in, or in relation to, a Commonwealth place; or<br>(f) for activities in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>354</td>
<td>Communities Environment Program</td>
<td>To provide grants for community projects that target environmental priorities relating to waste, threatened species, natural habitats, and coasts, wetlands and waterways.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) for activities in relation to places, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under international agreements; or<br>(c) for activities in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>355</td>
<td>Environment Restoration Fund</td>
<td>To support environmental restoration and protection projects directed at the following:<br>(a) protecting Australia’s coasts and coastal waterways;<br>(b) the clean‑up, recovery and recycling of waste;<br>(c) protecting threatened and migratory species and their habitat.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 6(a);<br>(ii) the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals, particularly Article III(4)(a);<br>(iii) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Article 3(1); or<br>(b) for activities that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) for activities in relation to places, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) for activities in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>356</td>
<td>Disability Royal Commission and Other Support Services</td>
<td>To provide funding for entities to provide one or more of the following:<br>(a) support services (including advocacy services) to assist persons to make submissions to, and appear before, the Royal Commission into Violence, Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation of People with Disability;<br>(b) support services (including counselling and referral services) to assist persons traumatised or otherwise affected, directly or indirectly, by:<br>(i) violence towards a person with a disability; or<br>(ii) the abuse, neglect or exploitation of a person with a disability; or<br>(iii) the Royal Commission, whether or not they participate in it;<br>(c) support services of the kind mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b) that are designed to meet the specific needs of Indigenous Australians;<br>(d) training, including training materials, to those who provide the services mentioned in paragraph (a), (b) or (c).<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 16 and 29;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 23 and 24;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(e) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>357</td>
<td>Skills Organisations</td>
<td>To provide funding for the development, trial and assessment of methods and standards (including standards for the endorsement of training providers) for vocational education and training that supports the needs of industry.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4; or<br>(b) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>358</td>
<td>Destination Australia Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to registered higher education providers (within the meaning of the <i>Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency Act 2011</i>), and registered training organisations (within the meaning of the <i>National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011</i>), in regional or remote areas of Australia to:<br>(a) provide scholarships to domestic and international students; and<br>(b) promote those scholarships; and<br>(c) promote higher education, and vocational education and training, in regional and remote areas of Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures or activities:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the State and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services; or<br>(c) relating to aliens; or<br>(d) for the provision of benefits to students; or<br>(e) relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(f) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(g) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>359</td>
<td>Foundation Skills for Your Future Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for the development and delivery of skills training in language, literacy, numeracy and digital literacy to facilitate the participation of training recipients in further training or the workforce.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>361</td>
<td>Additional Employment Support for Veterans</td>
<td>To fund measures to help veterans and other former defence force members find employment, including measures to:<br>(a) fund organisations to provide support (including counselling, vocational education and case management) to veterans and former deference force members and their families; and<br>(b) support employers to hire veterans and former defence force members; and<br>(c) encourage and promote the benefits of employing veterans and former defence force members.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) supporting any or all of the following:<br>(i) veterans;<br>(ii) defence force members;<br>(iii) the families of veterans and defence force members;<br>(iv) the communities of veterans and defence force members; or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>362</td>
<td>Research, tools and strategies to boost Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages education</td>
<td>To support the teaching and learning of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages in schools, including by providing funding to:<br>(a) conduct research into best‑practice resources and models for such teaching and learning; and<br>(b) develop resources and a national workforce strategy to support such teaching and learning; and<br>(c) develop and provide professional development courses to support such teaching and learning.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) for, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>363</td>
<td>International Cultural Diplomacy Arts Fund</td>
<td>To support international arts and cultural activities, including by funding measures:<br>(a) to fulfil Australia’s international commitments in relation to arts and culture, including by making payments to international organisations; and<br>(b) to support the cooperation and collaboration of Australian and international arts and cultural practitioners; and<br>(c) to support international residencies, exchanges and touring by Australian artists; and<br>(d) to support residencies and exchanges in Australia, and touring to Australia, by overseas artists; and<br>(e) to support Australia’s foreign and diplomatic relations through the use of Australian arts and culture, including through meetings and cultural dialogue; and<br>(f) to provide assistance to Australian artists to help them access foreign audiences and markets; and<br>(g) to support international arts and cultural forums, festivals and other events; and<br>(h) to support research in relation to international arts and cultural activities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries (within the meaning of paragraph 51(i) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>364</td>
<td>Veterans’ Wellbeing Centres Program</td>
<td>To provide grants to improve access to government and non‑government support services for veterans and their families through:<br>(a) the establishment, including the construction, redevelopment or extension, of buildings and related facilities, for veterans’ wellbeing centres; and<br>(b) the administration and operation of those centres; and<br>(c) the provision of support services through those centres.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>365</td>
<td>Women in Aviation</td>
<td>To foster and improve the participation of women in the aviation industry, including by providing funding to develop and implement measures that:<br>(a) expand and promote career opportunities for, and the participation of, women in the aviation industry; and<br>(b) increase awareness of such opportunities, and interest in the aviation industry, among women and girls.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories (within the meaning of paragraph 51(i) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 10, 11 and 14;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 3 and 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>366</td>
<td>Industry Training Hubs</td>
<td>To increase participation of young people (including school students) in vocational education and training, and to create better employment pathways for those young people, by supporting the establishment of vocational education and training hubs, including by providing funding for the following:<br>(a) costs associated with establishing and operating the hubs;<br>(b) engaging persons to build relationships between industry, schools and other educational institutions;<br>(c) developing and delivering training and other support for those young people to assist them to gain skills relevant to the trades sector;<br>(d) developing and delivering training to persons to enable them to better assist those young people.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Article 28;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 6;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4; or<br>(c) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>367</td>
<td>Regional Agricultural Show Development Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide grants for the construction, upgrade, maintenance or purchase of:<br>(a) agricultural showground infrastructure in regional areas; or<br>(b) other infrastructure and related assets that will enhance agricultural shows, or the capacity of show societies, in regional areas.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories (within the meaning of paragraph 51(i) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) in connection with assisting Australia to give effect to its obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 15; or<br>(c) to provide for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) as financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(e) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>368</td>
<td>Agriculture Stewardship Package</td>
<td>To promote the adoption of sustainable agriculture practices across Australia and in particular to develop and implement the following:<br>(a) a Sustainable Agriculture Policy directed at sustainable agricultural practices and biodiversity outcomes;<br>(b) an Agricultural Stewardship Program to support sustainable agriculture practices, including by funding projects to deliver on‑farm outcomes to enhance conservation and protect biodiversity;<br>(c) a Sustainable Agriculture Extension Program to increase farmers’ awareness of the benefits of implementing particular practices on their farms, including by providing grants to organisations to disseminate information about sustainable farming practices.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12;<br>(ii) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 5 and 10; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>369</td>
<td>Educating Kids about Agriculture</td>
<td>To provide grants for activities directed at increasing children’s understanding of:<br>(a) where and how their food and fibre are produced; and<br>(b) the role and importance of agriculture to Australia’s way of life, regional communities and the economy.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 28.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>370</td>
<td>National Farm Safety Education Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding to promote and support activities relating to safety in the agriculture, fisheries and forestry sectors, including:<br>(a) developing a strategy with key targets for fund investments; and<br>(b) developing safety resources to educate farm, fishing and forestry businesses on best practice; and<br>(c) developing initiatives to improve safety and safety culture; and<br>(d) building partnerships between industry and regulators in these sectors.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>373</td>
<td>Package Assisting Small Exporters</td>
<td>To provide support for small exporters to engage in overseas trade and commerce, including supporting small exporters to:<br>(a) overcome barriers to their participation in overseas trade and commerce; and<br>(b) identify and make use of opportunities to participate in overseas trade and commerce;<br>by funding projects aimed at improving market access for small exporters.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>375</td>
<td>National Orphanage Museum</td>
<td>To provide funding to support:<br>(a) the establishment of a national orphanage museum; and<br>(b) capital works at the national orphanage museum; and<br>(c) the operational costs of the national orphanage museum;<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit for the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>376</td>
<td>Community Languages Multicultural Grants</td>
<td>To provide funding to support community languages schools to teach school‑aged children to speak a foreign language, including by providing funding for the following:<br>(a) operating costs of the schools;<br>(b) the development and provision of curriculums, teaching materials and other educational supports to be used by the schools;<br>(c) the development and provision of teacher training activities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to giving effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Article 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>377</td>
<td>National Product Stewardship Investment Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding to support projects to:<br>(a) accelerate the development of new national industry‑led product stewardship schemes (<b><i>national schemes</b></i>); and<br>(b) improve recycling rates under new or existing national schemes.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for projects that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and which cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>378</td>
<td>Pacific Secondary School Scholarships Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for scholarships and other support for secondary school students from Papua New Guinea and other Pacific island countries to study in Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific; or<br>(e) for activities done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>379</td>
<td>Regional Airports Program</td>
<td>To provide grants for works (including repairs and upgrades) to improve safety and access at airports, and aerodromes, in regional and remote areas of Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) for measures undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory; or<br>(c) of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) for measures in relation to Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(e) in connection with the provision of medical services, or unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness or hospital benefits, or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(f) in relation to matters referred to the Parliament of the Commonwealth by the Parliament or Parliaments of any State or States; or<br>(g) in connection with postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>380</td>
<td>Promoting Sustainable Fisheries and Combatting Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing in Southeast Asia and Pacific Islands</td>
<td>To support the provision of technical assistance at the national and regional level to Southeast Asian and Pacific Island countries to:<br>(a) promote sustainable fisheries; and<br>(b) increase the capacity of those countries to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing; and<br>(c) enhance maritime domain awareness.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to supporting activities:<br>(a) relating to fisheries in Australian waters beyond territorial limits; or<br>(b) relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(c) relating to Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific; or<br>(d) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>381</td>
<td>Fisheries Habitat Restoration Program</td>
<td>To improve the health of fisheries and fish stocks by supporting activities to restore marine and estuarine habitats.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to supporting activities:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 8(d), (f) and (i); or<br>(b) directed at fisheries, fish stocks or habitats external to Australia; or<br>(c) funded by way of grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) carried out in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>382</td>
<td>Seniors Connected—Phone Support</td>
<td>To fund online and telephone support services to address loneliness and isolation amongst older Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>383</td>
<td>Future Leaders Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for training and supporting school leaders and potential school leaders, for the following purposes:<br>(a) addressing shortages in the number of school leaders in primary and secondary schools, primarily in regional, rural and remote areas of Australia;<br>(b) increasing the quality of school leadership in such schools.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>385</td>
<td>Online tertiary learning repository services</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) the development of an online tertiary learning repository; and<br>(b) the provision and administration of related services;<br>that facilitate access to, and sharing of, records of educational achievements, including tertiary education transcripts and other records of credentials.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or which are incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>386</td>
<td>Commonwealth Scholarships Program for Young Australians</td>
<td>To provide scholarships for vocational education and training for students from areas of social and economic disadvantage.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 13;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>387</td>
<td>Harvest Trail Service—Collaborating with Industry</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the horticulture industry to implement measures for increasing the supply of, and demand for, seasonal work for Australian workers by:<br>(a) promoting seasonal work opportunities to Australian job seekers; or<br>(b) addressing grower attitudes towards hiring Australian workers.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Article 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>388</td>
<td>Jobs and Education Data Infrastructure</td>
<td>To provide funding to support:<br>(a) the collection, analysis and sharing of information to inform the development of education, training and employment policy; and<br>(b) the online delivery of education, training and employment information and services, including the development of online tools for this purpose.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures or activities:<br>(a) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>389</td>
<td>National Careers Institute Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide grants to support the establishment of partnerships between industry, schools, school authorities and tertiary education providers for initiatives that:<br>(a) improve education and training pathways to employment; or<br>(b) enable employers to play an active role in job skills development.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>390</td>
<td>Grants for support relating to stillbirth, miscarriage and newborn death</td>
<td>To provide funding to organisations to provide in‑hospital, home and other support for women and their families following stillbirth, miscarriage or newborn death, including support of the following kinds:<br>(a) home visits, or telephone or video conference support, by trained support workers;<br>(b) medical support, including organising follow‑up medical visits, providing support during the post‑mortem process, explaining report findings and organising appointments with other practitioners;<br>(c) in‑hospital support, including making funeral arrangements, supporting memory‑making and cancelling antenatal classes;<br>(d) support for affected women, and members of their families, in transitioning back to work;<br>(e) support for children in affected families, including in transitioning back to school.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24; or<br>(b) which provide, or are incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>391</td>
<td>Electromagnetic Energy Program—public communications</td>
<td>To deliver a communications campaign to provide the public with information, based on scientific advice and research, about electromagnetic energy emitted from telecommunications facilities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>392</td>
<td>Supporting the Mental Health of Australians Affected by Bushfires</td>
<td>To provide funding for mental health support for individuals, families and communities who have been affected by the 2019‑2020 bushfire emergency, including the following:<br>(a) funding to establish and operate a program, to be known as the Bushfire Recovery Access Program, to provide support for individuals directly affected by the bushfires, including immediate front‑line distress and trauma counselling;<br>(b) funding to develop and deliver trauma support training for emergency services personnel and their employers;<br>(c) funding for Primary Health Networks to commission additional services and to coordinate services for individuals and communities affected by the bushfires;<br>(d) grants for activities that will support communities in recovery, including peer support activities, activities to strengthen social connectedness, and outreach initiatives to prevent suicide and identify post‑traumatic stress disorder.<br>In addition, to provide funding to develop a cross‑jurisdictional mental health framework to improve whole‑of‑government preparedness for future natural disasters.<br>These objectives also have the effect they would have if they were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, or other like services (with the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) that provide, or are incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7(b) and 12(2); or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>394</td>
<td>Traceability Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide grants for projects that enhance the supply chain traceability systems and arrangements that support the export of agricultural commodities.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing grants in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>395</td>
<td>Small business bushfire financial support line</td>
<td>To fund a national telephone service that offers financial counselling to small businesses that have been affected by the 2019‑2020 bushfire emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>397</td>
<td>Online resources and professional development for mathematics teachers</td>
<td>To fund:<br>(a) the establishment and delivery of massive open online courses to provide professional education to primary and secondary school mathematics teachers; and<br>(b) the establishment and maintenance of an online mathematics hub to function as a repository of mathematics teaching and learning resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>398</td>
<td>Support services for post‑traumatic stress disorder and other mental illnesses—emergency services workers involved in the 2019‑2020 bushfire season</td>
<td>To fund the provision of support services for post‑traumatic stress disorder and other mental illnesses to emergency services workers (including volunteers) involved in the response to bushfires in the 2019‑2020 bushfire season and their immediate families.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to:<br>(a) providing sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) providing funding for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) engaging in enterprises or activities which are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and which cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>399</td>
<td>Support and mental health literacy network for emergency services workers—pilot program</td>
<td>To fund a pilot program to provide a network of support and mental health literacy for emergency services workers (including volunteers) and their families and kinship groups.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing:<br>(a) sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) funding for measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) funding with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>400</td>
<td>Distributed National Collections Grant Program</td>
<td>To fund an Australian museum and gallery peak body to assist small and medium‑sized community organisations to manage, conserve and preserve cultural heritage materials of national significance, including by:<br>(a) providing opportunities for museum workers, volunteers and Indigenous representatives from across Australia to engage in professional development, learning, exchange of expertise and networking; and<br>(b) providing opportunities to participate in training, undertake internships and attend national conferences; and<br>(c) developing appropriate partnerships and networks with cultural organisations; and<br>(d) supporting innovative ways of managing collections and improving public access to collections.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) in connection with electronic communications; or<br>(c) for, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>401</td>
<td>250th Anniversary of James Cook’s Voyage to Australia and the Pacific</td>
<td>To commemorate the 250th anniversary of James Cook’s voyage to Australia and the Pacific, including by doing the following:<br>(a) supporting activities addressing historical and contemporary responses by Indigenous Australians to James Cook’s voyage to Australia;<br>(b) supporting, and providing grants for, local community‑based initiatives to be held in connection with the replica <i>Endeavour</i>’s commemorative voyages.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) for, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>402</td>
<td>Australian Music Industry Package</td>
<td>To support the Australian music industry by providing funding to do the following:<br>(a) establish and deliver a national mentoring program for women in the music industry;<br>(b) assist businesses and music industry organisations to support performances of Australian music by Australian musicians and bands;<br>(c) establish and deliver a national development program for Indigenous musicians and bands;<br>(d) promote Australian music overseas through funding the activities of Sounds Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures or activities:<br>(a) to promote trade and commerce with other countries; or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3 and 11; or<br>(d) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>403</td>
<td>Continuity of Support Fund for Clients of Programs Transitioning to the National Disability Insurance Scheme</td>
<td>To provide funding for continued disability support, and early intervention services, for people with disability who are clients of programs that are transitioning to the National Disability Insurance Scheme, but who are ineligible for that scheme.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>404</td>
<td>National Auslan Interpreter Booking and Payment Services</td>
<td>To fund the booking and provision of Auslan translation services at private medical consultations for deaf people over the age of 65 who are ineligible for the National Disability Insurance Scheme.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>405</td>
<td>Reducing regulatory and auditing burdens in the dairy export supply chain, and supporting Dairy RegTech 2022</td>
<td>To support the following:<br>(a) projects to minimise the burdens, for businesses in the dairy export supply chain, of compliance with regulatory and auditing requirements;<br>(b) projects to assist dairy businesses with export readiness;<br>(c) projects to improve the use of data in regulation of the dairy export supply chain;<br>(d) the Dairy RegTech 2022 initiative of Dairy Food Safety Victoria.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States; or<br>(b) by way of grants of financial assistance to a State.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>406</td>
<td>Youth Whole of Government Framework and Sector Support—Youth Action Support Project Grants Scheme</td>
<td>To fund organisations that work with marginalised youth to run one‑off or small‑scale innovative projects to pilot and evaluate mechanisms to assist young people who:<br>(a) are experiencing disadvantage; or<br>(b) may be missing out on existing services.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support for activities:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 19 and 26;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 19;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 11 and 12;<br>(v) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(vi) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>407</td>
<td>Destination Australia Cheung Kong Exchange Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to Australian higher education providers to subsidise the cost of short‑term opportunities:<br>(a) for Australian university students to study or undertake research overseas; and<br>(b) for non‑citizen students who are studying or undertaking research overseas to study or undertake research at Australian higher education providers.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>408</td>
<td>Coronavirus Economic Response—Assistance for Apprentices and Trainees</td>
<td>To provide payments to eligible employers of apprentices and trainees, Australian Apprenticeship Support Network providers and Group Training Organisations to:<br>(a) encourage and support apprenticeships and traineeships; and<br>(b) assist businesses, apprentices and trainees who may suffer adverse economic effects of the Coronavirus known as COVID‑19.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>409</td>
<td>Coronavirus Economic Response—Aviation Support Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to participants in the Australian aviation sector to assist with the impact on the sector of the Coronavirus known as COVID‑19.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) relating to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(c) for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and of the States; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under Annex 17 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation, particularly Chapter 4 of that Annex; or<br>(e) in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>410</td>
<td>Perinatal Mental Health and Wellbeing Program</td>
<td>To fund organisations to develop and provide perinatal mental health support, promotion and training and wellbeing peer support.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>411</td>
<td>Perinatal Mental Health Check</td>
<td>To establish, maintain and encourage uptake and delivery of a perinatal mental health screening program for new and expecting parents, including by:<br>(a) funding the provision of digital infrastructure, training and support for perinatal mental health screening in public hospitals; and<br>(b) funding initiatives to improve the assessment, management and treatment of perinatal mental health conditions; and<br>(c) disseminating information and support resources in relation to perinatal mental health.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>412</td>
<td>Donor Human Milk Bank Service</td>
<td>To support the ongoing operation and expansion of a coordinated network of donor human milk banks to ensure that premature babies born in Australia have access to human milk, including by providing funding for the following:<br>(a) infrastructure (including upgrading existing infrastructure) and the ongoing operation of facilities to enable the processing and distribution of donor human milk;<br>(b) to establish and maintain consistent production management and processes to ensure that donor human milk is safe and uncontaminated;<br>(c) to establish and undertake research programs concerned with improving outcomes for premature babies and investigating donor human milk processing technologies and product derivatives.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(b) which provide, or are incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 24;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>413</td>
<td>Medicare Mental Health Centres and Telephone Referral Service</td>
<td>To establish, support and publicise:<br>(a) Medicare Mental Health Centres and satellite clinics providing the following:<br>(i) counselling and other mental health services;<br>(ii) advice and referral to specialist mental health services;<br>(iii) information and support to family, friends and carers of persons with mental health conditions;<br>(iv) outreach services for persons who cannot attend a mental health centre or other primary mental health care service or who have recently been hospitalised or are at risk of hospitalisation;<br>(v) digital mental health services; and<br>(b) an intake and assessment telephone service providing advice, triage and referral to mental health services.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) which provide, or are incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 1, 4 and 25;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>414</td>
<td>Australia‑China Agricultural Regulatory Cooperation</td>
<td>To increase cooperation between Australia and the People’s Republic of China on agricultural trade, regulation and research, including by providing funding to support the following:<br>(a) collaborative agricultural research;<br>(b) collaboration and engagement on biosecurity and food safety;<br>(c) bilateral meetings and scientific exchange;<br>(d) the hosting of international standards meetings;<br>(e) cooperation to address non‑tariff measures affecting trade in agricultural products.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries; or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415</td>
<td>Phonics Targeted Assistance Program for Disadvantaged Schools</td>
<td>To assist children to develop literacy skills by providing funding to support teachers and school leaders in their use of phonics instruction, including funding for:<br>(a) the development and delivery of professional learning modules; and<br>(b) the placement of curriculum officers or phonics coaches in disadvantaged schools.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>416</td>
<td>Public Interest News Gathering Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to or for media organisations (including print, digital, radio or television) to support and encourage original, high quality public interest journalism, including such financial assistance to mitigate the adverse effects of the coronavirus known as COVID‑19 on the media sector.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) for, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>417</td>
<td>Support for the Cook Islands</td>
