<td>To provide ongoing financial assistance to, or for the benefit of, the Cook Islands, including for initiatives relating to regional issues in the Pacific.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>418</td>
<td>National Radioactive Waste Management Facility New Community Benefit Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the participation of the South Australian communities of Lyndhurst, Napandee and Wallerberdina in the selection process for the potential establishment and operation of a radioactive waste management facility under the <i>National Radioactive Waste Management Act 2012</i>, particularly to:<br>(a) mitigate and manage any potential social cohesion impacts of the site selection process on those communities, including by diversifying their economies; and<br>(b) contribute to the siting and establishment of a facility under that Act.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Joint Convention on the Safety of Spent Fuel Management and on the Safety of Radioactive Waste Management, particularly Article 11.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>419</td>
<td>National Environmental Science Program</td>
<td>To support Australian Government and other decision‑makers to understand, manage, conserve and restore Australia’s environment with the best available information based on world class science, by providing funding for:<br>(a) research; and<br>(b) the enhancement of research capabilities; and<br>(c) the development, communication and accessibility of research findings and practical guidance.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under international agreements, including:<br>(i) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6 and 12; and<br>(ii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4(1)(b) and (g); or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>420</td>
<td>Telecommunications Emergency Resilience Package</td>
<td>To provide funding to support improvements in:<br>(a) the resilience of telecommunications infrastructure to withstand natural disasters; and<br>(b) the availability of temporary telecommunications infrastructure for deployment before, during or after natural disasters; and<br>(c) the coordination of activities of telecommunications carriers during emergencies; and<br>(d) the communication of information to communities about access to telecommunications services during emergencies; and<br>(e) access to telecommunications services for rural fire services and at evacuation centres, through infrastructure to be deployed by NBN Co Limited.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>421</td>
<td>Multicultural Community Amenities Grants in the Northern Territory</td>
<td>To provide grants to multicultural community organisations to undertake activities in the Northern Territory to support social and economic participation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>422</td>
<td>Disaster Risk Reduction Package</td>
<td>To provide funding for national initiatives that reduce the risk, and limit the impact, of disasters associated with natural hazards on Australian communities and economies, including initiatives to:<br>(a) reduce existing, or minimise future, disaster risk; or<br>(b) equip decision‑makers with capabilities and information to reduce disaster risk and manage residual risk.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(c) with respect to insurance, other than State insurance; or<br>(d) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 11 and 26;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6 and 23;<br>(iii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iv) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 7 and 8;<br>(v) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(f) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(g) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>423</td>
<td>National Centre for the Prevention of Child Sexual Abuse</td>
<td>To provide funding for the establishment, and ongoing costs, of a national centre to carry out the functions set out in Recommendation 9.9 of the Final Report of the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, and to assist in responding to and preventing child sexual abuse.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 19 and 39; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>424</td>
<td>Local Roads and Community Infrastructure Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to:<br>(a) local government bodies, and similar bodies responsible for providing local community services and infrastructure; and<br>(b) States and Territories;<br>for the construction, maintenance or improvement of:<br>(c) roads and associated facilities; and<br>(d) community infrastructure.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) for, or in relation to, Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(da) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>425</td>
<td>Creative Economy Support Package</td>
<td>To provide assistance, including financial assistance, to mitigate, and to support the recovery of the arts sector from, the adverse effects of the national crisis resulting from the coronavirus known as COVID‑19 on that sector, and to enhance the resilience and sustainability of participants in that sector.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) in relation to Indigenous Australians or particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, particularly Article 7;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 15;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Article 1; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>426</td>
<td>Reconnect Program</td>
<td>To reduce and prevent homelessness by providing funding for services for:<br>(a) persons aged between 12 and 18 years who are homeless or at risk of homelessness; and<br>(b) persons aged between 12 and 21 years who are newly arrived in Australia and are homeless or at risk of homelessness, including persons who are non‑citizens; and<br>(c) the families of persons mentioned in paragraphs (a) and (b);<br>including services to assist such persons and their families to:<br>(d) stabilise their living situation; and<br>(e) achieve family reconciliation wherever practicable; and<br>(f) improve their level of engagement with:<br>(i) the community; and<br>(ii) education, training or employment, or a combination of those things.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 27;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 11.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>427</td>
<td>Payments to Plant Health Australia Limited</td>
<td>To support Plant Health Australia Limited to:<br>(a) facilitate and coordinate government‑industry partnerships on plant biosecurity matters, plant health, plant pests, diseases and weeds; and<br>(b) facilitate and coordinate emergency responses to plant biosecurity matters, threats to plant health and incursions of plant pests, diseases and weeds; and<br>(c) improve Australia’s preparedness and capability to identify, respond to and manage plant biosecurity matters, threats to plant health, plant pests, diseases and weeds; and<br>(d) develop, manage and coordinate national policies and programs on plant biosecurity matters, plant health, plant pests, diseases and weeds.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to supporting measures:<br>(a) in connection with the use of postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) in connection with quarantine; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s international obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (particularly Article 8(h)); or<br>(d) relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>428</td>
<td>Residential Aged Care Viability Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to residential aged care providers to ensure the provision of an adequate level of continued care for aged care residents, including funding to:<br>(a) assist a provider in relation to the impact on the aged care sector of the coronavirus known as COVID‑19; or<br>(b) support a provider to develop and undertake business improvement activities for sustaining the provision of residential aged care services; or<br>(c) support a provider with the sale of a residential aged care facility to facilitate the provision of care for aged care residents by another residential aged care provider; or<br>(d) support a provider to ensure continued care for aged care residents upon the closure of a residential aged care facility;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>429</td>
<td>Sport and Recreation Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to:<br>(a) support activities directed at Australia hosting major international sporting events, including the following:<br>(i) activities relating to the development of bids for Australia to host such events;<br>(ii) activities undertaken to prepare for, support or stage such events in Australia, including the construction or renovation of infrastructure and the purchasing of equipment;<br>(iii) promotion of such events hosted by Australia; and<br>(b) promote access to, and participation in, sporting or recreation activities:<br>(i) by members of the community who are Indigenous Australians, children, women, non‑citizens, immigrants or people with disabilities; or<br>(ii) by members of the community, to promote physical and mental health and prevent disease; or<br>(iii) by members of the community, to eliminate racial, cultural or ethnic discrimination and promote social cohesion within the community; or<br>(iv) in Pacific Island countries;<br>including by providing funding for infrastructure or other resources; and<br>(c) support the achievement of excellence in Australia’s representative athletes, including by:<br>(i) supporting the development of Australia’s current and future representative athletes, including by investing in research, equipment and infrastructure; and<br>(ii) establishing, delivering or supporting programs, and national and international sporting events, that are aimed at identifying and developing Australia’s representative athletes.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(d) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 10 and 13;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 30;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 6, 18, 24, 28, 29 and 31;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 12 and 15; or<br>(ea) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(eb) with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific; or<br>(f) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(g) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(h) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>430</td>
<td>Reading Writing Hotline</td>
<td>To provide funding for the provision to adults, online or by telephone, of information about language, literacy and numeracy courses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>431</td>
<td>Adult Learners’ Week</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities undertaken as part of the annual United Nations Week of Adult Learning referred to in the Hamburg Declaration on Adult Learning, as existing at the commencement of this item.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>432</td>
<td>School Leaver Program</td>
<td>To provide information, advice and referral services (including through telephone and online services) to support school leavers to:<br>(a) make informed decisions about their career; or<br>(b) transition to further learning or employment;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Article 3.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>433</td>
<td>Local Jobs—COVID‑19 Recovery</td>
<td>To deal with the nationwide economic impact of the coronavirus known as COVID‑19 by undertaking measures to help persons seeking employment to find and retain employment with suitable employers, including through:<br>(a) funding training, mentoring and support services; and<br>(b) funding projects; and<br>(c) engaging employment facilitators; and<br>(d) establishing Local Jobs and Skills Taskforces.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) providing, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>434</td>
<td>Coronavirus economic response—pandemic leave disaster payments</td>
<td>To provide payments to individuals unable to earn income because they:<br>(a) have tested positive for the coronavirus known as COVID‑19; or<br>(b) are a close contact of an individual referred to in paragraph (a); or<br>(c) are required to care for an individual referred to in paragraph (a) or (b);<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>435</td>
<td>PaTH Business Placement Partnerships</td>
<td>To develop and deliver, in collaboration with industry and employer groups, measures to assist young people to find employment (including apprenticeships, traineeships and other work experience opportunities) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to:<br>(a) postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) the provision of unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>436</td>
<td>Australian Training Awards</td>
<td>To support a national awards scheme recognising achievement by individuals (including students) and organisations in the vocational education and training sector by funding:<br>(a) monetary prizes forming part of awards; and<br>(b) expenses associated with the awards judging process, presenting awards to recipients and promoting the awards program;<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to the provision of, or measures incidental to the provision of, benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>437</td>
<td>National Careers Institute—Digital Platform</td>
<td>To develop, and provide online, information to support individuals and organisations to access, understand and compare:<br>(a) education, training, skills development and other learning options; and<br>(b) occupational choices; and<br>(c) employment opportunities; and<br>(d) advice about finding, applying for and gaining employment; and<br>(e) labour market trends; and<br>(f) other careers information in the possession of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>438</td>
<td>National Training System Commonwealth Own Purpose Expenditure Program</td>
<td>To provide essential governance and infrastructure for the operation of the national training system, including through the provision of funding for:<br>(a) vocational education and training (<b><i>VET</b></i>) data collection, analysis and research; and<br>(b) the development and evaluation of VET policy; and<br>(c) the development of VET standards, frameworks and supporting materials; and<br>(d) the collection and publication of VET information; and<br>(e) the development, hosting and maintenance of infrastructure (including telecommunication systems) to support the VET sector;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(f) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(g) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(h) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 and 2.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>439</td>
<td>Seniors Connected—Village Hubs</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the establishment and operation of community‑based organisations offering social, physical and other activities or opportunities to older Australians, to:<br>(a) address loneliness and isolation among older Australians, in order to reduce the incidence of mental health issues in the ageing population; and<br>(b) facilitate healthy ageing; and<br>(c) assist older Australians to participate in cultural and community life;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 12 and 15.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>440</td>
<td>Tracking Waste Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) the development and operation of an online platform displaying visualised data relating to waste and including analytical capabilities; and<br>(b) activities that address issues relating to data interoperability and connection with the online platform; and<br>(c) the development and implementation of waste data standards to support the online platform; and<br>(d) an engagement program to build awareness of, and obtain feedback on, the online platform.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>441</td>
<td>Grant for national food waste governance entity</td>
<td>To provide funding for the establishment and ongoing costs of a long‑term governance entity to work with industry and researchers to reduce food waste:<br>(a) in the supply chain through a voluntary commitment program; or<br>(b) by influencing behavioural change in business and households;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(c) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(d) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 and 12;<br>(e) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>442</td>
<td>Financial counselling for small regional businesses affected by drought, bushfires or COVID‑19</td>
<td>To provide funding to facilitate the provision of financial counselling and related services to small regional businesses facing financial hardship due to drought, the 2019‑2020 bushfire emergency or the coronavirus known as COVID‑19.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 4(2)(a) and 5; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>443</td>
<td>Bushfire Recovery for Species and Landscapes—Tranche 2 Emergency Intervention Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding for emergency intervention works for threatened species and landscapes affected by the 2019‑2020 bushfire emergency, including the following:<br>(a) environmental recovery activities in regions affected by the bushfires to prevent extinction, and limit the decline, of native species;<br>(b) supporting community organisations to participate in the recovery of species and landscapes by undertaking projects to conserve their local environment and manage the natural resources base;<br>(c) Indigenous cultural burning and land management workshops;<br>(d) scientific assessment of the conservation status of species and updating conservation planning documents;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6, 7, 8 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>444</td>
<td>Support for Australia’s Thalidomide Survivors</td>
<td>To provide support to thalidomide survivors, including by providing funding for:<br>(a) the establishment of a national site of recognition for thalidomide survivors and their families, in the form of a public memorial; and<br>(b) payments to thalidomide survivors to:<br>(i) acknowledge the pain and suffering experienced throughout their lives; and<br>(ii) meet their increased health needs due to early onset ageing; and<br>(c) an Extraordinary Assistance Fund through which thalidomide survivors will be given funds to assist them to adapt their homes, vehicles and environment; and<br>(d) a national disability support service to assist thalidomide survivors to identify and gain access to specific thalidomide‑related supports and services; and<br>(e) a Health Care Assistance Fund through which thalidomide survivors will be given funds to assist them with out‑of‑pocket health care expenses.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) providing, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits and medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 25;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>445</td>
<td>National identity crime and cybercrime support service</td>
<td>To provide funding to identity crime and cybercrime support service providers to assist individuals and businesses that have had their identities stolen or misused online.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to banking, other than State banking (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiii) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried out for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Commonwealth place; or<br>(f) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(g) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>446</td>
<td>Extended New Enterprise Incentive Scheme—COVID‑19 response</td>
<td>To provide self‑employed micro‑business owners with small business training, mentoring and other support to assist them to retain their employment as self‑employed micro‑business owners, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 13;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(c) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures dealing with the economic effects of the coronavirus known as COVID‑19, being measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>447</td>
<td>Combatting modern slavery</td>
<td>To provide funding to combat modern slavery, including funding to do the following:<br>(a) undertake activities to equip Australian businesses to manage supply chain risks, including the following activities:<br>(i) developing and hosting industry summits;<br>(ii) developing and delivering training to industry;<br>(iii) developing and maintaining the online Modern Slavery Statements Register;<br>(b) review the <i>Modern Slavery Act 2018</i>, including by commissioning a review of that Act;<br>(c) provide multi‑year grant opportunities to fund:<br>(i) projects to combat modern slavery; or<br>(ii) the development of supply chain resilience of Australian businesses; or<br>(iii) new research to support evidence‑based modern slavery policy;<br>(d) develop and deliver targeted training to:<br>(i) frontline government officials, on identifying and referring modern slavery cases and responding to new modern slavery trends; and<br>(ii) government officials, on addressing modern slavery risks in government procurement and investment;<br>(e) undertake activities to strengthen bilateral and multilateral cooperation to combat modern slavery in the Indo‑Pacific Region, including the following activities:<br>(i) developing and delivering training and technical assistance to partner governments;<br>(ii) participating in multilateral forums;<br>(f) establish multi‑sector networks in the States and Territories to enhance law enforcement capability, and bolster resources, dedicated to detecting and deterring modern slavery;<br>(g) develop and maintain a website with information and resources about modern slavery, in multiple languages;<br>(h) develop, translate and distribute information and resources for modern slavery victims, multicultural groups and the broader community to understand modern slavery, deter perpetrators and refer cases;<br>(i) develop and deliver national and targeted campaigns to raise community awareness of modern slavery, including the indicators of modern slavery and avenues to report modern slavery offences;<br>(j) engage with modern slavery victims to seek and receive feedback on existing and new, legal and policy, responses to modern slavery;<br>(k) commission the Australian Institute of Criminology to monitor and evaluate Australia’s <i>National Action Plan to Combat Modern Slavery 2020‑25</i>, including by:<br>(i) establishing new data collection processes; and<br>(ii) collecting data on emerging criminal methodologies; and<br>(iii) collecting and analysing monitoring and evaluation data; and<br>(iv) preparing and delivering reports.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Article 6;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 32, 34, 35 and 36;<br>(iii) the International Convention to Suppress the Slave Trade and Slavery, particularly Article 2;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 8;<br>(v) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Forced or Compulsory Labour, particularly Article 1;<br>(vi) the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on the sale of children, child prostitution and child pornography, particularly Article 9;<br>(vii) the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children, supplementing the United Nations Convention Against Transnational Organized Crime, particularly Article 9;<br>(viii) the Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery, the Slave Trade, and Institutions and Practices similar to Slavery, particularly Article 1; or<br>(c) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) with respect to Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(e) done in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>448</td>
<td>Joint Strike Fighter Industry Support Program</td>
<td>To further Australia’s defence capability and preparedness through the acquisition and sustainment of the F‑35 Joint Strike Fighter, by funding defence sector enterprises to develop and maintain their capability in relation to the production and maintenance of the F‑35 Joint Strike Fighter.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>450</td>
<td>Powering Communities Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to support community organisations to reduce energy use, improve energy productivity and deliver carbon abatement, including through:<br>(a) upgrading equipment to reduce energy use; and<br>(b) undertaking energy management activities and assessments, such as energy systems assessments and feasibility studies; and<br>(c) investing in energy monitoring and management systems; and<br>(d) investing in on‑site renewable energy and solar‑connected batteries;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(e) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(f) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(g) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>451</td>
<td>Building Energy Efficiency Program</td>
<td>To support activities that reduce energy use, improve energy productivity and deliver carbon abatement in buildings, including through:<br>(a) developing and providing information relating to building energy efficiency, including energy related requirements of the National Construction Code; and<br>(b) developing and providing information about, and assessing, the energy efficiency of heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems in buildings; and<br>(c) developing and providing tools and ratings for the energy performance of buildings;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(d) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(e) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(f) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>452</td>
<td>Technology Co‑Investment Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities that reduce energy use, improve energy productivity and deliver carbon abatement in the industrial, transport and agricultural sectors, including through:<br>(a) industrial and energy productivity benchmarking, including in manufacturing and construction; and<br>(b) improving transport fuel efficiency, including for freight; and<br>(c) increasing soil carbon; and<br>(d) reducing livestock emissions;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(e) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(f) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(g) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>453</td>
<td>Hydrogen Export Hub Program</td>
<td>To support the development of hydrogen production, hydrogen demand and hydrogen export supply chains, including through:<br>(a) funding research and development activities relevant to hydrogen technologies, hydrogen industry expansion and export supply chains; and<br>(b) international and domestic collaboration on hydrogen export supply chains and hub development; and<br>(c) supporting projects for the production, use, transformation, storage, transport or export of the following:<br>(i) hydrogen;<br>(ii) hydrogen feedstocks or derivatives; and<br>(d) supporting activities to increase the supply of, and demand for, hydrogen; and<br>(e) undertaking and supporting activities to improve the regulation or safety of hydrogen production, use, transformation, storage, transport or export.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(ii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 and 10;<br>(iii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(c) relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>454</td>
<td>Restoring native aquatic animals in the Murray‑Darling Basin and providing employment for Indigenous Australians</td>
<td>To support the restoration of native aquatic species and natural habitat in the Murray‑Darling Basin and to provide employment for Indigenous Australians, including by:<br>(a) establishing a hatchery, grow‑out facility and drought recovery centre for native aquatic species, with integrated commercial operations, in Menindee; and<br>(b) establishing a hatchery and grow‑out facility for native aquatic species, with integrated commercial operations, in St George; and<br>(c) restoring the natural habitat of native aquatic species; and<br>(d) conducting research activities in relation to native aquatic species.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6(a), 8(d) and (f) and 10(d).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>455</td>
<td>Reef Builder—the coastal communities recovery project</td>
<td>To support measures to rebuild and prevent the extinction of shellfish reefs along the Australian coastline to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 8(d) and (f) and 10(e).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>456</td>
<td>Murray‑Darling Basin Water Information Platform</td>
<td>To establish and maintain an online water information platform relating to the Murray‑Darling Basin to provide information about matters such as the following:<br>(a) water availability, allocations, use and trade;<br>(b) water planning, policies and programs;<br>(c) water levels in storages and in‑stream flow rates;<br>(d) water resource management and planning arrangements;<br>(e) environmental watering events;<br>(f) water markets and trading.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>457</td>
<td>National Forest Industries Plan—Online Resources</td>
<td>To support the growth of Australia’s renewable timber and wood‑fibre industry through developing online guidance material and advice for:<br>(a) persons engaging in farm forestry and private native forestry; and<br>(b) forest resources managers of Indigenous‑owned or Indigenous‑managed land.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>458</td>
<td>Home Care Transition Fund</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to Commonwealth funded home care providers who are insolvent, or at imminent risk of becoming insolvent or bankrupt, as a result of the change from pre‑service delivery payments to post‑service delivery payments by the Commonwealth.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to being a measure for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>459</td>
<td>National Microcredentials Marketplace</td>
<td>To establish and operate a website to provide information about microcredentials.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>460</td>
<td>Tertiary Access Payment</td>
<td>To encourage and assist students from regional and remote areas of Australia to access tertiary study by providing, as benefits to students within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution, one‑off payments to eligible students who relocate to commence tertiary study.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>461</td>
<td>Pacific Labour Mobility: Safeguarding Welfare of Workers (Community Connections)</td>
<td>To support the welfare of persons (the <b><i>participants</b></i>) who are:<br>(a) aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution) or immigrants; and<br>(b) participating in the Seasonal Worker Program or Pacific Labour Scheme;<br>by fostering the participants’ inclusion in their local Australian communities, including by funding organisations to:<br>(c) pursue initiatives designed to build connections between the participants and such communities; and<br>(d) provide ongoing support to the participants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>462</td>
<td>Online toolkit to promote the financial capability of young Australians</td>
<td>To enhance the financial capability of young Australians by funding the development and delivery of online content that:<br>(a) assists young Australians to manage money, including by improving their understanding of superannuation, taxation, insurance, budgeting and credit; and<br>(b) assists parents and other adults to explain to young Australians how to manage money, including by assisting parents and other adults to explain superannuation, taxation, insurance, budgeting and credit to young Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>463</td>
<td>Holocaust Memorial Week</td>
<td>To support the Australian Education Working Group within the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance to promote Holocaust education during Holocaust Memorial Week by developing and delivering online educational resources, and undertaking related activities, including the following:<br>(a) creating, promoting and maintaining an online platform to distribute those resources to schools;<br>(b) conducting a social media campaign to promote use of the online platform;<br>(c) evaluating the use by schools of the educational resources delivered through the online platform.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>464</td>
<td>Emerging Priorities Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to improve educational outcomes or to support career development (or both) for school students, including by:<br>(a) supporting school attendance and completion; and<br>(b) addressing health issues of school students, teachers and school leaders, including mental health issues; and<br>(c) providing professional development for school leaders and teachers directed at improving educational outcomes; and<br>(d) providing online or face‑to‑face educational resources for school leaders, teachers, students and parents to support the teaching and learning of school students; and<br>(e) providing career training, guidance and advice to school students; and<br>(f) researching, analysing and addressing the impacts of unexpected events, including the COVID‑19 pandemic, on educational outcomes for school students;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(g) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 24, 28 and 29;<br>(h) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 12 and 13;<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(j) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of<i>,</i> or incidental to the provision of, student benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>465</td>
<td>National Collecting Institutions Touring and Outreach Program</td>
<td>To provide, as a national initiative in the arts, financial assistance to national collecting institutions and organisations to develop and tour exhibitions, within Australia and overseas, and to bring cultural material, and works, from international collections to Australia for exhibition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>466</td>
<td>Australian Government International Exhibitions Insurance Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to cultural institutions and organisations to obtain insurance in relation to exhibitions in Australia of cultural material, and works, from international collections.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>467</td>
<td>Indigenous Repatriation Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to museums and cultural institutions in Australia to:<br>(a) facilitate the return of Indigenous Australian ancestral remains and secret sacred objects to their community of origin; and<br>(b) provide culturally appropriate care of, and access to, Indigenous Australian ancestral remains and secret sacred objects.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>468</td>
<td>Arts and Cultural Development Program—Arts Training Organisations</td>
<td>To provide, as a national initiative in the arts, financial assistance to national performing arts organisations for the training of young Australian performing artists.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>469</td>
<td>Australian 5G Innovation Initiative</td>
<td>To provide financial support to facilitate and encourage the deployment and use of the fifth generation of mobile telecommunications technology used for wireless communication (<b><i>5G</b></i>), including by providing:<br>(a) support to businesses in Australia to test and develop 5G applications, services and products and approaches to addressing technical challenges in relation to 5G; and<br>(b) incentives to business to adopt 5G solutions and to carriers to accelerate the roll out of 5G; and<br>(c) support to develop Australian expertise in relation to the deployment and application of 5G; and<br>(d) support to develop more advanced uses of 5G.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>470</td>
<td>Commonwealth Disability Support for Older Australians</td>
<td>To provide funding for disability services to individual older people with a disability who:<br>(a) are ineligible for the National Disability Insurance Scheme; and<br>(b) received services under any of the following programs:<br>(i) Continuity of Support—Block‑funded Activities;<br>(ii) Continuity of Support—Individual Support Packages;<br>(iii) Continuity of Support—Community Mental Health Services;<br>(iv) Continuity of Support Fund for Clients of Programs Transitioning to the National Disability Insurance Scheme.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 25.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>471</td>
<td>Murray‑Darling Healthy Rivers Program</td>
<td>To support community‑based environmental projects to improve the health and ecological condition of rivers and wetlands in the Murray‑Darling Basin, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of Japan for the Protection of Migratory Birds and Birds in Danger of Extinction and their Environment, particularly Articles III(1), IV(3), V and VI(a);<br>(b) the Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of the People’s Republic of China for the Protection of Migratory Birds and their Environment, particularly Articles III(3) and IV;<br>(c) the Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of the Republic of Korea on the Protection of Migratory Birds, particularly Articles 3(3), 4 and 5(a) and (b);<br>(d) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 8(d), (f) and (h);<br>(e) the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals, particularly Article III;<br>(f) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Articles 3(1) and 4(4);<br>(g) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 4(2)(a) and 5(a) and (d).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>472</td>
<td>Immediate Assistance Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding to States and Territories and to industry to improve Australia’s capacity to respond to pest and disease incursions, including for:<br>(a) provision of immediately available resources to facilitate rapid response and containment of pest and disease incursions; and<br>(b) deployment of and access to national and international experts; and<br>(c) access to specialised equipment required for the following:<br>(i) aiding responses to biosecurity incidents;<br>(ii) pest and disease eradication; and<br>(d) provision of improved information to inform decision making; and<br>(e) undertaking emergency preparedness activities.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries; or<br>(b) with respect to quarantine; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 8(h); or<br>(d) for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) by way of grants of financial assistance to States and Territories.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>473</td>
<td>Great Artesian Basin Lynn Brake Scholarship Grant Program</td>
<td>To fund a scholarship program for students which supports research related to the Great Artesian Basin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>474</td>
<td>Lake Eyre Basin Justin Costelloe Scholarship Grant Program</td>
<td>To fund a scholarship program for students which supports research and understanding in relation to the Lake Eyre Basin Agreement Area (as defined by the Lake Eyre Basin Intergovernmental Agreement made on 21 October 2000, as in force immediately before the commencement of this item).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>475</td>
<td>Tourism Aviation Network Support Program</td>
<td>To assist the recovery of regions in Australia that are economically reliant on tourism from the adverse effects on tourism and those regions of the national crisis resulting from the coronavirus known as COVID‑19, by providing financial assistance to Australian airline operators to enable them to:<br>(a) offer more flights to and from such regions; and<br>(b) discount fares for flights to and from such regions.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to being a measure:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>476</td>
<td>National Memorial for Victims and Survivors of Institutional Child Sexual Abuse</td>
<td>To provide funding or support for the following activities:<br>(a) holding a ceremony in the Australian Capital Territory to announce the design and future site for a national memorial for victims and survivors of institutional child sexual abuse;<br>(b) holding a commemorative ceremony in the Australian Capital Territory to mark the opening of the national memorial;<br>(c) assisting key stakeholders to attend the ceremonies referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b);<br>(d) establishing and maintaining a website to complement the national memorial and to serve as a commemorative and educational resource.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>477</td>
<td>Underwater Cultural Heritage Program</td>
<td>To protect and conserve Australia’s underwater cultural heritage, including by:<br>(a) providing for the identification, protection and conservation of Australia’s underwater cultural heritage; and<br>(b) enabling the cooperative implementation of national and international maritime heritage responsibilities; and<br>(c) promoting public awareness, understanding, appreciation and appropriate use of Australia’s underwater cultural heritage.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) by way of grants of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) in or in relation to a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>478</td>
<td>Indigenous Rangers Biosecurity Program</td>
<td>To support increased economic opportunities for Indigenous persons, entities and communities through activities that enhance biosecurity outcomes in northern Australia, including by:<br>(a) engaging Indigenous rangers and Indigenous land and sea managers to deliver biosecurity functions including preparedness, monitoring, surveillance and response functions; and<br>(b) providing support and equipment to Indigenous rangers and Indigenous land and sea managers to assist them to carry out their functions; and<br>(c) developing the capability of Indigenous rangers and Indigenous land and sea managers including through training and forums; and<br>(d) delivering Indigenous traineeships in biosecurity work; and<br>(e) providing support to Indigenous trainees to assist them in their biosecurity work; and<br>(f) providing grant funding to Indigenous persons or entities, or entities working with Indigenous persons, for initiatives relating to biosecurity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>479</td>
<td>Indigenous Rangers Coastal Clean‑Ups Project</td>
<td>To support increased economic opportunities for Indigenous persons, entities and communities through activities that protect biodiversity and preserve natural habitat in northern Australia, including by engaging Indigenous rangers to locate, retrieve and dispose of marine debris such as lost or discarded fishing equipment on beaches and waterways in northern Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) with respect to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 8.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>480</td>
<td>South Asia Regional Training and Technical Assistance Centre</td>
<td>To fund the International Monetary Fund to assist South Asian countries to design and implement policies that promote economic growth and reduce poverty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>481</td>
<td>Home Care Workforce Support Program</td>
<td>To support the aged care workforce, with a focus on home care, and to increase the skills of that workforce by providing funding to organisations and consortia to undertake activities, including the following:<br>(a) selecting and supporting suitable jobseekers to obtain employment providing home care services to older Australians;<br>(b) supporting new entrants to the home care sector to develop the skills, and to undertake the training, needed to provide home care services to older Australians;<br>(c) working with home care providers, employment services and registered training organisations to enhance the leadership capabilities of the existing aged care workforce to ensure new entrants to that workforce are adequately supported;<br>(d) providing additional targeted support to aged care providers, including residential care providers, in rural and remote areas where there are identified workforce shortages;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(e) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(f) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(g) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>482</td>
<td>Regional Arts Fund</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to support and promote the creation of, participation in and access to Australian arts and culture in regional and remote Australia, including by providing support for:<br>(a) professional development and employment of artists and arts workers; and<br>(b) arts or culture projects and activities of strategic benefit to Australian arts and culture.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more international agreements, including the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, particularly Articles 7 and 10;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 15;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Article 1; or<br>(d) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>483</td>
<td>Wellbeing and Support Program</td>
<td>To provide case management services to highly vulnerable veterans who:<br>(a) are transitioning into civilian life after their service in the Australian Defence Force; or<br>(b) have complex care needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>484</td>
<td>Volunteer Management Activity</td>
<td>To provide funding to:<br>(a) develop, establish and maintain an online platform to:<br>(i) provide information and digital resources to volunteer support services, volunteer involving organisations and volunteers, including in relation to training, reporting and capacity building; and<br>(ii) facilitate communication, collaboration and sharing of information and digital resources between volunteer support services and volunteer involving organisations; and<br>(b) volunteer organisations to:<br>(i) deliver support and training over the internet to volunteer support services, volunteer involving organisations and volunteers; and<br>(ii) provide support and training to volunteer involving organisations to access and use the online platform referred to in paragraph (a); and<br>(iii) increase access to volunteering opportunities, and remove barriers to volunteering, for identified priority groups; and<br>(iv) facilitate employment pathways for identified priority groups.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Article 3;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 19;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 6;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>485</td>
<td>Stronger Places, Stronger People</td>
<td>To improve outcomes for children in disadvantaged communities through:<br>(a) supporting families, and assisting communities to support families, to prepare for parenthood and caregiving responsibilities and further the development of the children in their care; and<br>(b) discouraging use of harmful substances such as tobacco, alcohol and drugs amongst prospective parents; and<br>(c) encouraging young people to seek employment; and<br>(d) preparing young people for employment; and<br>(e) ensuring women have access to appropriate pre‑natal and post‑natal services; and<br>(f) undertaking measures to help children to live safely and outside the youth justice system;<br>by providing funding to:<br>(g) design and implement a national model; and<br>(h) enable communities to develop, implement and evaluate strategies to achieve the outcomes of the program, including by establishing local project teams to support communities to do this; and<br>(i) develop tools and resources that can be tailored to, and used by, communities;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(j) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(k) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(l) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 6, 18, 19, 24, 27, 28, 29 and 31;<br>(m) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 12;<br>(n) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961 (as amended), particularly Articles 4 and 38;<br>(o) the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 14;<br>(p) the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, particularly Articles 5, 12 and 14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>486</td>
<td>Black Summer Bushfire Recovery Grants Program</td>
<td>To support:<br>(a) the short to medium‑term recovery needs of communities affected by the 2019‑2020 bushfire emergency; and<br>(b) initiatives to increase the resilience of such communities against future bushfires.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, or other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to astronomical and meteorological observations; or<br>(d) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(e) with respect to insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); or<br>(f) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits and medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(g) with respect to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(h) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6, 12 and 15;<br>(ii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 7 and 8;<br>(iv) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(i) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(j) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(k) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>487</td>
<td>Blue Carbon Ecosystems</td>
<td>To support:<br>(a) projects in regional Australia and in foreign countries that relate to restoring coastal ecosystems and demonstrating environmental economic accounting; and<br>(b) international events and partnerships relating to blue carbon and rainforests.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6 and 8;<br>(ii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 10;<br>(iv) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(b) relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>488</td>
<td>Australian Farm Data Code</td>
<td>To modify, expand, implement, and raise awareness of, the Australian Farm Data Code as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>489</td>
<td>AgCAREERSTART, AgUP and Modern Workforce Management and Planning Practices Project</td>
<td>To assist in shifting perceptions of agriculture, improve the reputation of the agricultural sector as an employer, and build workforce management and planning skills, including by:<br>(a) supporting a pilot initiative to provide school leavers with the opportunity to work in agriculture by undertaking a placement at a farm and relevant training; and<br>(b) providing grants for industry‑led initiatives to provide opportunities for upskilling and career progression; and<br>(c) supporting agricultural employers to implement best practice modern workforce management and planning practices.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>490</td>
<td>Innovation Fund for Online and Offshore Education Services</td>
<td>To support eligible higher education providers, and eligible providers of an English Language Intensive Course for Overseas Students, in relation to the provision of online and offshore education services to overseas students.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>491</td>
<td>Child care services website</td>
<td>To develop, establish and maintain a website to provide information about child care services, including information in relation to particular child care providers and the services that they offer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>492</td>
<td>COVID‑19 Disaster Payment</td>
<td>Certain persons residing or working in a COVID‑19 hotspot unable to earn usual income<br>To provide financial assistance to certain persons who:<br>(a) are Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents or holders of a temporary visa who have the right to work in Australia; and<br>(b) are aged 17 years or over; and<br>(c) reside or work in a location in Australia that is, or resided or worked in a location in Australia at a time that it was:<br>(i) subject to a State or Territory public health order restricting the movement of persons for a period; and<br>(ii) determined by the Commonwealth Chief Medical Officer to be a COVID‑19 hotspot for the purposes of Commonwealth support; and<br>(d) are, or were, unable to earn their usual income because the restrictions imposed by the public health order prevent, or prevented, them being able to undertake their usual work; and<br>(e) have, or had, no available pandemic‑related paid leave entitlements to cover the period of the restrictions; and<br>(f) declare that during the period of the restrictions they reside or work, or resided or worked, in the hotspot area; and<br>(g) during the period of the restrictions are, or were, not otherwise receiving:<br>(ii) pandemic leave disaster payments; or<br>(iii) pandemic payments from a State or Territory;<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>Certain persons previously in a COVID‑19 hotspot unable to earn usual income<br>In addition, to provide financial assistance to certain persons who:<br>(a) are Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents or holders of a temporary visa who have the right to work in Australia; and<br>(b) are aged 17 years or over; and<br>(c) were previously present in a location (the <b><i>hotspot area</b></i>) in Australia that was at that time, or is at a later time:<br>(i) subject to a State or Territory public health order restricting the movement of persons; and<br>(ii) determined by the Commonwealth Chief Medical Officer to be a COVID‑19 hotspot for the purposes of Commonwealth support; and<br>(d) are, or were, present in another location in Australia at a time that it was subject to a State or Territory public health order (the <b><i>second public health order</b></i>) restricting the movement of persons for a period where such persons were previously present in the hotspot area; and<br>(e) are, or were, restricted in their movement by the second public health order because they were previously present in the hotspot area; and<br>(f) are, or were, unable to earn their usual income because the restrictions imposed by the second public health order prevent, or prevented, them being able to undertake their usual work; and<br>(g) have, or had, no available pandemic‑related paid leave entitlements to cover the period of the restrictions; and<br>(h) declare that during the period of the restrictions they are, or were, in an area where restrictions have been imposed on persons who were previously present in the hotspot area; and<br>(i) during the period of the restrictions are, or were, not otherwise receiving:<br>(ii) pandemic leave disaster payments; or<br>(iii) pandemic payments from a State or Territory;<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>Certain persons residing or working in State or Territory but outside COVID‑19 hotspot unable to earn usual income<br>In addition, to provide financial assistance to certain persons who:<br>(a) are Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents or holders of a temporary visa who have the right to work in Australia; and<br>(b) are aged 17 years or over; and<br>(c) at a particular time, reside or work, or resided or worked, in a State or Territory that:<br>(i) contains a location that is or was, at the particular time, subject to a State or Territory public health order restricting the movement of persons for a period and determined by the Commonwealth Chief Medical Officer to be a COVID‑19 hotspot for the purposes of Commonwealth support; and<br>(ii) at or after the particular time, enters into an agreement with the Commonwealth to reimburse the Commonwealth for the financial assistance; and<br>(ca) at the particular time, do not reside and do not work, or did not reside and did not work, in a location determined by the Commonwealth Chief Medical Officer to be a COVID‑19 hotspot for the purposes of Commonwealth support; and<br>(d) are or were unable to earn their usual income as a direct or indirect result of the restrictions imposed by a public health order of the State or Territory; and<br>(e) have, or had, no available pandemic‑related paid leave entitlements to cover the period for which the financial assistance is provided; and<br>(f) make a declaration in relation to where they reside and work, or resided and worked, during the period of the restrictions; and<br>(g) declare that they are or were unable to earn their usual income as a result of the restrictions imposed by a public health order of the State or Territory; and<br>(h) during the period for which the financial assistance is provided are, or were, not otherwise receiving:<br>(ii) pandemic leave disaster payments; or<br>(iii) pandemic payments from a State or Territory;<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>Certain persons previously eligible for financial assistance under another objective<br>In addition, to provide certain persons who have ceased to be eligible to receive financial assistance under another objective of the program with up to 2 further payments of financial assistance, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>493</td>
<td>Indigenous Protected Areas</td>
<td>To provide funding to:<br>(a) Indigenous persons to enable them to manage areas of land and sea (known as Indigenous Protected Areas) for biodiversity conservation, and the protection of natural and cultural values, in collaboration with other relevant stakeholders; and<br>(b) support such management, including funding for infrastructure and services;<br>so as to benefit Indigenous persons, including by:<br>(c) promoting employment and economic opportunities for Indigenous persons; and<br>(d) assisting Indigenous persons to derive economic and social benefits from the use of land and sea, including through the development of sustainable industries and sustainable ocean economies; and<br>(e) supporting the intergenerational transfer of Indigenous ecological knowledge, and the mapping, research and monitoring of ecological and cultural values.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>494</td>
<td>Expensive Commonwealth Criminal Cases Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding to Legal Aid Commissions to support them to provide legal assistance in high cost Commonwealth criminal matters, and in matters relating to control orders, post‑sentence orders and community safety orders, under Commonwealth law.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>495</td>
<td>Provision of safety net television services</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the provision of television services to viewers who are unable to access or receive terrestrial television services.</td>
</tr>
