<tr>
<td>496</td>
<td>Peri‑Urban Mobile Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the provision of improved telecommunications connectivity in urban or peri‑urban areas of Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>497</td>
<td>Culture, Heritage and Arts Regional Tourism Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance for the Australian Museums and Galleries Association Incorporated to deliver support to community cultural, heritage and arts organisations in regional Australia, including museums, galleries and historical societies, to assist them to recover from the adverse effects of the national crisis resulting from the coronavirus known as COVID‑19, and to foster tourism and cultural participation.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, particularly Articles 7 and 10;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 15; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>498</td>
<td>Digital Skills Cadetship Trial</td>
<td>To fund the trial of cadetships with employers in digital technology fields, to:<br>(a) assist cadets to undertake vocational education and training in digital skills (including education and training provided by employers); and<br>(b) assist cadets with future employment opportunities;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(c) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(d) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(e) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>499</td>
<td>Career Revive Initiative Expansion</td>
<td>To give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 11, by providing assistance to specific employers:<br>(a) to develop an employer action plan to address barriers to women’s full and equal participation in the employer’s workforce; and<br>(b) to promote such full and equal participation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(b) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>500</td>
<td>Outcomes Measurement Initiative—Navigation Tool</td>
<td>To develop, build and maintain an online navigation tool for social impact organisations to access information about social impact investing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>501</td>
<td>Children and Family Intensive Support</td>
<td>To support vulnerable children and their families in the Northern Territory and the Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (APY) lands so that those children grow up strong in families and communities that are safe and nurturing, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18, 19 and 30.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>502</td>
<td>Individual Placement and Support</td>
<td>To improve the employment and education outcomes of people with mental illness through services that focus on the individual needs of people with mental illness who are seeking to enter, or remain in, employment or education, including services that integrate vocational assistance with clinical support and non‑vocational assistance, to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 1 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>503</td>
<td>Digital Work and Study Service</td>
<td>To improve the employment and education outcomes of young people with mental illness by providing work and study support online and by telephone and text message, integrated with clinical support and non‑vocational assistance.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 1 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>504</td>
<td>Birth of a Child project</td>
<td>To provide funding for online platforms that will facilitate the collection and sharing of data for the purpose of enabling access to Commonwealth, State and Territory services by a parent of, or a person with responsibility for, a newborn child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>505</td>
<td>Afghanistan Inquiry Legal Assistance Scheme</td>
<td>To provide funding for legal assistance to current and former serving members of the Australian Defence Force in relation to investigations or proceedings for criminal offences that arise out of the Inspector‑General of the Australian Defence Force’s Afghanistan Inquiry.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>506</td>
<td>COVID‑19 vaccine claims scheme</td>
<td>To provide compensation for individuals who suffer loss or injury as a result of being vaccinated against the coronavirus known as COVID‑19, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits, sickness benefits and medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>507</td>
<td>Addressing child sexual abuse</td>
<td>To prevent child sexual abuse and address the effects of child sexual abuse by providing funding including for activities, assistance, infrastructure, research and services for one or more of the following:<br>(a) the implementation of the National Strategy to Prevent and Respond to Child Sexual Abuse;<br>(b) the implementation of recommendations of the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse;<br>(c) the provision of assistance or support to, or in respect of, victims and survivors of child sexual abuse;<br>(d) the provision of assistance or support to people and organisations who provide support for victims and survivors of child sexual abuse;<br>(e) the provision of assistance or support to organisations to better equip them to prevent and respond to child sexual abuse;<br>(f) raising awareness of, preventing, and addressing the impacts of child sexual abuse.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services or sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 19, 25, 27, 34 and 39;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 12; or<br>(e) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(f) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(g) done in the exercise of executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(h) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(i) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>508</td>
<td>Safeguarding the Integrity of Australian Sport—Australia’s international anti‑doping commitments</td>
<td>To fulfil Australia’s international anti‑doping commitments, including through contributions to:<br>(a) the Oceania Regional Anti‑Doping Organisation; and<br>(b) the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Fund for the Elimination of Doping in Sport; and<br>(c) the World Anti‑Doping Agency.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Convention against Doping in Sport, particularly Articles 5, 14 and 15; or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(c) with respect to Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>509</td>
<td>Care and Support Workforce National Campaign</td>
<td>To increase the size of the care and support workforce by funding a communications campaign to increase public awareness of the employment opportunities that are available in the care and support sector, including in aged care.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>510</td>
<td>Community‑led Solutions</td>
<td>To fund the following to support recipients of social security payments in areas in which the Cashless Debit Card program or the Income Management program are or have operated (including to support Cashless Debit Card program and Income Management program participants while they transition off the programs):<br>(a) services that prevent domestic and family violence and support victims of such violence;<br>(b) services that provide assistance to unemployed persons so that they may prepare for, and find, work;<br>(c) services that provide treatment, rehabilitation, case management services and training assessments for people with mental illness;<br>(d) services that support families so as to ensure the safety and wellbeing of children;<br>(e) services that assist children to prepare them for employment;<br>(f) services that assist recipients of a social security payment to manage their payment, including improvement of their financial and digital literacy;<br>(g) infrastructure which facilitates recipients of a social security payment to access the internet;<br>(h) projects which create jobs for recipients of social security payments.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to being a measure:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) incidental to the provision of maternity allowances, widows’ pensions, child endowment, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness or hospital benefits, medical or dental services, benefits to students or family allowances (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18 and 19;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 6 and 12;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(v) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>511</td>
<td>National early childhood program for children with disability or developmental concerns</td>
<td>To provide information, and deliver community‑based supports, for the benefit of young children aged 0 to 8 years with disability or developmental concerns, including by funding measures to:<br>(a) enable parents and carers to access information about their child’s development and early capacity‑building supports; or<br>(b) help prepare children with disability or developmental concerns for school and other learning environments; or<br>(c) develop the skills and confidence of parents and carers to support their child’s learning and development and connect with services;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(d) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 7 and 24;<br>(e) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 18, 23 and 27.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>512</td>
<td>International Climate Action</td>
<td>To support activities that assist, promote or influence the development or implementation of:<br>(a) international policies and measures in relation to climate change, including through the pursuit of broad based international climate action and agreement; and<br>(b) carbon offset schemes, including in the Indo‑Pacific region; and<br>(c) climate change policies and measures external to Australia, including:<br>(i) accounting systems for greenhouse gases or offset projects; and<br>(ii) supporting the research, development or deployment of low emissions technologies; and<br>(iii) actions to conserve and enhance sinks and reservoirs of greenhouse gases; and<br>(iv) mechanisms to support internationally transferred mitigation outcomes;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(d) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4 and 6;<br>(e) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(f) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 to 13.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding or support with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>513</td>
<td>Community Refugee Integration and Settlement Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to community organisations to provide refugee integration and settlement services to achieve strong integration outcomes through a community‑supported settlement model that provides a dedicated settlement pathway to refugees and humanitarian entrants to Australia, as a measure with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to immigrants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>514</td>
<td>Economic Pathways to Refugee Integration</td>
<td>To provide support to organisations to implement initiatives that lift the rate of refugee and humanitarian entrants’ economic participation, including initiatives which help refugees and humanitarian entrants to:<br>(a) concurrently build English language abilities and vocational skills in areas of workforce shortage; or<br>(b) start their own businesses; or<br>(c) relocate to areas of workforce shortage in regional Australia; or<br>(d) directly access a role with a large employer;<br>as a measure with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing support:<br>(a) involving the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for measures with respect to immigrants; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 3 and 11;<br>(ii) the Convention relating to the Status of Refugees, particularly Article 17;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(iv) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 5;<br>(v) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(vi) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4; or<br>(d) for measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) for measures undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>515</td>
<td>Emerging Aviation Technologies Partnerships Program</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to, and deliver measures that, encourage and enable the development and deployment of emerging aviation technologies to enhance the competitiveness, efficiency and reliability of Australian aviation, including by:<br>(a) expanding employment in the aviation sector; and<br>(b) improving supply chain and market efficiency; and<br>(c) improving connections with regional and remote communities, including Indigenous communities.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing financial assistance or delivering measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>516</td>
<td>Online Formative Assessment Initiative</td>
<td>To provide funding for the development, implementation and maintenance of the Online Formative Assessment Initiative that facilitates access to online teaching resources, tools, student assessments, professional learning and other support for teachers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>517</td>
<td>City‑Country Partnerships Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to facilitate schools engaging in partnerships with remote schools to improve educational outcomes of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students in the remote schools.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>518</td>
<td>Migrant Skills Incentives</td>
<td>To increase the number of skilled migrants who can contribute to the Australian workforce at an appropriate skill level, by funding the development, promotion and provision of:<br>(a) skills assessments; and<br>(b) employability assessments; and<br>(c) skills training;<br>for aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to immigrants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>519</td>
<td>Skills for Education and Employment Program</td>
<td>To enable job seekers to secure sustainable employment or participate in further education, by providing access to language, literacy, numeracy and digital skills training, as benefits to students within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>520</td>
<td>VET system improvements</td>
<td>To support improvements to the vocational education and training (VET) system, including by:<br>(a) developing, maintaining and promoting nationally endorsed training packages; and<br>(b) developing, maintaining and promoting resources and products for use by VET providers; and<br>(c) assisting VET providers with training delivery and assessment; and<br>(d) engaging with industry, schools, VET providers and others to support and promote career pathways and outcomes; and<br>(e) trialling new arrangements for the delivery of training products; and<br>(f) undertaking skills forecasting and responding to emerging skills and workforce challenges;<br>to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(g) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(h) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>521</td>
<td>Australia Day Celebrations</td>
<td>To support Australia Day celebrations, including by providing funding to support the following:<br>(a) Australia Day events;<br>(b) communication campaigns that promote Australia Day;<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(d) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(e) involving the grant of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>522</td>
<td>Online measures to improve price transparency in perishable goods industries</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to research and development corporations and industry representative bodies to support the development and implementation of online measures to improve price transparency in perishable goods industries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>523</td>
<td>Agricultural innovation hubs program</td>
<td>To establish or develop, and operate, agricultural innovation hubs that support innovation in the agricultural, aquaculture, fishery and forestry industries, including by:<br>(a) providing places for activities relating to development, extension, adoption and commercialisation of research and innovations; and<br>(b) carrying out activities including field days, workshops, demonstrations, websites and social media.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) relating to fisheries in Australian waters beyond territorial limits; or<br>(c) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>525</td>
<td>National Cybercrime Capability Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding to Commonwealth, State and Territory agencies to improve Australia’s cybercrime law enforcement capabilities, including for:<br>(a) training to enhance cybercrime investigative skills; and<br>(b) measures to support the sharing of cybercrime intelligence between the Commonwealth and the States and Territories; and<br>(c) improved support for victims of cybercrime.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Cybercrime, particularly Article 14; or<br>(c) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>526</td>
<td>Market Information for Care and Support Providers</td>
<td>To improve and expand care and support services by establishing and maintaining a website to provide information about market demand and supply to the care and support sector, including providers of one or more of the following services:<br>(a) disability care and support services;<br>(b) care and support services for veterans;<br>(c) aged care and support services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>527</td>
<td>Schools Pathways Program</td>
<td>To:<br>(a) provide linkages, and enhance work and career pathways, for students into the Australian defence industry and address specific skills gaps in defence industry capability; and<br>(b) expand the pool of skilled workers from which the Australian defence industry can recruit (including by supporting studies, experiences and educational endeavours in science, technology, engineering and mathematics for students).<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to maintaining Australian defence industry capability; or<br>(b) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 28 and 29;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Article 13; or<br>(d) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>528</td>
<td>Preparing Australian Communities Program—Projects of Local Significance</td>
<td>To support measures to improve the resilience of Australian communities against natural disasters, including by reducing the impact of such disasters when they occur.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(ii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 7 and 8;<br>(iii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(b) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>529</td>
<td>Territories Stolen Generations Redress Scheme</td>
<td>To establish and maintain a scheme known as the Territories Stolen Generations Redress Scheme to provide benefits and promote healing in relation to removals that took place in the Northern Territory prior to self‑government, the Australian Capital Territory prior to self‑government or the Jervis Bay Territory, including by funding the following activities:<br>(a) making payments to:<br>(i) recognise the harm caused by removals; and<br>(ii) facilitate healing;<br>(b) providing direct personal responses;<br>(c) providing legal, financial, counselling and other advisory and support services in relation to the scheme;<br>(d) engaging independent persons to assess applications or perform other roles under the scheme;<br>as a measure with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>530</td>
<td>School Leavers Information Service</td>
<td>To do the following:<br>(a) provide information advice and referral services to support young people to make informed decisions about their career or to transition to further learning or employment;<br>(b) trial supporting job seekers aged 25 years and over through telephone and online services to make informed decisions about their career or to transition to further learning or employment.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>531</td>
<td>mRNA vaccines and treatments</td>
<td>To develop and maintain Australia’s onshore capability to manufacture mRNA vaccines and products, including by purchasing mRNA vaccines and products manufactured onshore, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical, sickness or hospital benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>532</td>
<td>Taskforce for Nature‑related Financial Disclosures</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the Taskforce for Nature‑related Financial Disclosures in activities relating to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>533</td>
<td>Innovation Development Fund (ELICOS)</td>
<td>To support eligible providers of an English Language Intensive Course for Overseas Students to deliver services to overseas students by providing funding:<br>(a) to diversify into online and offshore delivery; and<br>(b) to invest in infrastructure, staff expertise and the marketing and promotion of education services to prepare for the return of onshore international students; and<br>(c) to design curriculums and innovative digital teaching solutions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>534</td>
<td>Northern Australia Business and Community Growth Program</td>
<td>To support the economic development and diversification of Northern Australia by providing funding for infrastructure, workforce, business and community investment projects which create employment and support commercial or economic growth, resilience or diversification in Northern Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(e) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>535</td>
<td>Koala Conservation and Protection</td>
<td>To support the protection of koalas and their habitats by:<br>(a) funding training in koala care, treatment and triage for veterinarians, veterinary nurses, emergency management personnel, first responders, park rangers, and wildlife carers; and<br>(b) providing financial assistance for:<br>(i) projects to protect and restore koala habitat and mitigate threats to koalas; and<br>(ii) research to improve koala health outcomes; and<br>(iii) the implementation of measures to improve koala health outcomes.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 8, 10 and 12; or<br>(b) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>536</td>
<td>Cultivating Australia’s Traceability</td>
<td>To support the ongoing development, implementation and improvement of supply chain traceability systems and arrangements for Australian agricultural exports, and to enable market access and premium pricing for such exports, including through:<br>(a) research and modelling (including pilot projects); and<br>(b) the preparation of a national agricultural traceability roadmap and an agricultural supply chain data standard, as well as other strategies and plans; and<br>(c) support for industry to align with the national roadmap and adopt the data standard; and<br>(d) engagement and cooperation between governments and industry, including a national summit, and the establishment and operation of a community of practice and an advisory board; and<br>(e) the digitisation of export legislation and support for the development of systems that connect with digitised export legislation; and<br>(f) the development and maintenance of an online tool to provide industry with access to information relevant to supply chain traceability (including market intelligence and research into emerging trends); and<br>(g) supporting projects to develop credentials for Australian agricultural exports and promote adherence to credential requirements, and to develop industry‑specific plans for those purposes.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>537</td>
<td>NRL All Stars—State of Mind Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to the National Rugby League to deliver a range of mental health initiatives directed towards Indigenous youth, including:<br>(a) deploying social marketing initiatives relating to mental health and promoting the National Rugby League’s “State of Mind” mental wellbeing campaign; and<br>(b) delivering workshops and health and wellbeing sessions to National Rugby League clubs and teams, and in schools; and<br>(c) engaging with primary schools, and high schools, with a high population of Indigenous youth; and<br>(d) engaging “State of Mind All Stars Advocates” to promote the “State of Mind” mental wellbeing campaign to Indigenous communities.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>538</td>
<td>National Disability Data Asset</td>
<td>To provide funding for the establishment of an enduring National Disability Data Asset, including:<br>(a) building infrastructure and a model for a national data integration system; and<br>(b) linking de‑identified data from Commonwealth, State and Territory service systems; and<br>(c) providing data products on national priorities, including data to support outcomes reporting under the outcomes framework for Australia’s Disability Strategy 2021‑2031; and<br>(d) establishing governance arrangements; and<br>(e) working with the States and Territories and other stakeholders in relation to the matters referred to in paragraphs (a) to (d).<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(c) in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>539</td>
<td>Information, Linkages and Capacity Building</td>
<td>To give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 1, 8, 9, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25, and 29, by:<br>(a) funding projects that:<br>(i) create connections between people with disability, their families and carers and the communities they live in; and<br>(ii) build the knowledge, skills and confidence of people with disability, their families and carers; and<br>(iii) improve access to community and mainstream services for people with disability; and<br>(b) providing resources and delivering activities to support prospective applicants to apply for that funding and to deliver those projects; and<br>(c) providing opportunities for funding recipients to connect with each other and to share experiences and lessons from the delivery of funded projects.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>541</td>
<td>Australian Agriculture Visa program</td>
<td>To support the development and implementation of an Australian Agriculture Visa program.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to immigration or emigration; or<br>(c) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>542</td>
<td>Pacific Australia Labour Mobility Scheme</td>
<td>To support a circular mobility program to provide workers from Pacific island countries and Timor‑Leste with the opportunity to take up temporary seasonal and non‑seasonal work opportunities in Australia, including by providing assistance to those workers, and their families, to support or otherwise enable those workers to do one or more of the following:<br>(a) deploy to Australia;<br>(b) participate in the program while in Australia;<br>(c) reintegrate into their home country.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to immigration or emigration; or<br>(c) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>543</td>
<td>Support for the Republic of Palau</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to, or for the benefit of, the Republic of Palau, as a measure with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>545</td>
<td>Competitive fund for micro‑credentials (pilot program)</td>
<td>To develop micro‑credentials for international delivery by tertiary education providers.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>546</td>
<td>Scaling up Success in Remote Schools</td>
<td>To provide funding to improve educational outcomes of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students in regional and remote areas.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>547</td>
<td>Workforce Australia</td>
<td>To help job seekers find and keep a job by:<br>(a) providing employment and related assessments and services which assist job seekers to find and keep a job with suitable employers; and<br>(b) providing activities, including in not‑for‑profit and government organisations, to help prepare job seekers for the work environment; and<br>(c) engaging a panel of Workforce Specialists to identify and deliver projects that provide job seekers with opportunities in areas of workforce demand.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, allowances, benefits, endowments or services of the kind described in paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning the Organisation of the Employment Service, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 to 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>548</td>
<td>Veteran Wellbeing</td>
<td>To fund organisations that provide support to veterans and their families by means that include:<br>(a) undertaking projects to facilitate:<br>(i) the health and social wellbeing of veterans and their families; and<br>(ii) access to community services by veterans and their families; and<br>(b) assisting veterans and their families in the veterans’ transition to civilian life.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>549</td>
<td>Australian Government Disaster Recovery Payment (Special Supplement)</td>
<td>To provide payments to persons who have been directly affected by a natural disaster event, such as flooding, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>550</td>
<td>Community‑led Economic Development</td>
<td>To support employment in areas in which the Cashless Debit Card program and the Income Management program are or have operated by funding infrastructure projects and capital investments that do one or more of the following in those areas:<br>(a) create jobs and training opportunities;<br>(b) support community economic development;<br>(c) build community capacity.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>551</td>
<td>Assistance to Ukraine</td>
<td>To assist the government and people of Ukraine in relation to threats to their security, including through the supply of fuel for their energy system.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>552</td>
<td>Emergency income relief—2022 floods</td>
<td>To provide payments to eligible persons who are in areas directly affected by the 2022 floods and who have been unable to earn their usual income as a result of the floods, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>553</td>
<td>ADS‑B Rebate Program</td>
<td>To enhance the safety, regularity and efficiency of air navigation in Australia, by providing financial assistance to enable participants to install or carry equipment enabling Automatic Dependent Surveillance Broadcast (ADS‑B) capability in aircraft that operate under Visual Flight Rules.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>554</td>
<td>Australian Apprenticeships Incentive System</td>
<td>To provide funding, including for apprentices and employers of apprentices, to encourage and support the commencement and completion of apprenticeships.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 27;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>555</td>
<td>Veterans’ Chaplaincy Program—Pilot</td>
<td>To deliver chaplaincy support services to veterans and their families.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>556</td>
<td>Youpla Group Funeral Benefits Program</td>
<td>To make payments to eligible persons in respect of the death of a person whose death was covered by an eligible funeral insurance policy issued by a company in the group of companies known as the Youpla Group, in circumstances where the policy has been affected by the collapse and liquidation of those companies.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to bankruptcy or insolvency (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xvii) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>557</td>
<td>Co‑operative and Mutual Enterprises Support Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Business Council of Co‑operatives and Mutuals to support co‑operative and mutual enterprises to provide aged care, disability care, veterans’ care and primary and allied healthcare.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to support veterans and defence force members and their families; or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 25;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>558</td>
<td>Promoting quality in the existing teacher workforce</td>
<td>To fund the development and delivery of courses and programs that support the professional development of teachers.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>559</td>
<td>Australia’s Disability Strategy 2021‑2031</td>
<td>To give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13, 16, 24, 25, 27 and 28, by:<br>(a) improving disability service systems; and<br>(b) supporting disability advocacy services; and<br>(c) supporting early intervention for children with disability; and<br>(d) connecting people with disability to work, including by establishing disability leadership networks; and<br>(e) building positive community attitudes towards people with disability; and<br>(f) funding disability research.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>560</td>
<td>Legacy House Brisbane</td>
<td>To support the establishment of a centre to provide support services to veterans and their families.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>561</td>
<td>Recognising the service of First World War Veterans whose graves are unmarked</td>
<td>To contribute to the provision of private grave markers recognising the service of First World War Veterans who are not eligible for official commemoration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>562</td>
<td>Scott Palmer Services Centre</td>
<td>To support the establishment of accommodation in the Northern Territory for veterans experiencing homelessness.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>563</td>
<td>Bursaries to attract students into teaching</td>
<td>To increase the number of students entering teaching by funding, as benefits to students, bursaries to support students who are undertaking study for a recognised initial teacher education qualification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>564</td>
<td>First Nations Educators in primary schools program</td>
<td>To enable the placement in primary schools of First Nations Educators to teach First Nations languages and First Nations cultures.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 28 and 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>565</td>
<td>Justice Services—education and training for the justice sector on family, domestic and sexual violence</td>
<td>To support the education and training of persons involved in the enforcement and administration of the law (including legal practitioners, judicial officers, court administrators and law enforcement officers) about family, domestic and sexual violence, including by funding any of the following:<br>(a) training on how to identify and support victims of family violence (including victims of coercive control);<br>(b) training for law enforcement officers on how to identify and respond appropriately to family, domestic and sexual violence;<br>(c) training for judicial officers to be delivered by the National Judicial College of Australia;<br>(d) maintaining the National Domestic and Family Violence Bench Book by the Australasian Institute of Judicial Administration;<br>(e) education, training or information on the nature and impacts of family, domestic and sexual violence.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 19; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) incidental to the execution of any power vested by the Constitution in the Federal Judicature.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>566</td>
<td>Justice Services—justice reinvestment</td>
<td>To reduce the incarceration of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people by funding justice reinvestment, including by funding any of the following:<br>(a) assistance to communities to develop or implement justice reinvestment strategies and programs;<br>(b) services that will reduce or prevent the possibility of incarceration (such as counselling, recreation, housing and other support services);<br>(c) criminal diversion and post‑release support programs;<br>(d) activities to build the capacity of entities to provide justice reinvestment such as:<br>(i) providing advice on governance and strategy; and<br>(ii) providing data collection and analysis; and<br>(iii) purchasing assets and infrastructure to be used in justice reinvestment activities; and<br>(iv) providing information technology support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>567</td>
<td>Improve the Long‑term Sustainability of the South East Trawl Fishery and Support Fishers</td>
<td>To assist local industry to manage the impact of management changes in the Commonwealth South East Trawl Fishery in response to the decline in numbers of important commercial fish species, including by providing funding to eligible fishers in the Commonwealth South East Trawl Fishery who surrender their statutory fishing rights. This includes assisting local industry to manage the impact of any closure of parts of the Commonwealth South East Trawl Fishery that might result from such management changes.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for measures with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>568</td>
<td>Bolstering Australia’s Biosecurity System—Protecting Australia from escalating exotic animal disease risks</td>
<td>To prepare for, and strengthen Australia’s ability to respond to, escalating biosecurity risks from countries to the north of Australia. This includes measures to:<br>(a) prevent the entry into, and spread within, Australia of foot and mouth disease and lumpy skin disease; and<br>(b) enhance capability in northern Australia to detect and respond to the arrival of other exotic pests and diseases; and<br>(c) combat the spread of foot and mouth disease, lumpy skin disease and other emerging animal diseases in countries in the Indo‑Pacific region.<br>This objective has the effect it would have it if were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with quarantine; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 7 and 8; or<br>(c) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relationship with foreign countries; or<br>(d) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>569</td>
<td>National Forest Products Innovation</td>
<td>To provide funding to enhance Australia’s productivity and competitiveness through forestry research, development and innovation and to improve Australia’s sovereign capability in timber production, including by:<br>(a) providing funding to establish and support the operation of an Australia‑wide National Institute for Forest Products Innovation, comprising a central hub and regional research centres, to support forestry research and innovation; and<br>(b) continuing funding for the establishment and operation (including the provision of extension services) of Regional Forestry Hubs;<br>as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>The objective also has the effect it would have it if were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>570</td>
<td>Support Regional Trade Events</td>
<td>To provide funding to support industry events and forums that foster and encourage interstate and overseas trade and commerce by promoting agricultural sectors in Australia, including businesses that are in or support these sectors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>571</td>
<td>National Nurse and Midwife Health Service</td>
<td>To fund services (including counselling and other support services, and referral services) for nurses and midwives, and nursing and midwifery students, experiencing health issues.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7 and 17;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>572</td>
<td>National Messaging System</td>
<td>To establish and maintain a national messaging system that enables the Australian Government to send, or to support State and Territory governments to send, messages to the public, or targeted sections of the public, in relation to emergencies, disasters or events of national significance, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>573</td>
<td>Broadcasting Resilience Program</td>
<td>To fund improvements in the resilience of infrastructure that may be used for emergency broadcasting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>574</td>
<td>Telecommunications Resilience Disaster and Innovation Program</td>
<td>To fund the development and deployment of:<br>(a) improvements in the resilience of telecommunications facilities including against the impacts of power outages and natural hazards, particularly for vulnerable communities, and<br>(b) new technologies and solutions to improve the resilience of telecommunications services and networks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>575</td>
<td>On Farm Connectivity Program</td>
<td>To fund the costs of purchasing, delivering and installing equipment, and other costs associated with enabling the use of that equipment (for example, use subscriptions), that does either or both of the following:<br>(a) improves farmers’ access to telecommunications services;<br>(b) supports farming practices through the use of telecommunications services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>576</td>
<td>Terrestrial Television Transmission for Shortland, NSW</td>
<td>To fund the design, acquisition, construction, modification, and operation of infrastructure to improve digital television reception in the federal electoral division of Shortland in New South Wales.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>577</td>
<td>Investing in Our Communities Program</td>
<td>To build resilient communities and increase community liveability by providing funding for infrastructure projects.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more treaties; or<br>(e) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>578</td>
<td>Priority Community Infrastructure Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for the construction and upgrading of infrastructure, including community infrastructure.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more treaties; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>579</td>
<td>Payments to the International Whaling Commission</td>
<td>To provide funding to enhance Australia’s leadership in the International Whaling Commission by paying financial contributions to aid the International Whaling Commission’s financial sustainability and build its whale conservation expertise and agenda.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>580</td>
<td>National Biodiversity Market</td>
<td>To support the operation of a national biodiversity market by providing funding:<br>(a) for the development of innovative ways of assessing and monitoring biodiversity change at the project and landscape scale; and<br>(b) for research partnerships to support the delivery of methods and inputs for biodiversity assessment; and<br>(c) to ensure that key biodiversity assessment methods, models and information sources are fit for purpose to support the operation of the biodiversity market; and<br>(d) to assist organisations and persons, including natural resource management organisations, to improve their understanding of environmental markets; and<br>(e) to enable organisations and persons, including natural resource management organisations, to assist landholders in developing and implementing projects under existing and emerging environmental markets, including under the <i>Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011</i>; and<br>(f) to expand a project development and market platform to include an automated trading system for the private sector and landholders.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 8 and 10;<br>(ii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>581</td>
<td>Protecting the Great Barrier Reef and securing reef jobs</td>
<td>To protect, restore and conserve the Great Barrier Reef by providing funding:<br>(a) for the purpose of supporting local councils involved in the Reef Guardian Councils program to deliver projects proposed in Reef Action Plans prepared under that program; and<br>(b) to Central Queensland University to assist with costs associated with establishing the Coastal Marine Ecosystems Research Centre, and to support that Centre’s work.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, particularly Articles 4 and 5; or<br>(b) in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>582</td>
<td>ReMade in Australia</td>
<td>To establish and promote the trade marked ‘ReMade in Australia’ brand, including:<br>(a) establishing a licensing scheme for the use of the trade mark that is administered by a non‑government licensing body; and<br>(b) undertaking communications activities to promote the trade mark.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>583</td>
<td>Saving Native Species</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities to protect and support the recovery of Australian plant and animal species, and places, including to:<br>(a) protect, rehabilitate and support the recovery of, and prevent the extinction of, threatened native species and their habitats, and threatened ecological communities; and<br>(b) protect the biodiversity of the Wet Tropics of Queensland World Heritage Area and the Bowling Green Bay Ramsar internationally important wetland from invasive yellow crazy ants, including by providing support to the Wet Tropics Management Authority; and<br>(c) support coordination of recovery actions and monitoring of threatened species and their habitats, including by developing threat abatement spatial planning tools for land managers to protect threatened species on their land.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, particularly Articles 4 and 5;<br>(ii) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 7, 8, 9 and 10;<br>(iii) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Articles 3 and 4; or<br>(b) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>584</td>
<td>Engaging with First Nations Peoples on Climate Change</td>
<td>To provide funding to:<br>(a) support the creation and implementation of a coordinated approach to climate change issues with Torres Strait Islander and other First Nations communities, including by establishing and supporting the Torres Strait Climate Centre of Excellence; and<br>(b) establish and support activities to assist Torres Strait Islander and other First Nations communities to respond to climate change; and<br>(c) support the extension of activities described in paragraphs (a) and (b) to people in the islands of the Pacific.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to the people of any race for whom it is deemed necessary to make special laws; or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(c) with respect to Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>585</td>
<td>Referendum Engagement Group</td>
<td>To provide funding to enable the Referendum Engagement Group to meet to discuss building community awareness and understanding of, and support for, a referendum to alter the Constitution to provide for an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Voice, and to discuss building support for an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Voice enshrined in the Constitution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>586</td>
<td>Commonwealth Regional Scholarship Program</td>
<td>To fund a scholarship program to support students from regional and remote Australia to attend boarding school, or live at a boarding facility while attending school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>587</td>
<td>Consent and Respectful Relationships Education</td>
<td>To fund the States, Territories and non‑government representative bodies for the delivery of consent and respectful relationships education in schools.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 1, 2, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 9 and 19; or<br>(b) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>588</td>
<td>Status Resolution and Support Services—special purpose visa holders</td>
<td>To provide needs‑based support and assistance to holders of a special purpose visa under section 33 of the <i>Migration Act 1958</i>:<br>(a) as they seek to more permanently resolve their immigration status, or<br>(b) for whom there is no available pathway by which they can more permanently resolve their immigration status.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>589</td>
<td>Carbon Farming Outreach Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for the development and delivery of training, advice and tools to support farmers and land managers to engage in carbon markets and adopt low emission technologies and practices in the agriculture and land management sectors.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(ii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(iii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(b) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(c) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>590</td>
<td>Delivering the Basin Plan Program</td>
<td>To fund the recovery of environmental water from the Murray‑Darling Basin water resources, including through the following mechanisms:<br>(a) the purchase of water access entitlements;<br>(b) the provision of grants to organisations to purchase land and water parcels.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the international agreements referred to in the definition of <b><i>relevant international agreement</b></i> in subsection 4(1) of the <i>Water Act 2007</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>591</td>
<td>Energy efficiency grants for small and medium enterprises</td>
<td>To support small and medium‑sized enterprises to improve energy efficiency and reduce energy costs, including by upgrading or replacing equipment with new lower‑emissions technologies, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 3 and 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>592</td>
<td>Landcare Rangers Program</td>
<td>To:<br>(a) support the employment and upskilling of landcare rangers; and<br>(b) establish and support landcare facilitators;<br>to undertake activities directed towards protecting and restoring Australia’s environment and heritage.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, particularly Articles 4 and 5;<br>(ii) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 7, 8, 9, 10 and 13;<br>(iii) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Articles 3 and 4;<br>(iv) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4 and 6; or<br>(c) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>593</td>
<td>Vietnamese labour mobility for work in relation to primary industries in Australia</td>
<td>To support a mobility program that assists citizens of Vietnam to take up temporary seasonal and non‑seasonal work opportunities in, or in relation to, primary industries in Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>594</td>
<td>Pacific Engagement Visa</td>
<td>To fund a broad range of services to support citizens of Pacific Island countries and Timor‑Leste and members of their immediate family to find employment and settle in Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to immigration or emigration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>595</td>
<td>Protecting Australia’s National Interest in Critical and Emerging Technologies</td>
<td>To enhance Australia’s ability to influence the development of international standards in critical and emerging technologies, including by:<br>(a) supporting entities (whether public or private) to promote Australia’s interests in the development of those standards; and<br>(b) building international partnerships; and<br>(c) establishing systems to enable the Commonwealth to monitor and advise on the development of those standards;<br>as a measure in relation to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>596</td>
<td>Grants‑in‑Aid</td>
<td>To provide funding to national ex‑service organisations to support veterans and their families.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>597</td>
<td>Productivity, Education and Training Fund</td>
<td>To provide assistance to representative employers’ and workers’ organisations to:<br>(a) support engagement by representative employers’ and workers’ organisations, and their members, through enhanced tripartite governance structures across the Commonwealth workplace relations portfolio, to inform Commonwealth policy development; and<br>(b) enable running of workplace productivity, education and training initiatives by representative employers’ and workers’ organisations to support their members to engage in Commonwealth law reform processes, encourage take up of new Commonwealth laws in their workplaces, and monitor and evaluate implementation of Commonwealth law reforms on the ground; and<br>(c) ensure greater emphasis on tripartite engagement and social dialogue to deliver the Commonwealth Government’s workplace relations reform agenda and allow appropriate engagement on reforms by key peak agencies to manage the broad impacts of reforms; and<br>(d) enable representative employers’ and workers’ organisations, as key intermediaries, to raise awareness of Commonwealth workplace reforms among persons who are subject to those laws, which will help increase compliance with Commonwealth workplace laws and reduce the regulatory burden associated with unintended non‑compliance.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 7;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Labour Administration: Role, Functions and Organisation, particularly Articles 2, 4, 5 and 6; or<br>(b) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>598</td>
<td>Forced Adoption Support Services—Commemoration and Capacity‑Building</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) national and local activities to commemorate the tenth anniversary of the National Apology for Forced Adoptions; and<br>(b) the development and publication of online resources to complement those activities, and to serve as a commemorative and educational resource; and<br>(c) the development and publication of online training modules to help providers of support services and aged care to address the needs of people affected by past forced adoption practices.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>599</td>
<td>Referendum civics education and awareness program</td>
