<td>To fund public civics education and awareness programs, community initiatives and other activities to raise public awareness of, and community engagement with, a referendum to recognise Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples in the Constitution through an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Voice.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>600</td>
<td>Financial counselling services for veterans—pilot program</td>
<td>To support veterans and defence force members, and their families, by providing funding to The Trustee for Australian Defence Force Assistance Trust trading as Bravery Trust to pilot a financial counselling service for those veterans, members and families.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>601</td>
<td>Murray‑Darling Basin Aboriginal Water Entitlements Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the purchase and management of water entitlements in the Murray‑Darling Basin for the benefit of First Nations communities in the Murray‑Darling Basin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>602</td>
<td>Environmental legal services</td>
<td>To provide funding to environmental legal assistance organisations to:<br>(a) provide legal information and legal assistance services (including legal advice and legal representation):<br>(i) to persons in relation to matters in the federal jurisdiction or in relation to Commonwealth laws; or<br>(ii) specifically targeted to assist Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people; or<br>(iii) to persons in a Territory; or<br>(b) provide legal information and assistance services through the use of telephone and online communication services; or<br>(c) provide for online and telephone communication between environmental legal assistance organisations; or<br>(d) evaluate or improve the matters referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c) above.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) incidental to the execution of the legislative powers vested in the Commonwealth; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>603</td>
<td>Goyder Institute for Water Research Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Goyder Institute for Water Research to support or facilitate its activities or programs, including the following:<br>(a) research programs (including activities supporting the dissemination of research and knowledge exchange);<br>(b) training and education programs;<br>(c) communication and engagement programs;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(d) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 12 and 13;<br>(e) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Articles 3 and 4;<br>(f) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Articles 4 and 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>604</td>
<td>National Resource Sharing Centre</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Australasian Fire and Emergency Service Authorities Council Limited for the National Resource Sharing Centre, the role of which is to coordinate and facilitate the deployment of resources and assets in preparing for, and responding to, disasters in Australia and overseas.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia, or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>605</td>
<td>National Emergency Management Stockpile</td>
<td>To support the development, maintenance and deployment of a National Emergency Management Stockpile of critical disaster response and relief resources to augment State and Territory capabilities to respond to disasters of national significance, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>606</td>
<td>National livestock traceability reform to enhance agricultural biosecurity in relation to exports</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the improvement and enhancement of the national livestock traceability database and associated systems and activities.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>607</td>
<td>Build renewable fuels plant in the Burdekin region</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the development and operation of a facility in the Burdekin region to utilise sugar cane waste to produce renewable fuels, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>608</td>
<td>Assisted Reproductive Technology Storage Funding Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to organisations to store, for future use, eggs, sperm or embryos as part of, or incidental to, the provision of medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution) to:<br>(a) persons with cancer; or<br>(b) persons who are at risk of passing on genetic diseases or conditions and whose eggs, sperm or embryos have undergone preimplantation genetic testing in relation to which a medicare benefit under the <i>Health Insurance Act 1973</i> is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>609</td>
<td>Protecting Our Communities (Disaster Resilience) Program</td>
<td>To improve the ability of communities to endure and respond to natural disasters, by:<br>(a) funding the development, installation, improvement or alteration of telecommunications infrastructure; and<br>(b) funding projects to reduce the possibility of bushfires, assist with extinguishing bushfires or reduce the impact of bushfires on communities (including on communities’ ability to use telecommunications infrastructure during and after natural disasters), especially given the increased risk and effect of bushfires due to climate change; and<br>(c) funding the development, installation, improvement or alteration of infrastructure to help First Nations communities to endure and respond to natural disasters.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 7 and 8.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>610</td>
<td>Third country settlement support</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the settlement of non‑citizens in a foreign country, where settlement occurs pursuant to an arrangement between Australia and the foreign country.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>611</td>
<td>Jindelara Cottage—Permanent Accommodation</td>
<td>To fund the refurbishment and construction of permanent accommodation at Jindelara Cottage for people with disabilities, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligation under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 9, 19 and 28.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>612</td>
<td>Sustain myGov</td>
<td>To provide funding for the continued operation and maintenance of the online platform known as myGov, including to enable the use of myGov to access Commonwealth, State and Territory services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>613</td>
<td>Disability Worker COVID‑19 Leave Payments</td>
<td>To provide, as a sickness benefit (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution), payments to individuals (through the reimbursement of payments made by an individual’s employer) who:<br>(a) provide close personal support to National Disability Insurance Scheme participants; and<br>(b) are unable to earn their usual income due to testing positive for the coronavirus known as COVID‑19; and<br>(c) have, or had, no available paid leave entitlements to cover the period of their inability to earn their usual income.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>614</td>
<td>Workforce Advisory Services Program</td>
<td>To support aged care providers facing workforce challenges, including in relation to attracting, retaining and training workforce members, through:<br>(a) the provision of advice relating to workforce management; and<br>(b) offering linkages to critical workforce programs and initiatives.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to bankruptcy or insolvency (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xvii) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>615</td>
<td>Electronic prescribing system</td>
<td>To secure and sustain an electronic system for the exchange of information about prescribed medicines, including by funding:<br>(a) new or improved technology platforms and infrastructure, hardware, software, and related services; and<br>(b) operating and interoperability costs;<br>as a measure with respect to the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, pharmaceutical benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>616</td>
<td>Superannuation consumer advocate</td>
<td>To fund a superannuation consumer advocate to:<br>(a) represent the interests of superannuation members in superannuation‑related policy debates for the purpose of informing the development of Commonwealth policy; and<br>(b) conduct research and analysis on superannuation‑related issues affecting superannuation members for the purposes of:<br>(i) informing the development of Commonwealth policy; and<br>(ii) assisting superannuation members to understand the operation of Commonwealth laws and policies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>617</td>
<td>Growing Regions Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for capital works for community infrastructure across regional Australia, including capital works for Indigenous community infrastructure across regional Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more treaties, including the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(e) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>618</td>
<td>National Road Safety Action Grants Program</td>
<td>To reduce deaths and injuries from road crashes in Australia by funding activities or projects that relate to non‑infrastructure commitments in the National Road Safety Action Plan 2023‑25.<br>This objective has the effect it would have it if were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>619</td>
<td>Regional Precincts and Partnerships Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to State, Territory and local governments, universities and not‑for‑profit organisations to support the planning and delivery of precincts in regional, rural and remote areas, including for the benefit of Indigenous Australians.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more treaties, including the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4;<br>(iv) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(v) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 and 7; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>620</td>
<td>Extension of National Centre for Asia Capability</td>
<td>To facilitate trade and investment between Australia and Asia by funding the University of Melbourne (ABN 84 002 705 224) to continue the National Centre for Asia Capability (known as Asialink Business) so that it can support Australian businesses to expand and engage with Asian markets, including by facilitating leadership programs, outreach initiatives and market preparedness courses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>621</td>
<td>Smoking and Vaping Cessation</td>
<td>To support people to quit smoking and vaping by:<br>(a) improving access to evidence‑based smoking and vaping cessation information and support through:<br>(i) the development and implementation of a national consumer digital cessation hub to provide access to information, resources and support; and<br>(ii) the redevelopment of the My Quit Buddy mobile application; and<br>(iii) the provision of funding to State and Territory Quitline and Quit services to expand their workforce, train counsellors and enhance the use of technology to increase efficiencies; and<br>(b) improving the capacity of the health sector and health workforce to provide evidence‑based cessation support to patients through:<br>(i) ensuring best practice clinical guidance is available for health professionals; and<br>(ii) providing education and training to health professionals on evidence‑based practices to support patients to quit smoking and vaping; and<br>(c) developing and delivering anti‑smoking and anti‑vaping public health campaigns, in particular:<br>(i) a national campaign aimed at reaching priority and at‑risk population groups; and<br>(ii) a targeted education strategy to address vaping among young people.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, particularly Articles 5, 12 and 14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>622</td>
<td>Youth Suicide, Self‑Harm and Waitlist Management Strategy</td>
<td>To provide funding to headspace Newcastle to deliver suicide prevention services and mental health services, including funding to:<br>(a) support young people who are at risk of suicide or who have attempted suicide and their families; and<br>(b) support young people who are experiencing self‑harm; and<br>(c) support young people who have been bereaved by suicide; and<br>(d) implement strategies to reduce the wait times for accessing headspace Newcastle’s services; and<br>(e) provide safety planning training to headspace Newcastle staff; and<br>(f) increase referral pathways between acute clinical services and headspace Newcastle; and<br>(g) provide support for staff at high schools where a young person has died by suicide; and<br>(h) increase the staffing profile and premises of, and diversity of services delivered by, headspace Newcastle.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligation under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>623</td>
<td>Community Language Schools Grants Program</td>
<td>To support community language schools to deliver language education to preschool‑aged and school‑aged children, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 29;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>624</td>
<td>Go‑Green Co‑Innovation Program</td>
<td>To facilitate collaboration between Australian small and medium‑sized enterprises and Singaporean businesses in jointly undertaking projects that drive the decarbonisation of economic activities, or help Australia or Singapore to transition to net zero emissions, where the projects:<br>(a) are delivered in Singapore; or<br>(b) involve trade and commerce between Singapore and Australia; or<br>(c) foster or promote trade and commerce between Singapore and Australia;<br>as a measure with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>625</td>
<td>National Plan to End Violence against Women and Children 2022‑2032</td>
<td>To prevent family, domestic and sexual violence, and reduce the incidence and impact of such violence, including by:<br>(a) developing prevention measures and strategies in coordination with the States and Territories and non‑government organisations; and<br>(b) supporting and assisting women and children who are at risk of, or are victims of, such violence, including by providing legal, medical, housing, financial and other support; and<br>(c) funding measures to address the drivers of such violence; and<br>(d) funding measures to change attitudes and behaviours that support or condone such violence; and<br>(e) funding prevention, early intervention and response measures targeted towards perpetrators of, and people at risk of using, such violence, including measures to:<br>(i) assist them to change their violent and controlling behaviour; and<br>(ii) provide them with accommodation and other types of support in order to reduce the impacts of that behaviour on women and children; and<br>(f) training students, workers and volunteers to enable them to:<br>(i) provide to women and children who are at risk of, or are victims of, such violence the assistance and support mentioned in paragraph (b); and<br>(ii) provide to perpetrators of, and people at risk of using, such violence the assistance and support mentioned in paragraph (e); and<br>(g) targeting prevention of such violence against, and reduction in the incidence and impact of such violence on, the following groups:<br>(i) women and children;<br>(ii) LGBTQIA+ people;<br>(iii) people with disability;<br>(iv) people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds;<br>(v) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people; and<br>(h) supporting education initiatives aimed at preventing such violence and at being in healthy and non‑violent relationships; and<br>(i) supporting and disseminating research into such violence, including research into:<br>(i) the drivers and prevalence of such violence; and<br>(ii) attitudes towards such violence; and<br>(iii) interventions that reduce the incidence and impact of such violence.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to census and statistics; or<br>(c) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services, or unemployment, pharmaceutical or sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(f) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(g) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 6, 15 and 16;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 19, 34 and 36;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7 and 9;<br>(v) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 11 and 12; or<br>(h) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(i) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(j) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>626</td>
<td>First Nations Heritage Grants program</td>
<td>To support:<br>(a) the Australian Government’s commitment to add Indigenous heritage values to World Heritage‑listed and National Heritage‑listed places; and<br>(b) First Nations leadership on the protection of Indigenous heritage values by funding projects on‑Country;<br>including:<br>(c) the identification and assessment of Indigenous heritage values; and<br>(d) preparing and updating management plans; and<br>(e) providing access for First Nations people to express cultural practice; and<br>(f) facilitating First Nations people and organisations to undertake capacity‑building workshops; and<br>(g) providing on‑ground works for the protection of Indigenous heritage values.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>627</td>
<td>Powering the Regions Fund—safeguard transformation stream</td>
<td>To provide funding for decarbonisation activities at trade‑exposed facilities covered by the safeguard mechanism as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>628</td>
<td>Powering the Regions Fund—critical inputs to clean energy industries: cement, lime, alumina and aluminium sectors program</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the cement, lime, alumina and aluminium industries to:<br>(a) maintain a presence in Australia and continue to deliver critical inputs for the infrastructure and supply chains needed for Australia to be a renewable energy powerhouse; or<br>(b) decarbonise; or<br>(c) support sectoral transformation to achieve Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(d) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(e) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(f) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>629</td>
<td>Powering the Regions Fund—critical inputs to clean energy industries: primary steel production sector program</td>
<td>To provide funding to the primary steel production industry to:<br>(a) maintain a presence in Australia and continue to deliver critical inputs for the infrastructure and supply chains needed for Australia to be a renewable energy powerhouse; or<br>(b) decarbonise;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(c) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(d) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(e) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>630</td>
<td>Provision of commercial television services over Viewer Access Satellite Television</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the provision of free‑to‑air commercial television broadcasting services via satellite for viewers in remote areas, and viewers in other areas who do not have adequate reception of an applicable terrestrial digital commercial television broadcasting service (within the meaning of section 130ZG of the <i>Broadcasting Services Act 1992</i>).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>631</td>
<td>Behaviour Support Training Program</td>
<td>To fund the development and provision of training for disability workers and other providers delivering supports to participants in the National Disability Insurance Scheme with a psychosocial disability, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligation under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 25 and 26;<br>(b) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>632</td>
<td>Volunteering Awareness Campaign</td>
<td>To fund a communications campaign for the following purposes:<br>(a) to deliver campaign materials and messaging on the internet (including social media), and through television and radio, to:<br>(i) raise awareness and understanding of volunteering within the general public; and<br>(ii) highlight the various ways in which people can contribute by volunteering; and<br>(iii) address declining rates of volunteering within the general public;<br>(b) to encourage volunteering by members of the following groups:<br>(i) First Nations people;<br>(ii) new migrants to Australia;<br>(iii) persons with a disability;<br>(iv) women;<br>(v) persons aged under 18 years.<br>This objective has the effect it would have it if were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Article 3;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 19;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>633</td>
<td>Financial assistance scheme for respondents to applications brought under the <i>Family Law (Child Abduction Convention) Regulations 1986</i></td>
<td>To fund a scheme to provide for respondents to applications for orders under the <i>Family Law (Child Abduction Convention) Regulations 1986</i> to:<br>(a) obtain legal representation and advice for the purposes of those proceedings, including any appeal and any associated alternative dispute resolution processes; and<br>(b) pay for any necessary expenses incurred in responding to those applications (such as court fees, expert witness fees and other expenses of a kind ordinarily incurred in litigation).<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with divorce and matrimonial causes, including in relation to parental rights or the custody and guardianship of infants; or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>634</td>
<td>Assisted Passage Program</td>
<td>To provide funding:<br>(a) for:<br>(i) health screening; and<br>(ii) assisted passage; and<br>(iii) identity verification or other services relating to a person’s visa application; and<br>(iv) related costs;<br>for persons who have applied for, or been granted, a visa under the refugee category of the offshore humanitarian program; and<br>(b) for:<br>(i) health screening; and<br>(ii) travel documents; and<br>(iii) transit for identity verification services; and<br>(iv) related costs;<br>for persons who have applied for, or been granted, a visa under the global special humanitarian program of the offshore humanitarian program; and<br>(c) for:<br>(i) health screening; and<br>(ii) assisted passage; and<br>(iii) related costs;<br>for persons who have departed from, will be departing from, or have been displaced from, Afghanistan and who have been granted a Subclass 449 (Humanitarian Stay (Temporary)) visa;<br>as a measure with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>635</td>
<td>Settlement support programs</td>
<td>To fund services and activities to support eligible non‑citizens, including humanitarian entrants, to settle in Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to immigrants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>636</td>
<td>Advice, advocacy and support services for working women</td>
<td>To advance the rights of girls and women (including people who identify as a girl or woman regardless of their designated sex at birth) by funding persons to do one or more of the following:<br>(a) to provide information, education or legal advice to girls and women about their rights and obligations under Commonwealth, State and Territory workplace relations laws, including laws concerning anti‑discrimination, sexual harassment, bullying, workplace health and safety, long service leave and superannuation;<br>(b) to provide information and advice to girls and women about the operation of any Commonwealth law, policy or program;<br>(c) to provide legal advice and representation to girls and women in connection with:<br>(i) resolving a complaint about conduct that may be contrary to a law of a kind referred to in paragraph (a) above; or<br>(ii) a proceeding that involves an issue about a right or obligation under a law of a kind referred to in paragraph (a) above;<br>(d) to promote an understanding and acceptance of, and compliance with, a law of a kind referred to in paragraph (a) above, including by providing information or training to employers, employees and educational institutions;<br>(e) to promote gender equality in the workplace, including by providing information and training to employers on how to develop or implement a gender equality strategy;<br>(f) to represent the interests of girls and women in policy debates about the rights of workers for the purpose of informing the development of Commonwealth policy;<br>(g) to coordinate and support the provision of services delivered by persons that receive funding under the program, including by developing resources and undertaking research.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 3 and 11;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 3 and 7;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Labour Administration: Role, Functions and Organisation, particularly Articles 2 and 6; or<br>(c) incidental to the execution of the legislative powers vested in the Commonwealth; or<br>(d) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>637</td>
<td>Aged Care Work Value Case—historical leave provisions</td>
<td>To implement the outcome of the Fair Work Commission’s decision on the Aged Care Work Value Case by assisting aged care and veterans’ care service providers to meet the costs of historical leave provisions for aged care and veterans’ care service workers.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to support veterans and their families; or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>638</td>
<td>Aged Care Worker COVID‑19 Leave Payments</td>
<td>To provide, as a sickness benefit (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution), payments to individuals (through the reimbursement of payments made by an individual’s employer) who:<br>(a) provide aged care services (including home care services); and<br>(b) are unable to earn their usual income due to testing positive for the coronavirus known as COVID‑19; and<br>(c) have, or had, no available paid sick leave entitlements to cover the period of their inability to earn their usual income.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>640</td>
<td>Community Energy Upgrades Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding for energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to facilities owned or operated by local governments as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>641</td>
<td>Emergency Services Training for Electric Vehicles</td>
<td>To provide funding for the development and communication of EV safety guidance, demonstrations and training for emergency service workers responding to EV‑related accidents and fires involving lithium‑ion or other batteries, as a measure to give effect to, or incidental to the giving of effect to, Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>642</td>
<td>Immigration Advice and Application Assistance Scheme</td>
<td>To provide funding to legal services providers, registered migration agents and providers of interpretation services to provide the following to applicants, or prospective applicants, for Australian visas:<br>(a) assistance before the visa application process, including the following:<br>(i) advice on available visa pathways;<br>(ii) assistance in relation to offers by the Australian Government of a temporary stay in Australia during the visa application process;<br>(iii) the engagement of community representatives or leaders to provide support to prospective applicants, including by disseminating accurate information about visa pathways and the visa application process;<br>(b) assistance in preparing visa applications and participating in the visa application process, including by attending interviews with applicants;<br>(c) assistance in preparing applications for merits review or judicial review of visa application decisions and participating in the merits review or judicial review process, including by attending interviews and tribunal or court proceedings;<br>(d) interpretation services to support the assistance referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c);<br>as a measure with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to immigration or emigration; or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>643</td>
<td>Southeast Asia placements and internships pilot program</td>
<td>To provide funding to further Australia’s strategic relationship with countries in the Southeast Asia region through facilitating and supporting:<br>(a) placements and internships for Southeast Asian graduates and young professionals with Australian businesses; and<br>(b) placements and internships for Australian graduates and young professionals with Southeast Asian businesses.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>644</td>
<td>Support for victims of identity crime and misuse</td>
<td>To provide funding to identity crime and cybercrime support service providers to deliver specialised supports over the internet or telephone or via another telecommunications service to victims of identity crime, where:<br>(a) a Commonwealth credential relating to the person has been compromised; or<br>(b) a Commonwealth agency has referred the person to the support service provider; or<br>(c) the incident for which support is provided involved the compromise of a Commonwealth system; or<br>(d) the identity compromise has resulted in fraud against a Commonwealth agency.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) incidental to the provision of allowances, benefits, endowments or services of the kind described in paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>645</td>
<td>Reducing silicosis and other silica‑related diseases by increasing awareness</td>
<td>To raise awareness of, and provide education, information or advice about, the following:<br>(a) the risks to health caused by exposure to respirable crystalline silica or engineered stone that is in situ;<br>(b) measures that should be taken to prevent workers developing silicosis or any another other silica‑related disease;<br>(c) the effect of laws, including proposed changes to laws, that seek to reduce the incidence of silicosis and other silica‑related diseases in Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>646</td>
<td>Strengthening Families and Communities Partnership</td>
<td>To provide funding for place‑based initiatives that support Indigenous families and communities in Central Australia in the Northern Territory to improve family and community safety, including by:<br>(a) supporting people who are impacted by family and domestic violence; and<br>(b) preventing family and domestic violence; and<br>(c) supporting healthy relationships; and<br>(d) providing social supports to parents and families; and<br>(e) facilitating regional planning and community engagement; and<br>(f) building capacity to identify local needs in communities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>647</td>
<td>Regional Roads Australia Mobile Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for investment in telecommunications infrastructure and services to support improvements in mobile coverage along roads in regional, rural and remote areas, including in communities adjacent to such roads</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>648</td>
<td>Supporting Media Literacy in Culturally and Linguistically Diverse Communities</td>
<td>To improve media literacy in culturally and linguistically diverse communities, with a view to combatting misinformation and disinformation and supporting economic and civic engagement, by funding the Federation of Ethnic Communities’ Councils of Australia to:<br>(a) assist the Commonwealth to develop and implement improved community engagement strategies; and<br>(b) provide a grants program to support community organisations to develop and deliver information and education resources.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>649</td>
<td>Women and Girls in Sport—Play Our Way</td>
<td>To fund activities, including building more suitable facilities and supporting grassroots initiatives, to address discrimination and inequality experienced by women and girls in relation to accessing and participating in sport and physical activity, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 3, 10 and 13;<br>(b) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18 and 31.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>650</td>
<td>Youpla Support Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) payments and other assistance to eligible persons in respect of rights and entitlements under eligible funeral insurance policies issued by a company in the group of companies known as the Youpla Group, including policies affected by the collapse and liquidation of those companies; and<br>(b) related financial counselling for eligible persons.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to bankruptcy or insolvency (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xvii) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>651</td>
<td>Cyber systems in Pacific Island and Southeast Asian countries</td>
<td>To fund:<br>(a) a pilot program to scope and upgrade the cyber systems used by the governments of Pacific Island countries; and<br>(b) bilateral cyber exercises and training to prevent cyber incidents in Southeast Asian countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>652</td>
<td>Australia‑France Bilateral Roadmap</td>
<td>To build and maintain Australia’s relationship with France by providing funding for the following activities:<br>(a) the Australia‑France Centre of Excellence for the Indo‑Pacific, including the following:<br>(i) the Indo‑Pacific Studies Program;<br>(ii) the Energy Transition Program;<br>(iii) the Pacific Social Sciences Program;<br>(b) research relating to Antarctica and the Southern Ocean;<br>(c) a France‑Australia cultural initiative, including the following:<br>(i) establishing partnerships between French and Australian institutions and festivals;<br>(ii) establishing and expanding a network of performing arts professionals;<br>(iii) enhancing awareness of First Nations cultural assets in France;<br>(iv) advancing cooperation on film conservation and restoration.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>653</td>
<td>Forestry Workforce Training Program</td>
<td>To fund measures that support the development of the workforce needed to meet the requirements of Australia’s forest and wood products industries, including training, assessment, skills recognition, career guidance and mentoring, the definition and creation of career pathways, and measures to support Indigenous Australians to enter this workforce and develop relevant skills by responding to their particular needs.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3 and 11;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1 and 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>654</td>
<td>Veterans’ Acute Housing—Specialist Services</td>
<td>To support veterans and their families who experience, or who are at risk of experiencing, homelessness by funding organisations to provide services to assist veterans and their families with:<br>(a) case management and coordination; and<br>(b) accessing financial or other material supports; and<br>(c) accessing crisis or transitional accommodation; and<br>(d) accessing mental health treatment, rehabilitation services (including alcohol and other drug programs), health services and psychosocial supports; and<br>(e) identifying or securing employment; and<br>(f) identifying or retaining long‑term housing options; and<br>(g) accessing other Commonwealth or Commonwealth‑funded services and supports.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>655</td>
<td>New Jobs Program Trial</td>
<td>To provide funding for community organisations and local governments to create and sustain jobs and employment in regions in which the Community Development Program was delivered as at 15 August 2023.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligation under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>656</td>
<td>Supporting an online terrorist crisis response capability</td>
<td>To fund a program to detect and respond to online terrorist content and violent terrorist attacks with significant online elements that will operate, both nationally and internationally, continuously covering 24 hours each day.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>657</td>
<td>Expanded domestic monitoring and referral capability for terrorist and violent extremist content online</td>
<td>To fund a program to identify online terrorist and violent extremist content and to refer that content to industry.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>658</td>
<td>Cyber Awareness—Piloting a Support for Vulnerable Groups Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to:<br>(a) improve cyber security awareness amongst Australians, including people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people with disabilities and First Nations people; and<br>(b) establish a grant program to support advocacy, charity, not‑for‑profit and community groups to develop and deliver tailored cyber security literacy programs to vulnerable community groups;<br>as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>659</td>
<td>Information Sharing and Analysis Centre Acceleration Grant Pilot Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to establish and support an Information Sharing and Analysis Centre in the health sector to allow participating businesses to share information about cyber security threats, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>660</td>
<td>Professionalisation of the Cyber Workforce Grant Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for a voluntary cyber security professionalisation scheme to enable the recognition of qualifications and experience of professionals in the cyber security industry, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>661</td>
<td>Improving parenting confidence and supporting and promoting shared care</td>
<td>To support all parents and other caregivers of children to have the confidence and skills they need to provide nurturing, safe and healthy environments, including by:<br>(a) delivering evidence‑based parenting information to parents and caregivers to support improved outcomes for children in Australia; and<br>(b) building parenting and caregiving skills and knowledge, and improving equitable access to information; and<br>(c) supporting activities to build the confidence of all parents and caregivers to thrive in their parenting or caregiving role; and<br>(d) providing targeted supports and resources to parents and caregivers to thrive in their parenting or caregiving role, including parents facing complex and multiple vulnerabilities; and<br>(e) investing in programs designed to help young parents connect with existing support services to strengthen their parenting skills, achieve their educational goals and participate more fully in the workforce; and<br>(f) supporting early intervention activities to prevent gendered violence and support positive parenting and caregiving.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 6, 18 and 19.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>662</td>
<td>Forced Marriage Specialist Support Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for prevention and early intervention programs and tailored supports to people who are reasonably suspected of being victims, and people who are reasonably considered to be at risk of becoming victims, of forced marriage (within the meaning of section 270.7A of the <i>Criminal Code</i>), including by:<br>(a) the assignment of case workers to provide needs‑based emotional, moral and mental health support and education, and to engage with their family and community; and<br>(b) the provision of counselling services and mediation support to those at risk of, or who have experienced, forced marriage, and their family or those involved in organising the forced marriage; and<br>(c) the coordination of care arrangements with other services (such as temporary accommodation, child protection services and financial support) to assist those at risk of, or who have experienced, forced marriage;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(d) the Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3 and 16;<br>(e) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 32, 34, 35 and 36;<br>(f) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 9 and 23;<br>(g) the Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery, the Slave Trade, and Institutions and Practices Similar to Slavery, particularly Article 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>663</td>
<td>Aged Care Workforce Bonus Payment</td>
<td>To provide funding to assist in the retention of the aged care workforce, both in residential aged care and home care environments, by supporting entities that are not bodies corporate including:<br>(a) residential aged care providers and home care package providers, including state and local government approved residential aged care providers and home care package providers; and<br>(b) multipurpose service providers; and<br>(c) providers delivering aged care services to First Nations persons, including under the National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Flexible Aged Care Program (NATSIFAC); and<br>(d) agencies or brokers employing eligible staff who are contracted to provide services to entities described in paragraph (a), (b) or (c) above;<br>to provide retention bonuses to:<br>(e) residential aged care workers, including clinical and personal care workers, allied health workers, and workers providing food services and cleaning services; and<br>(f) home care workers, including workers providing clinical support, personal care, cleaning services, allied health services, respite services, support with household tasks, support with meal preparation, social support, shopping services, support with community access, transport services or support with transport.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>664</td>
<td>Australian Political Parties for Democracy</td>
<td>To provide grants to Australian political parties for activities directed at assisting in the development of democratic political party systems in other countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>665</td>
<td>Working for Women Program</td>
<td>To support the implementation of Australia’s <i>Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality</i> by funding activities that improve outcomes for women and progress gender equality in Australia, with a focus on the following areas:<br>(a) gender‑based violence against women;<br>(b) supporting women to balance unpaid and paid care;<br>(c) women’s economic equality and security;<br>(d) women’s health;<br>(e) women’s leadership, representation and decision‑making;<br>(f) gender attitudes and stereotypes affecting women;<br>including funding, among other activities, for the following:<br>(g) a women’s advisory mechanism to ensure women’s voices are central to decision‑making and policy outcomes;<br>(h) a research partnership to deliver insights into gender equality;<br>(i) international engagement;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligation under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3 and 11.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>666</td>
<td>Assistance to Papua New Guinea regarding former Regional Resettlement Arrangement caseload</td>
<td>To provide funding to, or for the benefit of, the Government of Papua New Guinea to assist it to:<br>(a) independently deliver services to, or in respect of; and<br>(b) independently provide assistance and support to, or in respect of; and<br>(c) address costs incurred for services, assistance or support already rendered to, or in respect of; and<br>(d) facilitate the transfer to a third country for medical treatment including subsistence support, or permanent settlement assessment of;<br>persons who:<br>(e) both:<br>(i) were transferred to Papua New Guinea prior to 31 December 2021 as unauthorised maritime arrivals, in connection with Papua New Guinea’s designation as a regional processing country; and<br>(ii) remain in Papua New Guinea after 31 December 2021 on a permanent or temporary basis; or<br>(f) are family members of a person referred to in paragraph (e);<br>as a measure with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>667</td>
<td>Specialised Domestic and Family Violence Visa Support Service</td>
<td>To provide support and assistance in relation to visa and immigration matters to visa holders experiencing domestic and family violence, as a measure with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>668</td>
<td>Voter Information Security Enhancement</td>
<td>To uphold the integrity of the Australian political system by providing grants to Australian political parties for measures that maintain and improve the security of data and information held on their systems, networks and premises.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and the States; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 17; or<br>(d) with respect to Commonwealth electoral and referendum processes; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>669</td>
<td>Aged Care Transition to Practice Program</td>
<td>To provide education, training and professional development opportunities to nurses who are new to the aged care sector and to early‑career nurses in the aged care sector.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>670</td>
<td>Aged Care Skills Development Program</td>
<td>To develop and deliver online educational and training materials about matters relevant to aged care including, but not limited to, dementia care, trauma informed care and palliative care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>671</td>
<td>Incorporating Emission Standards into a Digital Accounting Platform Program</td>
<td>To support the incorporation of greenhouse gas emission estimation and reporting standards into a digital accounting platform, for use in emissions calculators accessible to farmers and land managers, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>672</td>
<td>First Nations Water Security</td>
<td>To build local understanding, capability and solutions relating to First Nations water security, including by:<br>(a) developing and updating materials to support understanding of water infrastructure in First Nations communities; and<br>(b) interpretation and communication of resources into local First Nations languages; and<br>(c) developing information dashboards to provide water quality advice to First Nations communities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>673</td>
<td>Voluntary Emissions Reporting Standards for Agriculture and Land Program</td>
<td>To support the development, publication and maintenance of emissions estimation and reporting standards for the agriculture, fisheries and forestry industries, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>674</td>
<td>Capacity building for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Community Controlled Housing Organisations</td>
<td>To improve the capacity of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Community Controlled Housing Organisations to:<br>(a) apply for, manage and use Commonwealth funding; or<br>(b) deliver projects; or<br>(c) manage property;<br>with respect to housing and related services for:<br>(d) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people; or<br>(e) particular groups of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>675</td>
<td>Return and Reintegration Assistance Program</td>
<td>To directly or indirectly fund non‑citizens and their dependents to assist and support them to do either or both of the following:<br>(a) voluntarily depart Australia or a regional processing country;<br>(b) reintegrate in a country of return.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to immigration or emigration; or<br>(c) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>676</td>
<td>Post removal support</td>
<td>To provide funding to support the settlement of non‑citizens in a foreign country, as a measure with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>677</td>
<td>Strategic Fleet Pilot Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to enable the Australian Government to secure maritime capability to call on in times of need, such as natural disasters, crisis or conflict, including by:<br>(a) contributing towards meeting costs relating to vessel operation, flagging and seafarer training; and<br>(b) requisitioning vessels.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and of the States; or<br>(c) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(d) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>678</td>
<td>Measures to Progress First Nations Digital Inclusion</td>
<td>To develop the digital ability and online safety of First Nations Australians in the use of a service by providing funding:<br>(a) to establish services to provide general digital support and to support digital ability and connectivity literacy; and<br>(b) to develop culturally and linguistically appropriate resources and learning materials for the benefit of First Nations Australians; and<br>(c) to engage and maintain digital mentors to:<br>(i) support First Nations Australians with internet connectivity and the use of devices for communication; and<br>(ii) support First Nations Australians to understand and use online services; and<br>(iii) increase awareness amongst First Nations Australians of online risks and mitigation measures;<br>as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>679</td>
<td>Supporting Regional Aviation Programs</td>
<td>To provide funding for works (including repairs and upgrades) or services to improve safety, access and infrastructure at airports and aerodromes in regional and remote areas of Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) for the provision of medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(e) in relation to matters referred to the Parliament of the Commonwealth by the Parliament or Parliaments of any State or States; or<br>(f) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>680</td>
<td>Revive Live Program</td>
<td>To support the performance of Australian music by Australian artists, by providing funding to live music businesses, and to improve access and inclusion for people with disability at live music venues and festivals.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 9 and 30; or<br>(c) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(d) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>681</td>
<td>Falepili Union: Mobility with Dignity Program</td>
<td>To assist Tuvalu to ensure that its immigration, passport, citizenship and border controls are robust and meet international standards for integrity and security and are compatible with and accessible to Australia, including by assisting Tuvalu to:<br>(a) review and strengthen relevant legislation; and<br>(b) enhance identity verification processes; and<br>(c) review and strengthen services, policies, procedures and systems relating to passport and other travel documents utilised for border controls, to align with international standards, including those set by the International Civil Aviation Organization; and<br>(d) become a member of relevant international bodies; and<br>(e) build the capabilities of relevant Tuvaluan public servants.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Australia’s relations with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>682</td>
<td>Marine Resources Initiative</td>
<td>To build the capability of partner countries to manage their maritime domains and marine resources, including through training provision, information sharing and technology transfers relating to matters such as:<br>(a) maritime law enforcement and domain awareness; and<br>(b) geospatial mapping and hydrography; and<br>(c) coral reef monitoring and protection; and<br>(d) environmental governance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>683</td>
<td>Support to Peacebuilding and Peacekeeping</td>
<td>To support peacebuilding and peacekeeping activities outside Australia, including by funding:<br>(a) education, training and capacity building activities for civil or military personnel on peace related activities; and<br>(b) the provision of equipment or services to support foreign countries’ peace operations capabilities; and<br>(c) research and policy development on peace related issues; and<br>(d) the engagement of civil or military personnel in peace operations and institutions; and<br>(e) the improvement of infrastructure used in peace operations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>684</td>
<td>Support for non‑citizens during overseas crisis</td>
<td>To support the non‑citizen family members of Australian citizens and Australian permanent residents, and other non‑citizens, where the non‑citizen family members, or other non‑citizens, are overseas during an overseas crisis, including by providing one or more of the following:<br>(a) assisted departure (including travel to Australia);<br>(b) in‑person assistance;<br>(c) information, crisis updates and liaison services.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>685</td>
<td>Supporting Australian Associated Press</td>
<td>To support the core postal, digital and other like services of the Australian Associated Press, including:<br>(a) a wholesale newswire service to provide public interest news content to news media publications; and<br>(b) fact‑check services that assist digital platforms to address disinformation and misinformation online by assessing the accuracy of content posted by third parties on social media platforms; and<br>(c) a cadetship program to train aspiring journalists.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>686</td>
<td>Agricultural workforce initiatives</td>
<td>To support workforce initiatives that underpin ongoing productivity in the agriculture sector, by funding:<br>(a) the National Farmers Federation to continue to deliver a pilot of the AgCAREERSTART program, which is a structured employment program to help young Australians, up to the age of 25 years, trial and start a career in agriculture in their gap year, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4; or<br>(b) a pilot of the AgConnections program, which is a program that provides grants to universities for a skilled agricultural liaison officer to work with the agricultural industry to facilitate internship and work‑based learning opportunities for students with the aim of increasing the number of highly‑skilled graduates entering the agricultural sector, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Vocational Guidance and Vocational Training in the Development of Human Resources, particularly Articles 1, 2 and 4; or<br>(c) Farmsafe Australia to deliver a national campaign, known as National Farm Safety Week, to highlight the key risks in the agricultural industry and promote farm safety awareness, with the aim of reducing the number of injuries and fatalities in the agricultural sector, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>687</td>
<td>Trade Diversification and Free Trade Agreement Modernisation Program</td>
<td>To enable Australian entities, including industry stakeholders and peak bodies, to conduct activities to identify priorities for the modernisation of Australia’s free trade agreement network and progress mutual recognition agreements with other countries. Activities may include, but are not limited to, the following:<br>(a) trade‑related analysis, stakeholder engagement activities, studies or research related to areas of potential reform for free trade agreements;<br>(b) trade‑related policy development;<br>(c) support for development of potential or revised mutual recognition and similar arrangements.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>688</td>
<td>Investment Deal Teams Project Development Support Program</td>
<td>To facilitate Australian investment in projects located overseas by informing and supporting:<br>(a) proponents of projects located overseas which have the potential for Australian investment; and<br>(b) Australian investors in relation to investment opportunities located overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>689</td>
<td>Cultural Flows Planning for Cultural Economies</td>
<td>To support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in the Murray‑Darling Basin to prepare cultural flows plans, governance structures or water‑dependent business plans in relation to water in the Murray‑Darling Basin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>690</td>
<td>Modernised Multicultural Grants Program</td>
<td>To support multicultural Australia and multicultural communities by funding the following:<br>(a) grassroots multicultural organisations, to engage in capacity building activities, including festivals, celebrations, small amenity upgrades and community programs;<br>(b) peak bodies, to engage in activities directed to strengthening Australia’s multicultural capacity through:<br>(i) promoting inclusive and respectful communities; and<br>(ii) promoting the value of immigration, multiculturalism and Australian citizenship; and<br>(iii) strengthening understanding of Australian values and civic responsibilities;<br>(c) infrastructure projects for multicultural communities, for the purposes of:<br>(i) strengthening inclusion and cohesion at the local level; and<br>(ii) boosting civic participation; and<br>(iii) enabling new and established multicultural communities to connect with the wider Australian community;<br>(d) non‑religious training courses for faith leaders and persons holding pastoral roles in faith organisations, for the purposes of:<br>(i) increasing their capability to support their congregations’ understanding of Australia’s pluralistic and democratic society, and the opportunities and obligations of civic participation; and<br>(ii) otherwise equipping them to provide guidance and advice on issues of inclusion, civic participation, community resilience, and legal and civic rights and responsibilities;<br>(e) the multicultural media sector, to ensure sustainable and independent multicultural media;<br>(f) the Faith Communities Council of Victoria Inc., to develop resources to teach children about different faith communities, nurture mutual understanding, and build recognition of and respect for different faith traditions;<br>(g) entities that maintain, or agree to create and maintain, places of cultural significance, to fund upgrades of culturally significant museums and galleries and to build a centralised sports and education hub.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 7; or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>691</td>
<td>Protecting migrant workers—information and education package</td>
<td>To safeguard temporary migrant workers from workplace exploitation and enhance the integrity of Australia’s visa system by:<br>(a) designing information and educational materials on migrant worker rights, protections and obligations and migration compliance measures; and<br>(b) disseminating these information and educational materials to temporary migrant workers and their employers; and<br>(c) supporting non‑government organisations to provide services and other supports to temporary migrant workers and their employers in relation to migrant worker rights, protections and obligations and migration compliance measures.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>692</td>
<td>Enhancing First Nations Justice Policy Outcomes</td>
