<td>To enhance justice policy outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people by supporting the Justice Policy Partnership, implementing the priorities agreed from time to time by the Parties to that Partnership, and evaluating the effectiveness of that Partnership.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>693</td>
<td>Leaving Violence Program</td>
<td>To provide financial and other support to victims of intimate partner violence to:<br>(a) help victims to leave violent relationships; and<br>(b) help victims who have left violent relationships to stabilise their lives;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 9 and 17.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to bankruptcy or insolvency (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xvii) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>694</td>
<td>Industrial Uplift—Workforce Initiatives</td>
<td>To support and increase the capacity of Australia’s naval shipbuilding and sustainment industrial workforce with a focus on delivering conventionally armed nuclear‑powered submarines, including through the development and funding of career information and resources, vocational education and training programs, placements and incentives.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>695</td>
<td>Nuclear‑Powered Submarines Program Technical Scholarships Initiative</td>
<td>To increase the attraction and awareness of opportunities in the nuclear‑powered submarine enterprise by providing scholarships to domestic undergraduate students undertaking study in the fields of science, technology, engineering and mathematics.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>696</td>
<td>4WD buses for remote sports—Northern Territory</td>
<td>To acquire buses to assist with access to remote sports in the Northern Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>697</td>
<td>Volunteer Grants Program</td>
<td>To support community organisations, that rely on volunteers, to do any of the following:<br>(a) pay for one or more of the following:<br>(i) hardware and software to facilitate online, telephone or radio communications;<br>(ii) internet and telephone services;<br>(iii) insurance premiums;<br>(b) reduce or remove barriers to volunteering for the following cohorts:<br>(i) children;<br>(ii) people who support the development or wellbeing of children;<br>(iii) First Nations people;<br>(iv) new migrants to Australia;<br>(v) people with disability;<br>(vi) unemployed people;<br>(vii) veterans;<br>(viii) defence force members;<br>(ix) women experiencing, or at risk of experiencing, gender‑based violence or isolation;<br>(c) deliver volunteer‑run activities directed at supporting the following outcomes:<br>(i) the development and wellbeing of children;<br>(ii) the elimination of racial discrimination and the promotion of understanding, tolerance and friendship amongst racial or ethnic groups;<br>(d) deliver volunteer‑run activities directed at supporting the following cohorts:<br>(i) the cohorts covered by subparagraphs (b)(iii) to (viii);<br>(ii) women experiencing, or at risk of experiencing, gender‑based violence, discrimination, disadvantage or isolation.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to support veterans and defence force members; or<br>(c) with respect to insurance, other than State insurance (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xiv) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(e) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(f) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(g) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 11, 13 and 14;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 19, 26 and 28;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 6;<br>(iv) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 7;<br>(v) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>698</td>
<td>Supporting youth in Central Australia</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities, infrastructure and services in Central Australia in the Northern Territory that promote the safety and wellbeing of children and young people, their families and communities or otherwise support their positive development, including activities, infrastructure and services that:<br>(a) promote physical, mental, social and emotional wellbeing, good nutrition, food security and health and safety; or<br>(b) reduce the incidence of antisocial behaviour; or<br>(c) address the impact of violence and substance abuse; or<br>(d) promote social inclusion and engagement, including through creating or improving sporting, recreational and community opportunities, facilities or infrastructure; or<br>(e) develop and provide access to information and data to inform the design, promotion and evaluation of youth programs and community services; or<br>(f) provide better access to developmental and educational opportunities; or<br>(g) assist with the transition to work, vocational or higher education.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>699</td>
<td>Supporting Indigenous leaders and organisations in Central Australia</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities, projects, research and services in Central Australia in the Northern Territory that assist Indigenous leaders and Indigenous organisations to develop or improve leadership capabilities and related skills, including through developing or enhancing organisational governance and corporate functions.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>700</td>
<td>Remote Jobs and Economic Development Program—job creation</td>
<td>To provide funding to eligible employers to subsidise the wages and employee entitlements of eligible persons whom they employ, to support the creation of jobs in remote Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(ii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention Concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>701</td>
<td>Native Title Anthropologist Grant Program</td>
<td>To support the native title system by providing funding for activities that:<br>(a) enhance capacity for anthropological work in the native title system; or<br>(b) encourage stronger linkages between academic anthropologists and practising native title anthropologists; or<br>(c) provide professional development and support for currently practising or prospective native title anthropologists.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>702</td>
<td>Case Management and Mediation Services—Elder Abuse Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to organisations to provide services to address elder abuse, including through the provision of:<br>(a) legal information, advice and assistance; or<br>(b) administrative services; or<br>(c) psychological counselling services; or<br>(d) financial support services; or<br>(e) non‑legal advocacy and mediation between family members;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under:<br>(f) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 17 and 26; or<br>(g) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8 and 16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>703</td>
<td>Supporting victims and survivors of child sexual abuse and supporting children displaying harmful sexual behaviours</td>
<td>To provide social, therapeutic, legal and other support services to:<br>(a) victims and survivors of child sexual abuse; and<br>(b) children displaying harmful sexual behaviours or at risk of doing so;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention of the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 2, 4, 19, 34 and 39.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>704</td>
<td>High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza H5N1 Preparedness Capability Program</td>
<td>To support measures in preparation for any incursions of high pathogenicity avian influenza H5N1 in Australia, so as to limit its impacts on Australian wildlife and ecosystems and give effect to Australia’s obligations under international agreements including:<br>(a) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6, 8 and 9; and<br>(b) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Article 3.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>705</td>
<td>Quad Clean Energy Supply Chain Diversification Program</td>
<td>To develop and diversify clean energy supply chains in the Indo‑Pacific region by funding eligible projects, as a measure:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4;<br>(ii) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(iii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 and 10.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>706</td>
<td>Labelling Scheme for Smart Devices</td>
<td>To improve the security of communications made over the internet through consumer‑grade smart devices by funding:<br>(a) a voluntary labelling scheme in relation to the internet security features of those devices; and<br>(b) the development and delivery of training in relation to the voluntary labelling scheme to entities within the supply chain for those devices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>707</td>
<td>Mental Health Support for Emergency Services Workers Grant Program</td>
<td>To fund the delivery of best practice mental health services directed towards the prevention, treatment and control of recognised mental health conditions, targeting current and former (whether paid or voluntary) emergency services workers involved in disaster response, and their families, including by:<br>(a) providing clinical mental health treatment (including via telehealth); and<br>(b) providing support for referrals to appropriate services; and<br>(c) providing support to raise awareness of recognised mental health conditions; and<br>(d) providing prevention and well‑being services designed to prevent recognised mental health conditions;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>708</td>
<td>Community Broadcasting Program</td>
<td>To support the sustainability of certain broadcasting services (within the meaning of the <i>Broadcasting Services Act 1992</i>) by supporting:<br>(a) the Community Broadcasting Foundation; and<br>(b) broadcasters which operate on a not‑for‑profit basis and for community or educational purposes, the peak bodies for community broadcasting and related bodies (such as registered training organisations).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>709</td>
<td>Support for the Republic of Nauru</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance and other forms of support to, or for the benefit of, Nauru, including, but not limited to, support in connection with the Nauru–Australia Treaty signed on 9 December 2024, as a measure with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxix) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>710</td>
<td>Disaster Health Care Assistance Scheme</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance for out‑of‑pocket health care expenses to support access to necessary medical services by eligible persons who were affected by the following events:<br>(a) the bombing in Bali on 12 October 2002;<br>(b) the Indian Ocean tsunami on 26 December 2004;<br>(c) the bombing in London on 7 July 2005;<br>(d) the bombing in Bali on 1 October 2005;<br>(e) the bombing in Dahab, Egypt on 24 April 2006;<br>as a measure for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>711</td>
<td>General Practice Incentive Fund Thin Markets</td>
<td>To improve the provision of, and access to, primary health and care support services in areas where there is limited or unstable access to health, medical, care and support service systems, including by:<br>(a) providing and commissioning medical and health services; and<br>(b) supporting the development and design of new or alternative delivery and funding models for health and related service systems; and<br>(c) facilitating the coordination and integration of health care services offered for selected patient cohorts and communities; and<br>(d) facilitating the appropriate supply of medical and health professionals to address health workforce shortages.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8, 25 and 26.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>712</td>
<td>Intravenous Fluids Program</td>
<td>To increase production and supply, and to promote best practice use, of intravenous fluids in Australia by funding the following:<br>(a) the expansion of intravenous fluids production facilities in Australia;<br>(b) the conduct of a review into the use of intravenous fluids;<br>(c) the development of clinical guidelines relating to the best practice use of intravenous fluids;<br>(d) activities to support the uptake and use of those clinical guidelines;<br>(e) the establishment of a panel of suppliers of intravenous fluids;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>713</td>
<td>National Dementia Support Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities that support people living with dementia and that support their carers and communities to better care for them, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(b) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 19 and 26.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>714</td>
<td>Family Violence Prevention and Legal Services in the Jervis Bay Territory</td>
<td>To provide legal and other services in the Jervis Bay Territory to support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, their families and their kinship groups who are at risk of, are experiencing or are affected by family, domestic or sexual violence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>715</td>
<td>National Paediatric Telecare Service</td>
<td>To improve the developmental health of children in rural and remote communities by providing the following services over the internet or telephone:<br>(a) allied health therapy for children with developmental vulnerability;<br>(b) training and education for parents and educators to improve their ability to support children’s developmental health needs and engage with support services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>716</td>
<td>First Nations Clean Energy Grants and Toolkit</td>
<td>To support Indigenous Australians’ participation and engagement with clean energy project development, including by funding:<br>(a) the development of guidance materials and toolkits for Indigenous communities; and<br>(b) programs and activities to develop Indigenous Australian‑led clean energy projects; and<br>(c) community‑based service delivery; and<br>(d) access to, and procurement of, technical and cultural expertise;<br>as a measure with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to providing funding for activities that are engaged in to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(a) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(b) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(c) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>717</td>
<td>Junior Rangers</td>
<td>To support the educational engagement of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander young people, including through on‑Country learning opportunities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>718</td>
<td>Remote Australia Employment Service</td>
<td>To establish and deliver a remote employment service, including by funding:<br>(a) services to support participants in remote Australia to develop the skills and ability to access employment, overcome barriers to employment, meet income support mutual obligations and access and retain employment; and<br>(b) related service provider costs;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, unemployment benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>719</td>
<td>African‑Australian Communities Program</td>
<td>To support the participation and integration of African‑Australian communities in Australian society, enhance social cohesion and promote a sense of belonging, including by funding the following:<br>(a) measures that support the participation of African‑Australian youth in Australian society;<br>(b) measures that support the re‑engagement of African‑Australian youth in Australian society following experiences in the criminal justice system;<br>(c) measures with respect to mental health;<br>(d) employment services and employment opportunities that are tailored to the needs of African‑Australians;<br>(e) measures with respect to families, including the provision of parenting support and support for survivors of domestic violence;<br>(f) measures that strengthen African‑Australians’ understanding of Australian values and civic responsibilities, including by enabling and developing the capacity of grassroots African‑Australian community organisations to engage with government;<br>(g) measures that facilitate access to Commonwealth services.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) incidental to the provision of invalid or old‑age pensions (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiii) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) incidental to the provision of maternity allowances, widows’ pensions, child endowment, unemployment, pharmaceutical, sickness or hospital benefits, medical or dental services, benefits to students or family allowances (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 1, 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18, 19 and 29;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2, 6 and 12;<br>(iv) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2; or<br>(f) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>720</td>
<td>Security Uplifts for Muslim Communities Program</td>
<td>To fund the Australian National Imams Council Limited to provide security upgrades to mosques, Islamic centres, Islamic schools and other community facilities used and attended by the Muslim community in Australia, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 18 and 27.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>721</td>
<td>Australian Submarine Industrial Uplift Program</td>
<td>To build the capacity and capability of the Australian submarine industrial base, and increase Australian industry participation in global nuclear‑powered submarine supply chains, including by supporting Australian vendors to obtain necessary qualifications.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and of the States.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>722</td>
<td>Australian Cultural Diplomacy Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to support cultural and artistic activities that strengthen international partnerships and enhance perceptions of Australia overseas, including the following activities:<br>(a) building international cultural understanding, collaboration and connections;<br>(b) building international people‑to‑people partnerships;<br>(c) building institutional partnerships;<br>(d) telling Australian stories and amplifying First Nations voices overseas;<br>(e) promoting a peaceful, stable and prosperous Indo‑Pacific region.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(d) with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>723</td>
<td>Pacific Onshore Health Access</td>
<td>To cover costs of a limited number of persons from the Pacific accessing medical care in Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(c) with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>724</td>
<td>Support for Solomon Islands</td>
<td>To provide financial assistance to, or for the benefit of, Solomon Islands, including for initiatives relating to regional issues in the Pacific and support for the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>725</td>
<td>Australia‑India Trade and Investment Accelerator Fund</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities directed to increasing trade and investment between Australia and India, including the following activities:<br>(a) supporting the marketing and promotion of Australian goods and services in the Indian market;<br>(b) collecting and distributing information on one or more of the following:<br>(i) trading and investment opportunities for Australian businesses in India;<br>(ii) the Indian market and consumers in that market;<br>(iii) Indian requirements relating to trade or investment;<br>(c) connecting Australian businesses to expertise on either or both of the following:<br>(i) the Indian market and consumers in that market;<br>(ii) Indian requirements relating to trade or investment;<br>(d) minimising risk for Australian businesses wanting to invest in India or trade with Indian businesses;<br>(e) facilitating relationships between Australian and Indian governments, businesses and research institutions;<br>(f) building and expanding pathways for Australian businesses to import knowledge and skills from India;<br>(g) promoting opportunities for Indian businesses to invest in Australia.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to immigration or emigration; or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth; or<br>(d) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(e) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>726</td>
<td>Administration of the National Joint Replacement Registry</td>
<td>To support administration of the data management component of the National Joint Replacement Registry.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>727</td>
<td>Long‑Acting Reversible Contraception Centres of Excellence Program</td>
<td>To improve access to long‑acting reversible contraception by establishing centres of excellence to provide health services and training for health professionals in relation to such contraception, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>728</td>
<td>Endometriosis and Pelvic Pain Clinic Program</td>
<td>To improve health outcomes for individuals experiencing endometriosis, pelvic pain, perimenopause or menopause by funding existing health clinics, expanding the range of services provided at existing health clinics and providing and commissioning additional health clinics to support such individuals.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>729</td>
<td>Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Program</td>
<td>To improve health and social outcomes for individuals, families and communities affected by Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (<b><i>FASD</b></i>) by:<br>(a) providing services which diagnose FASD and assess the impairment caused by FASD; and<br>(b) training and educating health professionals and other health service providers in relation to the FASD diagnostic process; and<br>(c) supporting Australians affected by FASD and their families and carers; and<br>(d) raising awareness of, providing education and advice on and developing and disseminating information about FASD (including the prevention, treatment, management, control and health effects of FASD); and<br>(e) undertaking research in relation to FASD;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(f) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 8 and 25;<br>(g) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18 and 21;<br>(h) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>730</td>
<td>Support for the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime</td>
<td>To fund the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime to support the operation of the Joint Global Programme on Access to Controlled Substances for Medical and Scientific Purposes, While Preventing Diversion and Non‑medical Use, as a measure with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia or matters affecting Australia’s relations with foreign countries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>731</td>
<td>Supporting Living Organ Donors Program</td>
<td>To provide direct and indirect financial assistance to organ donors (including potential donors), including by:<br>(a) providing payments to the donor’s employer where paid leave has been taken by the donor; and<br>(b) providing payments to self‑employed donors for lost income; and<br>(c) reimbursing out‑of‑pocket travel and accommodation expenses for donors, their families and carers;<br>as a measure for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>732</td>
<td>Primary Health Networks Commissioning of Multidisciplinary Teams</td>
<td>To increase access to health services and improve community health outcomes by funding Primary Health Networks to:<br>(a) commission multidisciplinary teams of health professionals, including allied health professionals, nurses, nurse practitioners, midwives and Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander health workers and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health practitioners, to arrange health services for selected patient cohorts; and<br>(b) deliver practice support to allied health, nursing, midwifery and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health practices to improve the quality of health services and the capabilities of health professionals;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>733</td>
<td>Administration and Delivery of Services for the National Diabetes Services Scheme</td>
<td>To assist in the administration and delivery of services for the National Diabetes Services Scheme, including by:<br>(a) ensuring access to products required by people with diabetes; and<br>(b) facilitating support, training and outreach for health professionals working with people with diabetes; and<br>(c) providing advice in relation to diabetes and the operation of the National Diabetes Services Scheme; and<br>(d) providing other supports to people with diabetes, including educational activities and general information on diabetes management.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, sickness benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to, or incidental to the giving of effect to, Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>734</td>
<td>Rural and Remote Pharmacy Workforce Program</td>
<td>To support, improve and expand the pharmacy workforce in rural and remote areas by funding the following:<br>(a) financial support for pharmacists in rural and remote areas to access continuing professional development, including assistance with travel and accommodation costs;<br>(b) incentives for pharmacy owners or eligible hospital authorities to offer intern year placements for pharmacy graduates in rural and remote pharmacies;<br>(c) financial support to enable community pharmacies in rural and remote areas to retain newly registered pharmacists beyond their initial intern period;<br>(d) training allowances for pharmacy interns in rural and remote areas;<br>(e) direct access to emergency locum pharmacist services for pharmacies in rural and remote areas;<br>(f) financial support to students from rural and remote communities undertaking undergraduate or postgraduate studies in pharmacy;<br>(g) provision of rural pharmacist mentors to Indigenous students, or students from rural and remote locations, in order to encourage the pursuit of studies in pharmacy, and to provide guidance and support during each year of their studies;<br>(h) financial support to Australian universities to facilitate pharmacy student placements in rural and remote communities, including assistance with travel and accommodation costs;<br>(i) administrative support for pharmacy schools to administer rural and remote placement programs;<br>(j) support for pharmacists and pharmacy students practising and working in rural and remote areas, including programs to support clinical placements and promote intra‑professional collaboration;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services, pharmaceutical benefits or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>735</td>
<td>Medication Management Reviews and Quality Use of Medicines Program</td>
<td>To support the quality use of medicines and the minimisation of adverse medicine events by:<br>(a) assisting people to understand and manage their medicines through medication reviews conducted by credentialed pharmacists:<br>(i) in the home, including through initiatives to provide access to medication reviews in rural and remote areas; and<br>(ii) in residential aged care facilities; and<br>(b) supporting services and activities of pharmacists that facilitate the quality use of medicines in residential aged care facilities; and<br>(c) supporting the quality use of medicines in relation to services provided by Indigenous Health Services and associated service providers.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Internation Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services or pharmaceutical benefits (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>736</td>
<td>Indigenous Pharmacy Workforce Program</td>
<td>To encourage and assist participation in the pharmacy workforce by Indigenous Australians by providing:<br>(a) scholarships to Indigenous students for undergraduate or graduate entry studies in pharmacy; and<br>(b) funding to eligible pharmacies that employ and support Indigenous pharmacy assistants to enable the pharmacy assistants to complete pharmacy assistant training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>737</td>
<td>Local Environmental Projects Program</td>
<td>To support measures intended to benefit, protect or ensure the sustainability of ecosystems, natural habitats or biological resources, and measures intended to benefit or protect National Heritage places (within the meaning of the <i>Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999</i>), Commonwealth Heritage places (within the meaning of that Act) or Australian properties on the World Heritage List kept under Article 11 of the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, including measures relating to the following:<br>(a) the restoration of biodiversity;<br>(b) habitat remediation;<br>(c) weed management;<br>(d) the conservation, protection and presentation of those places or properties, including to ensure they are preserved for the benefit of future generations;<br>(e) revegetation;<br>(f) the removal of debris from riverbanks and creeks;<br>(g) wildlife care facilities.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(a) the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, particularly Articles 4, 5 and 6;<br>(b) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6, 8 and 9.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>738</td>
<td>Rural Financial Counselling Service Program</td>
<td>To provide financial counselling services to eligible farmers, fishers, foresters and small related businesses experiencing, or at risk of, financial hardship.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to bankruptcy or insolvency (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xvii) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(ii) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 7;<br>(iii) the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, particularly in Africa, particularly Articles 4 and 5;<br>(iv) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>739</td>
<td>Norfolk Island Employment Support Program</td>
<td>To provide employment services and related supports that meet the identified needs of Norfolk Island residents, including by:<br>(a) providing services to assist individuals to find, change and retain employment; and<br>(b) providing financial assistance to enable individuals to undertake vocational education and training courses; and<br>(c) supporting new residents to find employment and settle into the Norfolk Island community; and<br>(d) assisting employers to recruit employees; and<br>(e) assisting employers to retain employees; and<br>(f) providing wage subsidies to employers that employ individuals referred by the program provider; and<br>(g) working with stakeholders in the community to identify issues affecting economic and social participation on Norfolk Island, with the aim of ensuring the services and supports provided by the program are tailored to the needs of residents.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>740</td>
<td>Investing in LGBTIQA+ Community Connection</td>
<td>To support the provision by LGBTIQA+ media organisations of broadcasting services and digital and online content.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>741</td>
<td>Journalism Assistance Fund</td>
<td>To support Australian news publishers and safeguard media diversity in Australia by providing funding for the production or distribution of online or digital public interest news content, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>742</td>
<td>Maritime Skills and Training Initiative</td>
<td>To increase the number of seafarers certified in accordance with the International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under Articles I and VI of that Convention, including by funding the employers of seafarers to assist trainees to complete required periods of seagoing service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>743</td>
<td>Community Laundries in Remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities</td>
<td>To support the establishment or upgrade, and operation and maintenance, of community laundries in remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>744</td>
<td>Social and Emotional Wellbeing Flexible Funding Pool</td>
<td>To provide for a flexible funding pool to fund short‑term, place‑based social and emotional wellbeing and healing supports to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander families and communities affected by major trauma events.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>745</td>
<td>Social and Emotional Wellbeing Scholarships</td>
<td>To provide support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander undergraduate or postgraduate psychology students, including by providing:<br>(a) scholarships to provide financial support for study, living and transport costs; and<br>(b) funding to coordinating organisations to administer the scholarships and provide study support and pastoral care to scholarship recipients.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>746</td>
<td>Healing for Strong Families Program</td>
<td>To deliver healing programs for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people who are impacted by family violence or at risk of engagement with child protection systems.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>747</td>
<td>ASEAN‑Australia Centre Grants Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to the ASEAN‑Australia Centre for grants to eligible recipients to develop, promote and strengthen understanding and engagement between Australia and Southeast Asia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>748</td>
<td>Centre for Australia‑India Relations Maitri Program</td>
<td>To build and maintain Australia’s relationship with India, by funding the Centre for Australia‑India Relations to provide grants to eligible recipients for:<br>(a) projects that benefit that relationship, including artistic, cultural, sporting, scientific, academic, business and media projects; and<br>(b) postgraduate scholarships for Indian students to study higher education degrees at Australian universities; and<br>(c) fellowships for Australian and Indian researchers to work on Australia‑India geostrategic or geoeconomic policy issues.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) for the provision of benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(d) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>749</td>
<td>PacificAus Sports Grants Program</td>
<td>To strengthen relationships between Australia and the Pacific through sport by fostering elite sports pathways for Pacific athletes and sporting teams, and fostering engagement between Australian and Pacific sporting teams, athletes and stakeholders, including by funding activities that support:<br>(a) Pacific teams and athletes’ participation in multi‑sport events, including Olympic, Paralympic and Commonwealth Games; and<br>(b) Pacific teams and athletes’ participation in high level Australian and international sporting competitions; and<br>(c) the presence of Australian sporting codes in the Pacific; and<br>(d) the development of pathways for emerging Pacific athletes and officials to receive high performance coaching, training and competition.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) with respect to Australia’s relations with foreign countries; or<br>(c) with respect to the relations of the Commonwealth with the islands of the Pacific.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>750</td>
<td>Humanitarian Integration and Settlement Program</td>
<td>To fund onshore and offshore services and activities with respect to humanitarian entrants who are aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution), to assist them to settle in Australia, including through the provision of:<br>(a) pre‑arrival assessment and services; and<br>(b) on‑arrival services; and<br>(c) accommodation assistance, including the provision of basic household goods; and<br>(d) assistance with essential registrations; and<br>(e) intensive settlement services; and<br>(f) orientation to living in Australia and local services; and<br>(g) employment, education, health and English language support.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to immigrants; or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>751</td>
<td>Strengthening Community Safety</td>
<td>To support community crime prevention projects undertaken by local government bodies, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 9.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>752</td>
<td>Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drug Research</td>
<td>To support research relating to alcohol, tobacco and other drug use in Australia, including the following:<br>(a) data collection, analysis and evaluation activities on the emerging areas of local concern and the effectiveness of new technologies and methods for the full spectrum of care, from prevention to treatment;<br>(b) the development of evidence‑based policy and advice in consultation with relevant stakeholders, including in relation to harm reduction, demand reduction and supply reduction;<br>(c) the translation of research into accessible alternative formats for ease of understanding by a diverse audience;<br>(d) the development, promotion and dissemination of evidence‑based information and education;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(e) the Convention on Psychotropic Substances, particularly Article 20;<br>(f) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(g) the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, 1961, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, particularly Articles 4 and 38;<br>(h) the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, particularly Articles 5 and 20.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>753</td>
<td>General Practice Training</td>
<td>To fund measures that support the training of general practitioners, in order to sustain and increase the general practice workforce across Australia, by:<br>(a) supporting the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners Limited, the Australian College of Rural and Remote Medicine Ltd and the Remote Vocational Training Scheme Ltd to create and maintain vocational training places across all metropolitan, regional, rural and remote locations, to enable medical practitioners to specialise as general practitioners, including by providing general practice registrars with:<br>(i) support to achieve fellowship through a high quality education and training program accredited by the Australian Medical Council Limited; and<br>(ii) accredited training placements using a robust distribution methodology, accredited supervision, medical education, cultural education and mentorship, training and assessment services, advice, research and resources; and<br>(b) administering the National Consistent Payments Framework to deliver payments to:<br>(i) general practice registrars, including through the provision of parental leave incentives, study leave incentives and salary incentives; and<br>(ii) general practice supervisors; and<br>(iii) general practices, including through salary support; and<br>(c) enabling the Indigenous General Practice Trainee Network (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Corporation) to provide culturally appropriate and tailored support services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander general practice registrars; and<br>(d) supporting professional development activities for cultural educators and mentors; and<br>(e) supporting General Practice Registrars Australia Limited and GPTA Ltd to:<br>(i) provide general practice registrars and supervisors with professional support and peer networks; and<br>(ii) advocate for the interests of general practice registrars and supervisors; and<br>(iii) promote general practice to medical students and junior doctors, including by supporting the General Practice Students Network; and<br>(iv) deliver the National Terms and Conditions for the Employment of Registrars; and<br>(f) supporting research, data collection and consultation related to key issues in general practice training and supervision, to build an evidence base for policy and advocacy on general practice issues.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, benefits to students or medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>754</td>
<td>Peer Workforce Association</td>
<td>To fund the establishment and operation of a peer workforce association to represent and support peer workers across mental health and suicide prevention, alcohol and other drugs and psychosocial disability support service systems, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>755</td>
<td>Precision Medicine and Rare Cancers Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for:<br>(a) initiatives that facilitate patients with cancer and their clinicians accessing clinical trials, precision medicine or personalised treatments; and<br>(b) an online platform that facilitates patients with rare cancers and their clinicians accessing expert clinical advice, management guidelines, genetic testing, research opportunities or clinical trials.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution; or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>756</td>
<td>Strategic Agreement on Pharmacist Professional Practice</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Pharmaceutical Society of Australia Limited to implement the Strategic Agreement on Pharmacist Professional Practice, including by developing, implementing, reviewing and maintaining:<br>(a) the Professional Practice Standards; and<br>(b) the Code of Ethics for Pharmacists; and<br>(c) the National Competency Standards Framework for Pharmacists in Australia; and<br>(d) the Clinical Governance Principles for Pharmacy Services; and<br>(e) practice guidelines for pharmacy services; and<br>(f) pharmacy credentialing and accreditation systems;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>757</td>
<td>Translation and Interpretation Services for Primary Health Networks</td>
<td>To provide funding for translation and interpretation services to support culturally and linguistically diverse people access mental health services delivered by Primary Health Networks, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>758</td>
<td>Primary Health Care—Infrastructure Grants</td>
<td>To provide funding for the following health infrastructure projects:<br>(a) capital works for Burnie Health Hub;<br>(b) construction of Flinders Health Clinic, Smithton Health Hub and West Brisbane Health and Housing Clinic;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>759</td>
<td>Australian Bushland Program</td>
<td>To conserve Australia’s biodiversity by:<br>(a) increasing the amount of land which is protected and conserved in States and Territories; and<br>(b) supporting States and Territories, private environmental organisations and other persons or bodies to acquire and protect properties with particular importance for biodiversity and ecosystem functions and services;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Articles 6, 8 and 10.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>760</td>
<td>Supporting the resolution of income apportionment</td>
<td>To provide funding to organisations to support and inform the government’s resolution of the past practice of income apportionment in the administration of the law governing social security entitlements and other entitlements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>761</td>
<td>Building Early Education Fund Integrated Services Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for the construction or expansion of facilities to support the delivery of early childhood education and care integrated with either or both of the following:<br>(a) child and maternal health services or services supporting the development and wellbeing of children (including playgroups), including children with a disability;<br>(b) services for the benefit of Indigenous children and their families.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 19;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 2, 4, 18, 23, 24, 27, 28 and 29;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>762</td>
<td>NAIDOC Local Grants</td>
<td>To provide funding for National Aborigines and Islanders Day Observance Committee (NAIDOC) Week events and activities as a measure with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>763</td>
<td>Online Safety Education: Digital and Media Literacy for Younger Australians</td>
<td>To provide funding to non‑government organisations for online safety education activities that develop the digital and media literacy of younger Australians, by helping them to critically analyse and engage with online content, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4 and 19.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>764</td>
<td>Blood‑Borne Viruses and Sexually Transmissible Infections Research Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for research activities that support reducing the incidence and prevalence rates of blood‑borne viruses and sexually transmissible infections, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(c) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>765</td>
<td>First Nations Maternal and Child Health Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for the development and implementation of a new model of care that provides:<br>(a) continuous maternal and perinatal care for women who are pregnant with an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander child; and<br>(b) health care for Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander infants that can extend to children aged 2 years old;<br>as a measure with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>766</td>
<td>Growing the Psychiatry Workforce—Certificate of Postgraduate Training in Clinical Psychiatry Scholarships</td>
<td>To provide benefits to students by funding scholarships for medical professionals to undertake postgraduate training in clinical psychiatry.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>767</td>
<td>Medicare Urgent Care Clinics Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for the establishment and operation of Medicare Urgent Care Clinics to improve health care outcomes in the community, including by:<br>(a) providing accessible, urgent medical services for non‑life‑threatening conditions; and<br>(b) reducing pressure on the public hospital system by diverting non‑life‑threatening cases away from hospital emergency departments.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>768</td>
<td>Palliative Care Capability in Aged Care</td>
<td>To provide advice to general practitioners and aged care providers that provide the following types of services (<b><i>palliative care services</b></i>):<br>(a) palliative care;<br>(b) end of life care;<br>(c) advance care planning;<br>to recipients of aged care services to:<br>(d) enhance the quality and support of palliative care services for recipients of aged care services; and<br>(e) improve linkages and coordination between palliative care services and aged care services.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>769</td>
<td>Peer Workforce Training Placements</td>
<td>To provide benefits to students by funding peer worker training placements for individuals with personal experience of mental health challenges, to assist these individuals in meeting the minimum work requirements for a professional qualification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>770</td>
<td>Psychiatry Workforce Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for training posts in psychiatry and associated supervisory support, as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>771</td>
<td>Tackling Bullying and Harmful Behaviour in Schools</td>
<td>To address bullying, cyberbullying and other harmful behaviours to ensure that Australian schools are safe, respectful and inclusive learning environments, including by:<br>(a) developing targeted resources to help parents, caregivers, school leaders, teachers and students understand, prevent and address bullying, cyberbullying and other harmful behaviours; and<br>(b) developing and delivering a national anti‑bullying awareness campaign.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18 and 29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>772</td>
<td>Bondi Terrorist Attack Response and Recovery</td>
<td>To support the short to medium‑term recovery needs of individuals and communities (in particular, the Jewish community) affected by the antisemitic terrorist attack at Bondi Beach on 14 December 2025.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>773</td>
<td>Family Violence and Cross‑Examination of Parties Scheme</td>
<td>To provide funding to legal aid commissions in connection with the provision of legal representation to persons subject to the ban on direct cross‑examination in section 102NA of the <i>Family Law Act 1975</i> and similar provisions in State or Territory laws.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in relation to marriage; or<br>(b) in connection with divorce and matrimonial causes, including in relation to parental rights or the custody and guardianship of infants; or<br>(c) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 15 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3 and 4;<br>(iii) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 9 and 17; or<br>(d) in relation to matters referred to the Parliament of the Commonwealth by the Parliament or Parliaments of any State or States; or<br>(e) in connection with, or incidental to, the investing of any court of a State with federal jurisdiction.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>774</td>
<td>Anti‑bullying Additional Measures</td>
<td>To support students, teachers, parents and communities to respond to bullying in schools by developing and delivering:<br>(a) communication activities that address student wellbeing and promote the recommendations from the Anti‑Bullying Rapid Review to wider school communities; and<br>(b) educational resources and activities to students, teachers, school leaders and parents that support whole‑of‑school community understanding of behavioural expectations and offer practical strategies to promote pro‑social behaviour at home;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18 and 29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>775</td>
<td>Game on—Teaming Up for Climate Action Program</td>
<td>To improve engagement with Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets by:<br>(a) funding community sports clubs to make energy performance and climate resilience improvements (the <b><i>upgrades measure</b></i>); and<br>(b) funding other entities to promote and facilitate engagement with:<br>(i) the upgrades measure; and<br>(ii) the transition to net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(c) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(d) the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 4;<br>(e) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>776</td>
<td>Advancing Australian Antarctic Scientific Research</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Australian Centre for Excellence in Antarctic Science to enable its researchers to undertake data analysis and publish outcomes of Antarctic research, including from the Denman Terrestrial Campaign and Denman Marine Voyage, as a measure that is peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to places, persons, matters or things external to Australia; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>777</td>
<td>Assistance for Ukraine’s self‑defence</td>
<td>To directly or indirectly provide military or financial assistance to Ukraine in connection with the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List for Ukraine’s self‑defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>778</td>
<td>Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Professional Organisations</td>
<td>To provide funding to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health professional organisations to support the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health workforce, including by:<br>(a) improving skills, capacity, recruitment and retention of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health professionals; and<br>(b) increasing the number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students studying for health qualifications and improving the graduation and employment rates of those students; and<br>(c) delivering mentoring, support, professional networking and development opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health students and health professionals; and<br>(d) promoting culturally safe and responsive environments for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health students, health professionals and health consumers; and<br>(e) improving the quality of health workforce planning and policies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>779</td>
<td>Perinatal Mental Health Centres</td>
<td>To support the mental health of new and expectant parents by funding the establishment and operation of perinatal mental health centres that:<br>(a) provide specialist assessment, diagnosis and treatment for people experiencing, or at risk of, perinatal mental illness; and<br>(b) provide multidisciplinary team‑based mental health care for new and expectant parents, including by clinical psychologists, registered psychologists and social workers; and<br>(c) contribute to the development of a specialist perinatal mental health workforce;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>780</td>
<td>Rural Health Multidisciplinary Training Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to university organisational units, such as:<br>(a) university departments of rural health; or<br>(b) rural clinical schools; or<br>(c) regional training hubs;<br>in critical health fields, including medicine, nursing, midwifery, dentistry and allied health, to support students to study and train in regional, rural and remote areas and remain in those areas once qualified.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services or benefits to students (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>781</td>
<td>Youth specialist care centres</td>
<td>To provide funding to:<br>(a) establish and operate a network of youth specialist care centres that provide comprehensive treatment and care for young people with complex mental health needs and support for their families and caregivers; and<br>(b) support the governance of those centres; and<br>(c) collect data about those centres; and<br>(d) support the continuous improvement of those centres by evaluating them.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>782</td>
<td>News Media Assistance Program—News Innovation Fund</td>
<td>To support the digital news media sector by providing funding for innovative projects aimed at increasing capacity, building sustainability and realising efficiencies in the sector, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>783</td>
<td>Upper Murrumbidgee Drought Operating Framework</td>
<td>To provide funding to Snowy Hydro Limited to compensate the company for electricity generation revenue the company has foregone due to holding water intended for release, or releasing water, from Tantangara Dam into the Upper Murrumbidgee River for either or both of the following purposes:<br>(a) promoting environmental outcomes;<br>(b) protecting and restoring environmental assets;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(c) the Convention on Biological Diversity, particularly Article 8;<br>(d) the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat, particularly Articles 3 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>784</td>
<td>East Melbourne Synagogue Program</td>
<td>To deliver at the East Melbourne Synagogue:<br>(a) a social cohesion and community engagement initiative to strengthen Jewish communal life and wider social harmony; and<br>(b) a capital works renewal initiative to construct a community centre for a cohesive and strong multicultural precinct;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2, 5 and 7.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and that cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>785</td>
<td>Grants in Aid Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to non‑government organisations that undertake work in:<br>(a) science, humanities or public policy; or<br>(b) animal welfare; or<br>(c) the promotion of acts of bravery or heroism across Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(b) undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>786</td>
<td>Antisemitism and discrimination teacher training</td>
<td>To develop and deliver training, educational programs and curriculum resources for school leaders and teachers to address discrimination (including antisemitism) in Australian schools, in order to promote tolerance in response to antisemitism and combat religious discrimination more generally, including materials primarily directed towards:<br>(a) addressing and combatting antisemitism; and<br>(b) assisting teachers to deliver lessons on antisemitism; and<br>(c) equipping teachers to identify, prevent and confront antisemitism in Australian schools;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under either or both of the following:<br>(d) the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, particularly Articles 2 and 7;<br>(e) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 27.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>787</td>
<td>Birthing on Country Services</td>
<td>To fund Birthing on Country services that provide maternal care services throughout the perinatal period to First Nations women and women who are pregnant with a First Nations child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>788</td>
<td>Chronic Conditions Grant Program</td>
<td>To support investment in chronic health conditions (whether generally or on a condition‑specific basis), including by contributing to the funding of initiatives that have one or more of the following aims:<br>(a) raising awareness of, providing education and advice in relation to, and developing and disseminating information about, health conditions (including their prevention, treatment, management and control), including for the benefit of health professionals and other health providers;<br>(b) prevention, early detection and intervention;<br>(c) improving continuity of care, including by providing system‑integrated, multi‑disciplinary and person‑centred support services;<br>(d) prevention, early detection and intervention;<br>(e) managing multimorbidity;<br>(f) achieving equitable health outcomes across members of the general population;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>789</td>
<td>LGBTIQA+ Safe Spaces Grant Program</td>
<td>To fund a provider, or a consortium led by a provider, to promote the provision of respectful and culturally safe primary health care services to LGBTIQA+ people by:<br>(a) developing and delivering training to health service providers, including administrative and support staff; and<br>(b) developing and implementing accreditation processes to recognise health service providers that meet evidence‑based standards; and<br>(c) undertaking monitoring and compliance activities in relation to accredited health service providers; and<br>(d) subsidising the costs of training and accreditation for health service providers; and<br>(e) monitoring and evaluating the implementation of the program, including by an independent evaluation; and<br>(f) consulting with relevant stakeholders in relation to the activities covered by paragraphs (a) to (e);<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>790</td>
<td>National Institute for Youth Mental Health</td>
<td>To provide funding to establish and operate a National Institute for Youth Mental Health to:<br>(a) provide evidence‑based advice to the Commonwealth government in relation to youth mental health; and<br>(b) provide training, information and capacity building to people who work in the field of youth mental health to improve the quality of youth mental health services; and<br>(c) conduct research in relation to youth mental health; and<br>(d) collect and analyse data and other evidence about youth mental health;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.<br>This purpose also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures undertaken in the exercise of the executive power of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>791</td>
<td>Rural Locum Program</td>
<td>To support:<br>(a) health professionals practising in rural, regional and remote Australia to take leave and undertake continuing professional development activities; and<br>(b) the delivery of locum services by health professionals in rural, regional and remote Australia, including in rural, regional and remote areas in the Northern Territory, including through the continuing professional development of metropolitan‑based health professionals.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(c) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>792</td>
<td>Mental Health Measures–Eating Disorders</td>
