<td>To provide funding to support the operation of the Eating Disorder Credential, which includes:<br>(a) formal recognition of health professionals who have the qualifications, knowledge and training, and who engage in the professional development activities, needed to meet minimum standards for the delivery of safe and effective eating disorder care; and<br>(b) ensuring people with an eating disorder can easily identify credentialed health professionals; and<br>(c) the provision of professional development training and supervision to health professionals to support them to become credentialed or retain their credential.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of, or incidental to the provision of, medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>793</td>
<td>Strengthening First Nations Health–Renal Care and Services for First Nations Peoples</td>
<td>To deliver culturally safe dialysis closer to home in remote and very remote communities, as a measure with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians.<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>794</td>
<td>Support for the Health Workforce to Integrate Digital Mental Health Tools</td>
<td>To fund a provider, or a consortium led by a provider, to engage general practitioners and other health professionals in the use of digital mental health supports, including by:<br>(a) developing and distributing training material, webinars and other resources; and<br>(b) collecting data and developing reports on digital mental health service access and usage; and<br>(c) increasing visibility and awareness of e‑Mental Health in Practice and of the training, resources and conferences offered by e‑Mental Health in Practice; and<br>(d) e‑Mental Health in Practice reporting key insights, learnings and advice to the Australian Government; and<br>(e) delivering promotional activities on the use of digital mental health options and Medicare Mental Health, including engagement with Primary Health Networks; and<br>(f) undertaking engagement, co‑design, collaboration, research and design activities;<br>as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>795</td>
<td>Grants to Australian Organisations Program</td>
<td>To provide funding for activities that relate to, or assist with, the pursuit of an equitable and accessible system of federal justice, including in relation to law reform, legal research, legal education and law enforcement.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(c) incidental to the execution of any power vested by the Constitution in the Federal Judicature.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>796</td>
<td>Foundation Skills Campaign</td>
<td>To deliver a communications campaign over the internet (including social media), and through television and radio, for the following purposes:<br>(a) to promote lifelong learning for adults;<br>(b) in respect of foundation skills that underpin workforce participation, productivity and social inclusion, such as language, literacy, numeracy and digital literacy skills—to do the following:<br>(i) address and reduce any stigma associated with having low level foundation skills;<br>(ii) encourage people with low level foundation skills to undertake training to develop those skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>797</td>
<td>Prescribed Bodies Corporate Strategic Projects</td>
<td>To support the following entities:<br>(a) prescribed bodies corporate within the meaning of the <i>Native Title (Prescribed Bodies Corporate) Regulations 1999</i>;<br>(b) traditional owner group entities within the meaning of the <i>Traditional Owner Settlement Act 2010</i> (Vic.);<br>(c) corporations established for the purpose of representing traditional owners under native title settlement agreements;<br>to realise strategic and economic opportunities and other benefits arising from or in connection with native title determinations or native title settlement agreements, including by:<br>(d) building their capacity to maximise the social, cultural and economic aspirations of their respective native title‑holding groups; and<br>(e) assisting them to acquire equipment and services to support business functions and business opportunities; and<br>(f) building their long‑term organisational and operational capacity; and<br>(g) supporting them to work with government and industry partners and make native title agreements effectively; and<br>(h) building their capacity to meet corporate compliance obligations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>798</td>
<td>Indigenous Broadcasting and Media Program</td>
<td>To support the First Nations broadcasting and media sector by funding First Nations community broadcasters, sector peak bodies and sector strengthening projects.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>799</td>
<td>Pacific Parliamentary Partnerships</td>
<td>To provide funding for projects to strengthen parliamentary capacity in the Commonwealth Pacific Parliaments of Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Niue, Vanuatu, Tonga, Nauru, Tuvalu, Fiji, Samoa, Cook Islands and Bougainville by:<br>(a) enabling democratic benchmark assessments to identify individual reform priorities and technical support needs and delivering programs targeted to those priorities and needs; and<br>(b) providing access to multilateral professional development seminars and other forums to develop skills and knowledge in parliamentarians and parliamentary officials and ensuring Pacific perspectives are represented in those seminars and other forums;<br>as a measure with respect to external affairs (within the meaning of s 51(xxix) of the Constitution).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>800</td>
<td>National Security Hotline Upgrades</td>
<td>To fund information and communications technology upgrades to support the ongoing operation of the National Security Hotline, as a measure with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution).<br>This objective also has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures for the purposes of the defence of the Commonwealth and of the States.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>801</td>
<td>Thriving Suburbs Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to Territory and local governments, or to entities collaborating with local governments, to plan and construct or upgrade community infrastructure to enhance amenity, liveability and social cohesion in urban, suburban and peri‑urban areas of Australia.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(b) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>802</td>
<td>Urban Precincts and Partnerships Program</td>
<td>To provide funding to State, Territory and local governments, universities and not‑for‑profit organisations to support the planning and delivery of precincts in urban areas, including for the benefit of Indigenous Australians.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) in connection with trade and commerce with other countries, or among the States and Territories; or<br>(b) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to Indigenous Australians and particular groups of Indigenous Australians; or<br>(d) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 10;<br>(ii) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 6;<br>(iii) the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Employment Policy, particularly Articles 1 and 2;<br>(iv) the Paris Agreement, particularly Articles 4 and 7;<br>(v) the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, particularly Article 4; or<br>(e) that are peculiarly adapted to the government of a nation and cannot otherwise be carried on for the benefit of the nation; or<br>(f) involving the granting of financial assistance to a State or Territory; or<br>(g) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>803</td>
<td>Carer‑Inclusive Workplace Initiative</td>
<td>To support carers by funding the following measures to assist organisations to develop and adopt practices that encourage and support employees with caring responsibilities:<br>(a) an online self‑assessment tool allowing organisations to assess their level of carer‑inclusivity, and either identify areas for improvement or self‑identify as a carer‑friendly workplace;<br>(b) a website containing information and resources for organisations and carers, including learning modules.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Labour Organization’s Convention concerning Equal Opportunities and Equal Treatment for Men and Women Workers: Workers with Family Responsibilities, particularly Articles 1, 3, 4 and 7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>804</td>
<td>Drs4Drs Program</td>
<td>To fund the delivery of mental health telehealth consultation services for doctors and medical students.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>805</td>
<td>Strengthening Medicare—Targeted Interventions to Ensure 9 in 10 General Practice Non‑Referred Attendances are Bulk Billed by 2030</td>
<td>To provide funding to the Primary Health Network in the Central Coast, Newcastle, Lake Macquarie and Hunter region to:<br>(a) commission the establishment and maintenance of up to 6 fully bulk billing general practice clinics; and<br>(b) increase bulk billing rates in regions with historically low bulk billing rates; and<br>(c) evaluate the impact and cost‑effectiveness of those clinics in those regions to support extending the program to other regions.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) for the provision of medical services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxiiiA) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>806</td>
<td>Thriving Kids</td>
<td>To provide early intervention and improve outcomes for children (<b><i>targeted children</b></i>) with developmental delay or neurodevelopmental differences, including autism, and to provide supports for their families, kin, carers, teachers and other professionals, by:<br>(a) providing information, advice and assistance to find resources or services, to support the development of targeted children; and<br>(b) providing national telephone services and online platforms and resources to provide access to the information, advice and assistance referred to in paragraph (a); and<br>(c) providing an online peer support program for targeted children; and<br>(d) providing an evidence‑based tool to guide the conduct of, and response to, annual health assessments by general practitioners of targeted children, or children suspected to be targeted children; and<br>(e) providing a digital application for children’s health and neurodevelopmental information; and<br>(f) funding the Murdoch Children’s Research Institute to establish and maintain a national coordination office to:<br>(i) oversee the national delivery of training and resources to teachers and other school staff to support the mental health of children; and<br>(ii) implement tailored approaches to the delivery of training and resources to regional, rural and remote schools; and<br>(g) providing workforce capability building initiatives, training, resources, supports or micro‑credentials in relation to the following:<br>(i) embedding evidence‑informed best practices appropriate for children’s developmental needs;<br>(ii) identifying and supporting targeted children, or children suspected to be targeted children, including implementing reasonable adjustments;<br>(iii) referrals to services and supports;<br>(iv) providing culturally safe and responsive services for the benefit of First Nations targeted children and their families, kin and carers; and<br>(h) undertaking activities to retain or expand the capacity of the First Nations workforce, including activities to enhance the operational capacity of Aboriginal Community‑Controlled Organisations; and<br>(i) developing resources to support primary health care professionals identify and respond to children with neurodevelopmental differences, including autism.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18, 23, 24 and 27;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4, 7 and 24.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>807</td>
<td>Inclusion Support Program</td>
<td>To support either or both of the following:<br>(a) all children having the opportunity to participate in a quality approved early learning program;<br>(b) parents or carers of children with additional needs having access to appropriate and affordable child care services that allow them to participate in the workforce, including parents or carers of:<br>(i) children with disability; and<br>(ii) children who are undergoing disability assessment; and<br>(iii) Indigenous children; and<br>(iv) children from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds; and<br>(v) children from a background that involves refugee status or humanitarian intervention;<br>as a measure to give effect to Australia’s obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 4, 18 and 23.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>808</td>
<td>Store Efficiency and Resilience Package</td>
<td>To provide funding for stores in remote or very remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities to improve storage capacity and store infrastructure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>809</td>
<td>Children and Family Support</td>
<td>To deliver flexible and evidence‑informed prevention and early intervention services that provide:<br>(a) parents and caregivers the support they need to guide children’s social and emotional growth; and<br>(b) children and young people the social and emotional support they need to reach their full potential;<br>including by providing any of the following:<br>(c) online supports and online information services to build parenting capacity and strengthen child and family wellbeing;<br>(d) parenting programs (including home visiting programs), counselling and skill‑building programs and programs supporting the social and emotional development of children, such as playgroups;<br>(e) intensive family supports for families and children with multiple or complex needs.<br>This objective has the effect it would have if it were limited to measures:<br>(a) with respect to postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services (within the meaning of paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution); or<br>(b) with respect to aliens (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xix) of the Constitution); or<br>(c) with respect to marriage; or<br>(d) with respect to divorce and matrimonial causes; and in relation thereto, parental rights, and the custody and guardianship of infants; or<br>(e) to give effect to Australia’s obligations under one or more of the following:<br>(i) the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, particularly Articles 2, 3, 5 and 16;<br>(ii) the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, particularly Articles 4 and 23;<br>(iii) the Convention on the Rights of the Child, particularly Articles 3, 4, 6, 18, 19, 23, 24 and 28;<br>(iv) the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, particularly Articles 2, 7, 9 and 17;<br>(v) the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, particularly Articles 2 and 12; or<br>(f) undertaken in, or in relation to, a Territory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>810</td>
<td>Online gambling public awareness and education campaign</td>
<td>To develop and deliver a public awareness and education campaign to help reduce harm from online gambling by communicating the risks and harms posed by online gambling and encouraging help‑seeking.</td>
</tr>
</table>

## Endnotes

### Endnote 1—About the endnotes

The endnotes provide information about this compilation and the compiled law.

The following endnotes are included in every compilation:

Endnote 1—About the endnotes

Endnote 2—Abbreviation key

Endnote 3—Legislation history

Endnote 4—Amendment history

**Abbreviation key—Endnote 2**

The abbreviation key sets out abbreviations that may be used in the endnotes.

**Legislation history and amendment history—Endnotes 3 and 4**

Amending laws are annotated in the legislation history and amendment history.

The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.

The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.

**Editorial changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* authorises First Parliamentary Counsel to make editorial and presentational changes to a compiled law in preparing a compilation of the law for registration. The changes must not change the effect of the law. Editorial changes take effect from the compilation registration date.

If the compilation includes editorial changes, the endnotes include a brief outline of the changes in general terms. Full details of any changes can be obtained from the Office of Parliamentary Counsel.

**Misdescribed amendments**

A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the *Legislation Act 2003*.

If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.

### Endnote 5—Editorial changes

In preparing this compilation for registration, the following kinds of editorial change(s) were made under the *Legislation Act 2003*.

**Part 3 of Schedule 1AA (subheading before table item 324.001)**

**Kind of editorial change**

Removal of redundant text

**Details of editorial change**

Schedule 1 paragraph 1(c) of the *Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Amendment (2026 Measures No. 1) Regulations 2026* instructs to repeal item 324.001 from the table in Part 3 of Schedule 1AA.

This amendment results in a table subheading containing no table items.

This compilation was editorially changed to remove the redundant table subheading.
